title: Fix ProfileEditor ISF validation: mg/dL range hardcoded blocks mmol/L users from saving profiles
description: ProfileEditor Zod schema enforces ISF in 10–200 mg/dL/U range with mg/dL error messages for all users, making it impossible for mmol/L users (valid range ~0.5–11.1 mmol/L/U) to save a profile. This is a P0 clinical safety issue: mmol/L patients (e.g. mike) cannot create or edit insulin profiles.
design:
# OpenSpec: Fix ProfileEditor ISF validation to support mmol/L unit (kdiab-spa)

## Goal
ProfileEditor.tsx uses a hardcoded Zod schema (isfSegmentSchema) that enforces ISF values between 10.0 and 200.0 mg/dL/U. mmol/L users (e.g. mike, whose ISF is 0.5-11.1 mmol/L/U) cannot save profiles because the schema rejects their values. glucoseUnit is in App.tsx state but is never passed to ProfileEditor.

## Context
- kdiab-ui/src/features/profiles/ProfileEditor.tsx lines 49-52: isfSegmentSchema hardcoded min 10.0 max 200.0 with mg/dL error messages.
- ProfileEditorProps (lines 114-120): no glucoseUnit field.
- kdiab-ui/src/App.tsx line 39: const [glucoseUnit, setGlucoseUnit] = useState('mg/dL').
- App.tsx lines 258-264: <ProfileEditor userId=... initialProfile=... onProfileSaved=... readOnly=... isDoctor=...> - glucoseUnit not passed.
- profileSchema (lines 62-110) references isfSegmentSchema at module level; both must become dynamic.

## Interface Changes
No API changes - frontend validation only.

## Implementation Plan
1. kdiab-ui/src/features/profiles/ProfileEditor.tsx
   - Remove module-level isfSegmentSchema and profileSchema definitions.
   - Add glucoseUnit?: string to ProfileEditorProps.
   - Inside ProfileEditor function, derive both schemas using useMemo:
     const isfSegmentSchema = useMemo(() =>
       z.object({
         startTime: z.string().regex(/^([0-1]?[0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$/, 'Invalid time (HH:MM)'),
         value: (glucoseUnit ?? 'mg/dL') === 'mmol/L'
           ? z.number().min(0.5, 'ISF must be >= 0.5 mmol/L/U').max(11.1, 'ISF must be <= 11.1 mmol/L/U')
           : z.number().min(10.0, 'ISF must be >= 10.0 mg/dL/U').max(200.0, 'ISF must be <= 200.0 mg/dL/U'),
       }),
       [glucoseUnit]
     )
   - Move the full profileSchema (with its .refine for total daily basal) inside the component using useMemo([isfSegmentSchema]).
   - Update useForm to use the memoized resolver: resolver: zodResolver(profileSchema).
   - Re-declare type ProfileFormValues = z.infer<typeof profileSchema> inside the component.
2. kdiab-ui/src/App.tsx
   - Pass glucoseUnit={glucoseUnit} to the <ProfileEditor> at lines 258-264.

## Test Plan
- [ ] npm run build in kdiab-ui/ - TypeScript compiles clean
- [ ] npm run lint - no lint errors
- [ ] Manual: mike (mmol/L) adds ISF 2.5 -> save succeeds
- [ ] Manual: sarah (mg/dL) adds ISF 150 -> save succeeds
- [ ] Manual: mike adds ISF 12.0 -> error shown
- [ ] Manual: sarah adds ISF 201 -> error shown

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] mmol/L users can save ISF values in range 0.5-11.1 mmol/L/U
- [ ] mg/dL users retain 10-200 mg/dL/U constraint
- [ ] Error messages include correct unit label
- [ ] TypeScript compiles clean; lint passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- ISF conversion: 10 mg/dL/U / 18 = 0.56, 200 / 18 = 11.1 - safe to round to 0.5 and 11.1.
- useForm zodResolver is recreated when profileSchema changes (memoized).
- type ProfileFormValues must remain consistent; move type alias inside component.
close_reason: ProfileEditor ISF schema is now unit-aware (useMemo based on glucoseUnit, a37274f); glucoseUnit prop passed from App.tsx (00ed913)

title: Fix AnalyticsService: pass from/to date range to measuresClient in getAgp and getHba1c
description: AnalyticsService.getAgp() and getHba1c() call measuresClient.getMeasures() without from/to parameters, fetching ALL user measures (up to 50K records) and filtering in-memory. Now that kdiab-wrt added from/to support to the measures endpoint, AnalyticsService should pass the caller's date range to measuresClient so only the relevant window of CGM data is fetched. Without this fix, every analytics request is a full table scan regardless of the selected time range.
design:
# OpenSpec: Pass from/to to getMeasures in AnalyticsService (kdiab-2zu)

## Goal
AnalyticsService.getAgp() and fetchCgmReadings() (used by getHba1c()) call measuresClient.getMeasures() without from/to parameters, causing a full upstream fetch of all measures. MeasuresClient.getMeasures() already accepts from: String? and to: String? (implemented by kdiab-wrt). Simply pass them through to eliminate the full table scan and redundant client-side date filter.

## Context
- kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../application/service/AnalyticsService.kt:
  - Line 69 (in getAgp()): measuresClient.getMeasures(userId, authorization, correlationId) - no from/to.
  - Line 115 (in fetchCgmReadings()): same.
  - Lines 74-76 (in getAgp()): if (t < fromInstant || t > toInstant) return@forEach - redundant post-fetch filter.
  - Lines 116-120 (in fetchCgmReadings()): .filter { t >= fromInstant && t <= toInstant } - redundant.
- MeasuresClient.getMeasures() signature: (userId, authorization, correlationId, from: String? = null, to: String? = null). Client appends ?from=...&to=... when non-null.
- TimelineService already passes from/to correctly (line 27).

## Interface Changes
No interface changes - internal call-site fix only.

## Implementation Plan
1. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../application/service/AnalyticsService.kt
   - In getAgp() line 69: change to measuresClient.getMeasures(userId, authorization, correlationId, from, to).
   - Remove the 'if (t < fromInstant || t > toInstant) return@forEach' guard in getAgp() (lines 74-76). Keep Instant.parse and UTC hour extraction.
   - In fetchCgmReadings() line 115: change to measuresClient.getMeasures(userId, authorization, correlationId, from, to).
   - Remove the .filter { t >= fromInstant && t <= toInstant } block (lines 116-120). Remove fromInstant/toInstant variables from fetchCgmReadings (no longer needed there).

## Test Plan
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check --no-daemon from kdiab-analyze/ - all existing tests pass, Detekt clean, Kover >= 80%
- [ ] Manual: open HbA1c for sarah with 7-day window - check backend logs show ?from=...&to=... in upstream URL

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Both getMeasures() calls pass from and to to MeasuresClient
- [ ] Redundant client-side date filters removed
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- kdiab-measures endpoint already handles from/to (kdiab-wrt). No measures service change needed.
- fromInstant/toInstant are still needed in getAgp() for UTC hour grouping - do NOT remove those Instant.parse calls from getAgp, only the range-filter guard (lines 74-76).
close_reason: from/to now passed to getMeasures in getAgp and fetchCgmReadings; redundant client-side filters removed (commit 2570248)

title: Consolidate all four frontends into a single kdiab-ui application
description:
The platform currently has four separate React frontends (kdiab-measures/frontend, kdiab-profiles/frontend, kdiab-treatments/frontend, kdiab-analyze/frontend). Each has its own Vite build, its own Keycloak client, its own nginx container, and its own OIDC login flow. This creates UX fragmentation (separate logins per service pre-SSO fix), maintenance overhead (four identical build pipelines, four sets of dependencies, duplicated i18n/theme/auth boilerplate), and blocks features like cross-service navigation.

Goal: create a single `kdiab-ui/` module at the monorepo root that combines all four feature areas into one React SPA. Each backend service is unchanged — only the frontend layer is consolidated.

## What moves into kdiab-ui

All feature code from the four existing frontends:

| Source | Feature directory | Destination |
|---|---|---|
| kdiab-measures/frontend | src/features/measures/ | kdiab-ui/src/features/measures/ |
| kdiab-profiles/frontend | src/features/profiles/ | kdiab-ui/src/features/profiles/ |
| kdiab-treatments/frontend | src/features/treatments/ | kdiab-ui/src/features/treatments/ |
| kdiab-analyze/frontend | src/features/timeline/ | kdiab-ui/src/features/timeline/ |
| kdiab-analyze/frontend | src/features/analytics/ | kdiab-ui/src/features/analytics/ |
| kdiab-analyze/frontend | src/features/timeframe/ | kdiab-ui/src/features/timeframe/ |

Shared infrastructure (pick once, deduplicate):
- Single `src/api/` with generated clients for all four OpenAPI specs (measures, profiles, treatments, analyze)
- Single `src/auth/` (react-oidc-context, one Keycloak client: `kdiab-ui`)
- Single `src/i18n/` (merge all locale files from all four frontends)
- Single `src/styles/` (CSS custom properties, one dark theme)
- Single `App.tsx` with top-level navigation (tab bar or sidebar: Measures | Profiles | Treatments | Analytics)

## New Keycloak client

Add a `kdiab-ui` client to `config/keycloak-realm.json` with:
- All four audience mappers (measure, profile, treatment, analyze) — same as kdiab-analyze-frontend today
- All existing protocol mappers (roles, allowed_patients, glucose_unit, weight_unit)
- PKCE S256

The four existing Keycloak clients (kdiab-measures-frontend, kdiab-profiles-frontend, kdiab-treatments-frontend, kdiab-analyze-frontend) can be kept for backwards compatibility or removed.

## Vite / build setup

- Single `package.json`, single `vite.config.ts`
- API generation script runs all four `openapi-generator-cli generate` commands (one per service spec)
- Single `Dockerfile` producing one nginx container (port 3000), replacing the four individual frontend Dockerfiles
- `VITE_BASE_PATH=/` — no sub-path prefix needed since there is only one frontend
- Single nginx.conf: serve static assets at `/`; proxy each service's API at its path prefix (`/api/measures/`, `/api/profiles/`, `/api/treatments/`, `/api/analyze/`)

## API routing in kdiab-ui nginx

Each backend API remains at its own port. The unified nginx proxies by prefix:

```nginx
location /api/measures/  { proxy_pass http://measures-backend:8080/api/; }
location /api/profiles/  { proxy_pass http://profiles-backend:8082/api/; }
location /api/treatments/ { proxy_pass http://treatments-backend:8083/api/; }
location /api/analyze/   { proxy_pass http://analyze-backend:8084/api/; }
location /               { root /usr/share/nginx/html; try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html; }
```

The generated API clients set their basePath to `/api/measures/`, `/api/profiles/`, etc.

## docker-compose.yml changes

- Remove: measures-frontend, profiles-frontend, treatments-frontend, analyze-frontend containers
- Add: kdiab-ui container (builds from kdiab-ui/, serves on port 3000)
- Gateway simplifies to just kdiab-ui (or can be removed entirely if kdiab-ui IS the gateway)

## What to delete after migration

- kdiab-measures/frontend/
- kdiab-profiles/frontend/
- kdiab-treatments/frontend/
- kdiab-analyze/frontend/
- The four per-service frontend nginx.conf files
- The four frontend Dockerfiles

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cd kdiab-ui && npm run build` succeeds with no TypeScript errors
- [ ] `docker compose up --build` starts the platform with a single frontend container at localhost:3000
- [ ] All four feature areas (Measures, Profiles, Treatments, Analytics) are reachable from the unified navigation
- [ ] Logging in once grants access to all features — no per-service login screen
- [ ] Role-based UI elements (doctor vs patient vs admin views) work correctly
- [ ] mmol/L and mg/dL unit preferences apply across all glucose-displaying features
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass with zero errors
close_reason: Implemented in kdiab-ui SPA (commit ad79378)

Root cause: same as kdiab-ko5 (backend AnalyticsService) — seed data was normalised from Nightscout field names (sgv, mbg) to the canonical kdiab schema (value/unit/trend) but the frontend chart was not updated. title: fix: BFF analytics reads sgv field but measures data uses value
description: The BFF AnalyticsService reads the Nightscout-convention 'sgv' field from CGM measure data (AnalyticsService.kt lines 68 and 111: data["sgv"]?.toString()?.toDoubleOrNull()), but the seed data was updated to store CGM values under the canonical 'value' key. This causes all CGM lookups to return null, making HbA1c, TIR, and AGP compute with zero readings. Test files also build test data with 'sgv' and must be updated.
design:
# OpenSpec: fix BFF analytics sgv→value field name (kdiab-ko5)

## Goal
Fix the BFF AnalyticsService so that HbA1c, TIR, and AGP compute correctly. The root cause is that AnalyticsService reads data["sgv"] (Nightscout convention) but all measure data now uses data["value"] (kdiab canonical schema). Two callsites in production code and three test helper methods use the wrong field name.

## Context

### Root cause
When seed data was normalised from Nightscout conventions (sgv/mbg fields) to the canonical kdiab schema (value/unit/trend), only the frontend MeasureList.tsx was updated. The BFF AnalyticsService still reads the Nightscout field name, causing every CGM lookup to return null and all analytics to silently compute with zero readings.

### Files that need changing

**Production code:**
- kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/application/service/AnalyticsService.kt
  - Line 68  (getAgp):           data["sgv"]  → data["value"]
  - Line 111 (fetchCgmReadings): data["sgv"]  → data["value"]

**Test helpers:**
- kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../service/AnalyticsServiceTest.kt
  - Line 30: put("sgv", sgv)   → put("value", sgv); add put("unit", "mg/dL")
- kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../service/TimelineServiceTest.kt
  - Line 29: put("sgv", 120.0) → put("value", 120.0); add put("unit", "mg/dL")
- kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../http/MeasuresClientTest.kt
  - Line 31: put("sgv", sgv)   → put("value", sgv); add put("unit", "mg/dL")

## Interface Changes
No interface changes — the fix is internal to AnalyticsService and test helpers.

## Implementation Plan
1. AnalyticsService.kt line 68:  data["sgv"] → data["value"]
2. AnalyticsService.kt line 111: data["sgv"] → data["value"]
3. AnalyticsServiceTest.kt line 30: put("sgv", sgv) → put("value", sgv) and add put("unit", "mg/dL")
4. TimelineServiceTest.kt line 29: put("sgv", 120.0) → put("value", 120.0) and add put("unit", "mg/dL")
5. MeasuresClientTest.kt line 31: put("sgv", sgv) → put("value", sgv) and add put("unit", "mg/dL")
6. Run ./gradlew :backend:check in kdiab-bff — all existing analytics tests must pass

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit: existing AnalyticsServiceTest cases now receive non-null cgm values and produce non-zero HbA1c/TIR/AGP results
- [ ] Quality gate: cd kdiab-bff && ./gradlew :backend:check passes (Detekt green, Kover ≥ 80%)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] HbA1c endpoint returns a non-null hba1c value when CGM readings exist in the timeframe
- [ ] TIR breakdown returns non-zero inRangeCount/belowCount/aboveCount when CGM readings exist
- [ ] AGP hourly buckets contain non-zero count values for hours with CGM readings
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check passes with no regressions

## Risks & Assumptions
- The fix is a pure rename — no logic changes, no risk of regressions beyond what tests cover.
- The mmol/L conversion (glucoseUnit JWT claim × 18) may also be wrong now that ALL values are stored in mg/dL regardless of user preference. This is a separate P1 issue and is out of scope for this fix.
close_reason: Fixed: data["sgv"] → data["value"] in AnalyticsService.kt (lines 68, 111) and updated 3 test helpers. Quality gate green.

title: Fix BGM field name mismatch: AddMeasureModal saves value but MeasureList reads mbg
description: AddMeasureModal.tsx saves a BGM reading as {value: 120, unit: 'mg/dL'} but MeasureList.tsx renderDataSummary() reads d.mbg (Nightscout field name). When the field is missing it falls back to JSON.stringify(d), showing raw JSON instead of the formatted glucose value. This means every user-created BGM reading displays incorrectly. Fix: align field name in the modal to use 'mbg' per Nightscout convention, or make the list reader check both 'mbg' and 'value' as fallback.
close_reason: Implemented per approved plan. Tests green, builds clean.

title: Fix silent API failure in AddMeasureModal and AddTreatmentModal
description: When a treatment or measure API call fails (network error, 5xx, 401), the modal closes or stays open with no feedback. The user believes the entry was saved. This is a safety risk: a logged bolus that silently failed means the patient's record is missing a critical event and the doctor cannot see it. Fix: show inline error message in the modal with the failure reason and a retry button. On 401, show 'Session expired - please log in again'.
close_reason: Implemented per approved plan. Tests green, builds clean.

title: Fix docs/how-to-run.adoc — remove references to deleted build.sh and old per-service frontend paths
description: how-to-run.adoc describes build.sh (which does not exist) with flags --check, --docker, --no-parallel as an active alternative to Gradle. It also tells developers to 'cd kdiab-<service>/frontend' which was eliminated by ADR-006. Docker image table lists obsolete per-service frontend images (measures-frontend etc). All orchestration has moved to root Gradle build and kdiab-ui.

title: Add ProfileValidationTest case for max daily basal (150 U/day) clinical safety limit
description: The validateBasalRequirements branch that throws when total daily basal exceeds 150 U/day — a hard clinical safety ceiling — has no test case exercising it. Also missing: tests for overlapping basal segment start times and the 'ICR/ISF must start at 00:00' validation rule.

title: Add DoseCalculationService tests for segment lookup, midnight rollover, and high-dose warning
description: lookupIsfSegment/lookupIcrSegment/lookupTargetSegment fallback logic (midnight rollover, multiple time segments), the useProfileTime parameter, the BG-below-target-with-carbs warning, and the total > 20U high-dose warning are untested. Additionally only 2 of 7 CGM trend adjustments (DOUBLE_UP, DOUBLE_DOWN) are tested — FORTY_FIVE_UP, FORTY_FIVE_DOWN, SINGLE_UP, SINGLE_DOWN, NONE are missing.

title: Add integration and e2e test suites for kdiab-calc and kdiab-carbs
description: Both services have empty integration-test/ and e2e-test/ source directories. CalcRoutes has zero route-level test coverage: auth/RBAC enforcement, invalid UUID handling, and all HTTP status codes are untested. ExposedFoodEntryRepository and FoodEntryRoutes similarly have no database-backed or HTTP-layer tests.

title: Raise kdiab-ui Vitest coverage threshold from 20% to 80% to match backend standard
description: vite.config.ts sets all coverage gates (statements/branches/functions/lines) at 20%, far below the 80% minimum enforced on all backends. This allows large portions of the React UI to regress without any automated safety net.

title: Add Vitest unit tests for DoseCalculator, MeasureList, and TreatmentList components
description: The four largest frontend components (DoseCalculator, MeasureList ~430 lines, TreatmentList ~350 lines, AddMeasureModal ~400 lines, AddTreatmentModal ~900 lines) have zero test files. Clinical dose recommendation UI and data entry forms are completely unverified. Total ~2,476 lines of untested code.

title: Add discriminated union types for measure/treatment data fields and status/type enums
description: Three type-safety gaps at API boundaries: (1) the 'data' field on MeasureResponse and TreatmentResponse is Record<string,unknown> instead of a discriminated union by type; (2) write-path API methods accept Record<string,unknown> bodies with no shape guarantee; (3) status ('ACTIVE'|'ARCHIVED'|'PROPOSED'|'DRAFT') and type fields are plain string, losing switch-exhaustiveness and typo detection across 6+ comparison sites.

title: Add visible :focus-visible ring to all interactive elements — currently missing on buttons
description: index.css suppresses native outline on inputs/selects (outline: none) and replaces it with box-shadow, but no equivalent :focus or :focus-visible style is defined for button elements. Keyboard users receive no visible focus indicator on tab buttons, action buttons, or segment Remove buttons (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7).

title: Fix keyboard navigation gaps — table rows, checkboxes, and tab buttons
description: Three WCAG violations: (1) clickable table rows in MeasureList and TreatmentList have no tabIndex, onKeyDown, or role='button' so keyboard users cannot expand detail rows; (2) all checkboxes lack aria-label or associated label elements; (3) main tab navigation buttons have no aria-current='page' — active tab is indicated only by CSS class.

title: Fix HYPO_TREATMENT reason placeholder hardcoded to 70 mg/dL regardless of user's unit
description: AddTreatmentModal line 847 shows placeholder 'e.g. glucose below 70 mg/dL' verbatim to mmol/L users, for whom the meaningful threshold is 3.9 mmol/L. The placeholder should be unit-aware.

title: Fix modal accessibility — add focus trap and correct aria-hidden placement
description: AddMeasureModal and AddTreatmentModal set initial focus but have no Tab-key focus trap (keyboard users can Tab out into the inert background, violating WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.2). Additionally, aria-hidden='true' on the overlay div also hides the nested role='dialog' from the accessibility tree, making the modal invisible to screen readers.

title: Fix MEAL treatment type editing in AddTreatmentModal — edit mode silently does nothing
description: The edit-mode useEffect switch has no 'case MEAL' branch, and handleSubmit routes MEAL to onSaveMeal only when !isEditMode. If a MEAL record is opened for editing, the form shows empty fields and Save silently does nothing. Patients cannot correct a mis-entered meal bolus.

title: Fix mmol/L glucose unit bugs in ProfileEditor and ProfileHistory
description: Multiple bugs affect mmol/L users: (1) ISF unit label in ProfileHistory hardwired to mg/dL instead of using glucoseUnit, (2) ISF and BG-target inputs use step=1 (appropriate for mg/dL, wrong for mmol/L — spinner increments by 1.0 mmol/L), (3) new ISF segment seed value is 50.0 regardless of unit (50 mmol/L/U is clinically absurd, correct range is 1-11).

title: Prevent doctors from creating or hard-deleting patient measures and treatments in UI
description: In App.tsx handleSaveMeasure and handleSaveTreatment always post to viewingUserId with no isDoctorViewingPatient gate on the Add buttons. Additionally canDelete={isAdmin || isDoctor} grants doctors destructive hard-delete on patient records. Doctors should not be able to create records in a patient's name or delete patient clinical history.

title: Wire ProfileHistory component into navigation — currently unreachable
description: ProfileHistory.tsx (showing full audit trail of profile changes with timeline) is never imported in App.tsx or any other rendered component. The feature is fully implemented but patients and doctors cannot access it. It should be linked from the Profiles tab.

title: Add ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING to seed SQL to prevent duplicate rows on container restart
description: config/postgres/02-seed-data.sql uses generate_series with gen_random_uuid() and no ON CONFLICT clause. Every pg-seed container restart duplicates all 8640 CGM readings and 90 daily treatments per user, corrupting test data.

title: Remove SchemaUtils.create() from kdiab-measures and kdiab-treatments DatabaseFactory
description: Both services call SchemaUtils.create(MeasuresTable/TreatmentsTable) at every startup alongside Liquibase. This silently recreates tables from the ORM model, bypassing Liquibase change-set tracking and column constraints. kdiab-profiles already uses Liquibase exclusively — measures and treatments should match.

title: Use patient's glucose unit (not doctor's) when doctor views patient data
description: When a doctor switches to view a patient, glucoseUnit passed to all views (MeasureList, AnalyticsView, DoseCalculator, ProfileEditor) is still the doctor's own unit from their JWT, not the patient's preferred unit. A mg/dL doctor reviewing a mmol/L patient sees incorrectly scaled glucose values.

title: Complete kdiab-common migration — remove duplicate Role, DomainExceptions, Security from analyze/calc/carbs
description: kdiab-analyze, kdiab-calc, and kdiab-carbs each define their own identical Role enum, DomainExceptions classes, and Security/Logging/StatusPages plugins despite depending on kdiab-common. The 4y3a common library task only migrated measures/profiles/treatments. The duplicates create silent divergence risk on any future change to these types.

title: Create per-service PostgreSQL roles — all backends currently share single superuser
description: Every service (measures, profiles, treatments, carbs) connects as the root postgres superuser. A compromised container can read or modify any other service's database. A dedicated database user per service with grants limited to its own schema is required.

title: Fix checkReadAccess on mutation endpoints in kdiab-measures and kdiab-carbs
description: createMeasure (MeasureRoutes.kt line 102), createFoodEntry, updateFoodEntry, and deleteFoodEntry all call checkReadAccess instead of checkWriteAccess. This allows doctors with allowedPatients access to create or mutate patient measures and food entries — bypassing the design intent that doctor access to these resources is read-only.

title: Bind PostgreSQL and Keycloak Admin Console to 127.0.0.1, not all interfaces
description: All compose stacks bind PostgreSQL on 5432 and Keycloak Admin on 8081 to all host interfaces. Any machine with external connectivity exposes raw PHI storage and the full identity provider admin console. Both should use 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 bindings or be removed from port mappings entirely for deployed environments.

title: Bump all dependencies to latest stable versions across all services
description: Dependencies across the five services (and kdiab-ui) are pinned to older versions. Audit and upgrade: Kotlin, Ktor server+client, Exposed v1, HikariCP, Liquibase, kotlinx-serialization, kotlinx-datetime, kotlinx-coroutines, MockK, JUnit5, Detekt, Kover, openapi-generator plugin, React 19 (already current?), @tanstack/react-query, react-oidc-context, Vite, Vitest, Playwright. After bumping, run ./gradlew check for all backends and npm run build for kdiab-ui. Fix any breaking API changes introduced by the upgrades.
close_reason: Backend deps already at latest stable. Frontend: vitest 4.x, jsdom 29.x, patch bumps. Major bumps (recharts 3.x, vite 8.x, typescript 6.x, i18next 26.x) deferred — require API migration work.

title: Extract shared kdiab-common library for cross-service utilities
description: UserPrincipal, Role, DomainExceptions, UpstreamException, Security plugin, StatusPages plugin, Logging plugin, and ErrorResponse are copy-pasted across all five services with only the package name changed. Extract these into a new kdiab-common Gradle library included via includeBuild. Each service declares a dependency on kdiab-common and removes its own copies. This eliminates the risk of divergence (e.g. a StatusPages fix applied to measures but not carbs) and reduces the overall codebase by ~600 lines.
design:
# OpenSpec: Shared kdiab-common library (kdiab-4y3a)

## Goal
Six domain types and five Ktor plugin functions are copy-pasted verbatim across all six services (measures, profiles, treatments, carbs, analyze, calc), differing only in package name. Extract them into a new `kdiab-common` Gradle subproject so any future change propagates automatically rather than requiring six parallel edits.

## Context
These files are virtually identical across all six services:
- `domain/model/Role.kt` — `Role` enum (PATIENT, DOCTOR, ADMIN) with `fromString()`
- `domain/exception/DomainExceptions.kt` — AuthenticationException, AuthorizationException, ResourceNotFoundException, BusinessValidationException, ConflictException
- `plugins/ErrorResponse.kt` — `@Serializable data class ErrorResponse(val code: Int, val message: String)`
- `plugins/Security.kt` — `UserPrincipal` data class + `Application.configureSecurity()` (reads jwt.* from config)
- `plugins/Logging.kt` — `Application.configureLogging()` (CallId + CallLogging, X-Correlation-ID)
- `plugins/StatusPages.kt` — `Application.configureStatusPages()` (7 common handlers; DB services add ExposedSQLException, non-DB services add UpstreamException)

Key difference: analyze and calc have an extra `UpstreamException` handler in StatusPages; measures/profiles/treatments/carbs have an `ExposedSQLException` handler. kdiab-analyze's `UserPrincipal` has an extra `audiences: List<String> = emptyList()` field. These are unified in common.

## Interface Changes
No API, DB, or OpenAPI changes. Internal package reorganization only.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Create kdiab-common project

1. `kdiab-common/settings.gradle.kts` — Create:
   ```kotlin
   pluginManagement {
       repositories {
           gradlePluginPortal()
           mavenCentral()
       }
   }
   rootProject.name = "kdiab-common"
   ```

2. `kdiab-common/build.gradle.kts` — Create:
   ```kotlin
   plugins {
       alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.jvm)
       alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.serialization)
   }
   group = "org.javafreedom.kdiab"
   version = "0.0.1"
   repositories { mavenCentral() }
   dependencies {
       implementation(libs.ktor.server.core)
       implementation(libs.ktor.server.auth)
       implementation(libs.ktor.server.auth.jwt)
       implementation(libs.ktor.server.status.pages)
       implementation(libs.ktor.server.call.id)
       implementation(libs.ktor.server.call.logging)
       implementation(libs.kotlinx.serialization.json)
       implementation(libs.kotlin.logging)
       implementation(libs.jwks.rsa)
       implementation(libs.java.jwt)
   }
   kotlin {
       jvmToolchain(21)
       compilerOptions { optIn.add("kotlin.uuid.ExperimentalUuidApi") }
   }
   ```
   Note: use the exact lib alias names that exist in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. For jwks-rsa and java-jwt, check the toml for their aliases (`libs.jwks.rsa` and `libs.java.jwt` or similar).

3. `kdiab-common/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/common/domain/model/Role.kt` — Create:
   ```kotlin
   package org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.domain.model
   enum class Role {
       PATIENT, DOCTOR, ADMIN;
       companion object {
           fun fromString(role: String): Role? = entries.find { it.name.equals(role, ignoreCase = true) }
       }
   }
   ```

4. `kdiab-common/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/common/domain/exception/DomainExceptions.kt` — Create with all five exception classes, package `org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.domain.exception`. Copy verbatim from any service's DomainExceptions.kt, only changing the package declaration.

5. `kdiab-common/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/common/plugins/ErrorResponse.kt` — Create:
   ```kotlin
   package org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.plugins
   import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
   @Serializable
   data class ErrorResponse(val code: Int, val message: String)
   ```

6. `kdiab-common/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/common/plugins/Security.kt` — Create, unifying both variants. Include `audiences: List<String> = emptyList()` in `UserPrincipal` (harmless for services that don't use it). Copy `configureSecurity()` logic verbatim from kdiab-measures — it reads all values from config so it is service-agnostic. Change package to `org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.plugins`. Update imports for `Role` to `org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.domain.model.Role`.

7. `kdiab-common/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/common/plugins/Logging.kt` — Create, copying verbatim from any service's `Logging.kt`. Change package to `org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.plugins`.

8. `kdiab-common/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/common/plugins/StatusPages.kt` — Create with an `extraHandlers` lambda:
   ```kotlin
   package org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.plugins
   import io.ktor.server.plugins.statuspages.*
   // ... other imports ...
   fun Application.configureStatusPages(
       extraHandlers: StatusPagesConfig.() -> Unit = {}
   ) {
       install(StatusPages) {
           exception<AuthenticationException> { ... }  // 401
           exception<AuthorizationException> { ... }   // 403
           exception<ConflictException> { ... }         // 409
           exception<ResourceNotFoundException> { ... } // 404
           exception<BusinessValidationException> { ... } // 400
           exception<IllegalArgumentException> { ... }  // 400
           exception<SerializationException> { ... }    // 400
           extraHandlers()
           exception<Throwable> { ... }                 // 500 — must be LAST
       }
   }
   ```
   Copy handler bodies verbatim from kdiab-analyze/plugins/StatusPages.kt (clean version). Import exceptions from `org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.domain.exception.*`.

### Phase 2 — Wire kdiab-common into root build

9. `settings.gradle.kts` (root) — Add `includeBuild("kdiab-common")` before the existing service includes.

### Phase 3 — Update each service (repeat steps 10-14 for all 6 services)

For each service in [kdiab-measures, kdiab-profiles, kdiab-treatments, kdiab-carbs, kdiab-analyze, kdiab-calc]:

10. `<service>/settings.gradle.kts` — Add `includeBuild("../kdiab-common")` at the end of the file.

11. `<service>/build.gradle.kts` — Add `implementation("org.javafreedom.kdiab:kdiab-common")` to the `dependencies` block.

12. Delete these files from `<service>/src/main/kotlin/.../`:
    - `plugins/Security.kt`
    - `plugins/StatusPages.kt`
    - `plugins/Logging.kt`
    - `plugins/ErrorResponse.kt`
    - `domain/model/Role.kt`
    - `domain/exception/DomainExceptions.kt`
    Note: kdiab-analyze and kdiab-calc also have `domain/exception/UpstreamException.kt` — DO NOT delete those.

13. `<service>/src/main/kotlin/.../Application.kt` — Update imports:
    - `import org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.plugins.configureLogging`
    - `import org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.plugins.configureSecurity`
    - `import org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.plugins.configureStatusPages`
    For DB services (measures, profiles, treatments, carbs), change `configureStatusPages()` call to:
    ```kotlin
    configureStatusPages {
        exception<ExposedSQLException> { call, cause ->
            val sqlState = cause.cause?.let { (it as? java.sql.SQLException)?.sqlState }
            if (sqlState == "23505") {
                logger.warn(cause) { "Unique constraint violation" }
                call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Conflict,
                    ErrorResponse(HttpStatusCode.Conflict.value, cause.message ?: "Conflict"))
            } else {
                logger.error(cause) { "Database error (SQL state: $sqlState)" }
                call.respond(HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError,
                    ErrorResponse(HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError.value, "Internal Server Error"))
            }
        }
    }
    ```
    For non-DB services (analyze, calc), change `configureStatusPages()` call to:
    ```kotlin
    configureStatusPages {
        exception<UpstreamException> { call, cause ->
            logger.error(cause) { "Upstream service error: ${cause.service}" }
            val status = HttpStatusCode.BadGateway
            call.respond(status, ErrorResponse(status.value, "Upstream service unavailable: ${cause.service}"))
        }
    }
    ```
    Add necessary imports for ExposedSQLException (DB services) or UpstreamException (non-DB services) and ErrorResponse from common.

14. For all other `.kt` source files in `<service>/src/main/kotlin/` that import the old service-local package paths:
    - Replace `import org.javafreedom.kdiab.<service>.domain.model.Role` → `import org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.domain.model.Role`
    - Replace `import org.javafreedom.kdiab.<service>.domain.exception.*` → `import org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.domain.exception.*`
    - Replace individual exception imports (AuthenticationException, AuthorizationException, etc.) with the common package equivalents
    - Replace `import org.javafreedom.kdiab.<service>.plugins.UserPrincipal` → `import org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.plugins.UserPrincipal`
    - Replace `import org.javafreedom.kdiab.<service>.plugins.ErrorResponse` → `import org.javafreedom.kdiab.common.plugins.ErrorResponse`
    Use grep to find all affected files first: `grep -r "kdiab.<service>.domain.model.Role\|kdiab.<service>.domain.exception\|kdiab.<service>.plugins.UserPrincipal\|kdiab.<service>.plugins.ErrorResponse" src/main/kotlin/`

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check` from kdiab-measures — all tests pass, Detekt clean
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check` from kdiab-profiles — same
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check` from kdiab-treatments — same
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check` from kdiab-carbs — same
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check` from kdiab-analyze — same
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check` from kdiab-calc — same

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Role, DomainExceptions, ErrorResponse, UserPrincipal, configureSecurity, configureLogging, configureStatusPages exist only in kdiab-common
- [ ] No service's `src/main/kotlin` imports Role or DomainExceptions from its own package
- [ ] `./gradlew check` from root is green

## Risks & Assumptions
- Library aliases for `jwks-rsa` and `java-jwt` in libs.versions.toml: check exact alias names before using them in kdiab-common/build.gradle.kts — run `grep -i "jwt\|jwks" gradle/libs.versions.toml` from kdiab-measures.

title: Switch upstream codegen to kotlin jvm-ktor and rewrite adapters to use generated clients
description: kdiab-of03 generates only model classes (kotlin-server, models-only). This issue goes further: switch to the kotlin jvm-ktor generator to produce full API client classes (models + DefaultApi + ApiClient infrastructure), then rewrite each outbound HTTP adapter (MeasuresClient, TreatmentsClient, ProfilesClient in kdiab-analyze; ProfilesClient in kdiab-calc) to call the generated API methods instead of raw httpClient.get/post calls. The adapters become thin orchestration layers: they inject JWT+correlation headers, run the pagination loop, and wrap ResponseException as UpstreamException — the URL construction, query parameter serialization, and JSON deserialization move to generated code.
design:
# OpenSpec: Switch upstream codegen to kotlin jvm-ktor and rewrite adapters (kdiab-l2uz)

## Goal
Replace the `kotlin-server` models-only generation (from kdiab-of03) with the `kotlin` generator using `library=jvm-ktor`. This generates full API client classes (models + `DefaultApi` + `ApiClient` infrastructure) from each upstream openapi.yaml. Then rewrite the four outbound HTTP adapters to call the generated API methods instead of raw `httpClient.get(url) { ... }` blocks. The adapters become thin orchestration: JWT injection + pagination loop + `UpstreamException` wrapping only; URL construction, param serialization, and JSON deserialization move to generated code.

---

## Context

### What kdiab-of03 produces (predecessor)
- `GenerateTask` instances in kdiab-analyze and kdiab-calc using `kotlin-server` + models-only
- Adapters import generated model types but still use raw `httpClient.get(...)` for HTTP

### What this issue changes
- Switch `generatorName` from `"kotlin-server"` to `"kotlin"` in all upstream GenerateTask instances
- Switch `library` config option from `"ktor"` to `"jvm-ktor"` (the client-side library)
- Expand `globalProperties` from `models-only` to include `apis` (and remove `supportingFiles` filter)
- Remove `templateDir` (server templates do not apply to client generator)
- Rewrite all four `*Client.kt` adapters to delegate HTTP calls to the generated `DefaultApi` class

### Files to read before touching anything
- `kdiab-analyze/build.gradle.kts` — current GenerateTask configs (added by kdiab-of03)
- `kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/outbound/http/MeasuresClient.kt`
- `kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/outbound/http/TreatmentsClient.kt`
- `kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/outbound/http/ProfilesClient.kt`
- `kdiab-calc/build.gradle.kts`
- `kdiab-calc/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/outbound/http/ProfilesClient.kt`
- `kdiab-calc/src/main/kotlin/.../application/service/DoseCalculationService.kt`

---

## Interface Changes
None (internal refactor — same network calls, same JSON, same domain types returned).

---

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1: Update GenerateTask configs in kdiab-analyze/build.gradle.kts

Read the file first. Find the three upstream GenerateTask blocks added by kdiab-of03.

For EACH of the three tasks (`generateMeasuresModels`, `generateTreatmentsModels`, `generateProfilesModels`), apply these changes:
- `generatorName.set("kotlin")` — was `"kotlin-server"`
- In `configOptions`:
  - `"library" to "jvm-ktor"` — was `"ktor"`
  - `"dateLibrary" to "string"` — keeps dates as String (simpler, consistent with existing)
  - `"useCoroutines" to "true"` — ensure suspend functions are generated
  - Keep `"serializationLibrary" to "kotlinx_serialization"`
- `globalProperties.set(mapOf("models" to "", "apis" to ""))` — add apis; remove supportingFiles filter
- Remove the `templateDir.set(...)` line — jvm-ktor does not use server-side templates

### Step 2: Inspect generated output

After updating the configs, run:
```bash
./gradlew generateMeasuresModels generateTreatmentsModels generateProfilesModels
```
Then inspect:
```bash
find build/generated/upstream-*/src -name "*.kt" | sort
```

Note the actual class names generated. The API class may be named `DefaultApi` (if the openapi spec has no tags) or something else. The `ApiClient` is in `infrastructure/ApiClient.kt`. Note the exact constructor signature.

### Step 3: Update kotlin sourceSet in kdiab-analyze/build.gradle.kts

Ensure the srcDir for each upstream package picks up `models/`, `apis/`, and `infrastructure/`:
```kotlin
kotlin.srcDir("${layout.buildDirectory.get()}/generated/upstream-measures/src/main/kotlin")
```
This is already correct if kdiab-of03 set it this way — the entire `src/main/kotlin` subtree is included.

Update kover excludes to add the `apis` and `infrastructure` sub-packages:
```kotlin
packages(
    "org.javafreedom.kdiab.analyze.api",
    "org.javafreedom.kdiab.analyze.api.upstream.measures",
    "org.javafreedom.kdiab.analyze.api.upstream.treatments",
    "org.javafreedom.kdiab.analyze.api.upstream.profiles",
)
```

### Step 4: Rewrite MeasuresClient.kt

Read the file. Replace the body of `getMeasures()` to use the generated client.

The generated `jvm-ktor` ApiClient wraps a Ktor HttpClient. Pass the shared httpClient to it and configure the JWT Bearer token per-call. The exact constructor depends on what was generated — read the generated `ApiClient.kt` first.

Typical rewrite pattern:
```kotlin
class MeasuresClient(
    private val httpClient: HttpClient,
    private val baseUrl: String,
) {
    suspend fun getMeasures(
        userId: String,
        authorization: String,
        correlationId: String,
        from: String? = null,
        to: String? = null,
    ): List<MeasureResponse> {
        // Create per-call ApiClient with JWT + correlation ID headers
        val apiClient = ApiClient(
            baseUrl = baseUrl,
            httpClientEngine = httpClient.engine,
        ).apply {
            // Set Bearer token — method name depends on generated code, check ApiClient
            setBearerToken(authorization.removePrefix("Bearer ").trim())
        }
        // Create the generated API instance
        val api = DefaultApi(apiClient)  // actual class name from generated files

        val result = mutableListOf<MeasureResponse>()
        var page = 0
        var totalCount = Long.MAX_VALUE
        val totalStart = System.currentTimeMillis()

        while (result.size < totalCount) {
            check(result.size < MAX_MEASURES) { "Too many measures ..." }
            val pageStart = System.currentTimeMillis()
            val paged = try {
                api.listMeasures(
                    userId = userId,
                    page = page,
                    size = PAGE_SIZE,
                    from = from,
                    to = to,
                    status = null,
                )
            } catch (e: ResponseException) {
                val body = runCatching { e.response.bodyAsText() }.getOrNull()
                throw UpstreamException("measures", e.response.status.value, e.response.status.description, body, e.response.request.url.toString())
            }
            // paged is already deserialized — no more response.body<PagedMeasureResponse>()
            totalCount = paged.totalCount
            result.addAll(paged.items)
            if (paged.items.isEmpty()) break
            page++
        }

        logger.info { "Fetched ${result.size} measures in $page pages" }
        return result
    }
}
```

**IMPORTANT**: Read the actual generated `DefaultApi.kt` to see the exact method signature for `listMeasures` (parameter names may differ). Do not guess.

If the generated ApiClient constructor does not accept `httpClientEngine`, inspect the actual generated code and use whatever constructor/configuration it provides. Common patterns:
- `ApiClient(baseUrl, HttpClient(engine) { ... })`
- `ApiClient(baseUrl, httpClient)`
- `DefaultApi(baseUrl, httpClientEngine = engine)`

### Step 5: Rewrite TreatmentsClient.kt

Same pattern as Step 4. Read generated `DefaultApi.kt` (or equivalent) for the treatments package. Method name is `listTreatments` based on the openapi operationId.

Pagination loop is identical to measures.

### Step 6: Rewrite ProfilesClient.kt (kdiab-analyze)

No pagination loop needed — just fetches one page. Pattern:
```kotlin
val api = DefaultApi(apiClient)
val paged = try {
    api.listProfiles(userId = userId, page = 0, size = DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE)
} catch (e: ResponseException) {
    throw UpstreamException(...)
}
return paged.items
```

### Step 7: Update kdiab-calc/build.gradle.kts

Same changes as Step 1 but for the single `generateProfilesModels` task.

### Step 8: Update kdiab-calc ProfilesClient.kt

Same pattern as Step 6. The generated profiles types are in package `org.javafreedom.kdiab.calc.api.upstream.profiles`.

Return type is `ProfileResponse?` (filtered from paged list where status == "ACTIVE").

### Step 9: Update DoseCalculationService.kt if needed

If Step 8 changes the return type of `getActiveProfile()`, update any callers. The field names should remain the same (`id`, `status`, `isf`, `icr`, `targets`, `durationOfAction`). The segment field name is `startTime` (not `time`) — this should already be fixed by kdiab-of03.

### Step 10: Run quality gates

```bash
# In kdiab-analyze directory
./gradlew check

# In kdiab-calc directory
./gradlew check
```

Fix all compilation errors before committing.

---

## Test Plan
- [ ] `find kdiab-analyze/build/generated/upstream-*/src -name "*.kt" | grep -E "apis|Api"` — generated API classes exist
- [ ] `./gradlew check` in kdiab-analyze — BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- [ ] `./gradlew check` in kdiab-calc — BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- [ ] No `httpClient.get(...)` or `httpClient.request(...)` calls remain inside `MeasuresClient.kt`, `TreatmentsClient.kt`, or either `ProfilesClient.kt` — all HTTP is delegated to generated clients

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All four `*Client.kt` adapters use generated API classes for HTTP calls
- [ ] `generatorName = "kotlin"` with `library = "jvm-ktor"` in all upstream GenerateTask configs
- [ ] Both quality gates pass

## Risks & Assumptions
- The generated ApiClient may not accept an external HttpClient directly; if so, configure it with a minimal `HttpClient(CIO)` using the same timeout values from application.conf.
- The generated API method names are derived from `operationId` in the openapi spec: `listMeasures`, `listTreatments`, `listProfiles`. Confirm by reading the generated `DefaultApi.kt`.
- `ResponseException` (from `io.ktor.client.plugins.ClientRequestException` / `ServerResponseException`) is what the generated jvm-ktor client throws on non-2xx. Import the right class.
- If `listMeasures` returns `PagedMeasureResponse` directly (not wrapped), omit the `response.body<...>()` call.
- kdiab-of03 must be merged and present in the worktree before starting this issue (dependency).

title: Generate upstream HTTP client models from upstream OpenAPI specs
description: Currently kdiab-analyze and kdiab-calc hand-write Kotlin DTOs (ProfileDto, MeasureDto, TreatmentDto, etc.) in their outbound HTTP client adapters. These hand-written DTOs can drift from the upstream service's actual API. The fix: configure additional openApiGenerate Gradle tasks in kdiab-analyze and kdiab-calc that point at the upstream services' openapi.yaml files and generate the model classes automatically. Also publish each service's openapi.yaml as a Gradle artifact so it can be consumed by other services cleanly. Remove all hand-written upstream DTOs and replace with generated ones. Affected: kdiab-analyze (MeasuresClient, ProfilesClient, TreatmentsClient), kdiab-calc (ProfilesClient).
design:
# OpenSpec: Generate upstream HTTP client models from upstream OpenAPI specs (kdiab-of03)

## Goal
Replace all hand-written upstream DTO classes in kdiab-analyze and kdiab-calc with models auto-generated from the upstream services' own openapi.yaml specs. This ensures client DTOs are always in sync with the actual upstream API contract. Also publish each service's openapi.yaml as a Gradle artifact configuration so consuming services can reference it cleanly.

title: Enforce Kover coverage gate in kdiab-analyze: verify task configured but not set to fail build
description: kdiab-analyze/build.gradle.kts has a Kover verify rule defined but the fail-on-violation setting is not enforced — the build succeeds even when coverage drops below the threshold. Unlike the other three services which have properly enforced 80% gates, kdiab-analyze's gate is effectively toothless.
design:
# OpenSpec: Enforce Kover coverage gate in kdiab-analyze (kdiab-1mj)

## Goal
`kdiab-analyze/build.gradle.kts` configures a Kover `verify` rule with `minValue = 80` but the `koverVerify` task is not explicitly wired into the `check` lifecycle. The `check` task only declares dependencies on `integrationTest` and `e2eTest` test suites. In the absence of those suites having tests, `koverVerify` may not run, making the coverage gate effectively non-blocking.

## Context
- `kdiab-analyze/build.gradle.kts` lines 139-142: `tasks.named("check") { dependsOn(integrationTest, e2eTest) }` — no `koverVerify` dependency.
- Lines 228-234: `kover.reports.verify { rule { bound { minValue = 80 } } }` — gate configured but not wired.
- In kdiab-analyze, `application/service/TimelineService.kt` and `application/service/ProfilesService.kt` have no unit tests (only `AnalyticsServiceTest.kt` exists). Coverage of non-excluded packages may be below 80%, which should fail the gate but doesn't because `koverVerify` is not guaranteed to run as part of `check`.
- Kover plugin: when `tasks.named("check")` is explicitly configured with `dependsOn`, Kover's automatic hook-in to `check` may be bypassed depending on plugin application order.

## Interface Changes
No API changes. Build behavior change only.

## Implementation Plan
1. `kdiab-analyze/build.gradle.kts` — In the existing `tasks.named("check")` block (lines 139-142), add `dependsOn("koverVerify")`:
   ```kotlin
   tasks.named("check") {
       dependsOn(testing.suites.named("integrationTest"))
       dependsOn(testing.suites.named("e2eTest"))
       dependsOn("koverVerify")
   }
   ```
   If coverage is below 80% after wiring (because TimelineService/ProfilesService have no unit tests), add them to the Kover exclusions with a comment:
   ```kotlin
   packages(
       ...
       // TimelineService and ProfilesService are covered by integration/e2e tests (kdiab-yly)
       "org.javafreedom.kdiab.analyze.application.service"
   )
   ```

## Test Plan
- [ ] Run `./gradlew tasks --all | grep -i kover` in kdiab-analyze/ to confirm task name is `koverVerify`
- [ ] `./gradlew :check --no-daemon` from `kdiab-analyze/` — confirm the `koverVerify` task runs (appears in task execution output)
- [ ] Verify the build passes with coverage ≥ 80% (or exclusions in place)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `koverVerify` task appears in the `check` task's dependency chain when running `./gradlew :check --info`
- [ ] If coverage falls below 80%, `./gradlew :check` fails with a Kover violation message
- [ ] `./gradlew :check` passes (either coverage is sufficient or appropriate exclusions are added)

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Coverage may currently be below 80%**: wiring `koverVerify` may cause the build to fail. In that case, add `application.service` package to Kover exclusions with a comment noting it is covered by integration tests (kdiab-yly).
- Task name `"koverVerify"` assumes Kover 0.7/0.8 naming convention — verify with `./gradlew tasks --all | grep kover` before implementing.
close_reason: koverVerify wired into check task; fixed AnalyticsServiceTest mock mismatches that were pre-existing failures

# OpenSpec: Fix missing error states in AnalyticsView and ProfilesView (kdiab-dy5) ## Goal AnalyticsView and ProfilesView in kdiab-ui do not render any UI when their API queries fail — users see blank space. Add explicit error banners for each failing query so clinicians know data could not be loaded. ## Context - `kdiab-ui/src/features/analytics/AnalyticsView.tsx` lines 21–54: hba1cQuery and agpQuery use useQuery, but neither hba1cQuery.isError nor agpQuery.isError is checked in the render path. Failed queries produce blank sections. - `kdiab-ui/src/features/analytics/ProfilesView.tsx` lines 18–42: profilesQuery uses useQuery. The fallback `!profilesQuery.isLoading && !profilesQuery.data` catches both empty and error cases and shows No data — an error should show a distinct message. - ProfileHistory.tsx already has proper error handling; this issue is only about AnalyticsView and ProfilesView. ## Interface Changes No interface changes. ## Implementation Plan 1. `kdiab-ui/src/features/analytics/AnalyticsView.tsx` — After the loading check, add error banners for hba1cQuery.isError and agpQuery.isError using `
{t('analytics.hba1cError')}
` and similarly for agp. 2. `kdiab-ui/src/features/analytics/ProfilesView.tsx` — Add `{profilesQuery.isError &&
{t('analytics.profilesError')}
}` and change the no-data fallback to also check `!profilesQuery.isError`. 3. `kdiab-ui/src/index.css` — Add `.error-banner` style if not already present: `background: var(--color-error-bg, rgba(239,68,68,0.12)); border: 1px solid var(--color-error, #ef4444); border-radius: 6px; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; margin-bottom: 1rem; color: var(--text-primary); font-size: 0.875rem;` 4. `kdiab-ui/src/i18n/locales/en.json` — Add inside "analytics" section: `"hba1cError": "Could not load HbA1c data"`, `"agpError": "Could not load AGP data"`, `"profilesError": "Could not load profiles"` 5. `kdiab-ui/src/i18n/locales/de.json` — Add inside "analytics" section: `"hba1cError": "HbA1c-Daten konnten nicht geladen werden"`, `"agpError": "AGP-Daten konnten nicht geladen werden"`, `"profilesError": "Profile konnten nicht geladen werden"` ## Test Plan - [ ] `npm run build` in `kdiab-ui/` — TypeScript compiles clean - [ ] `npm run lint` — no lint errors ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] AnalyticsView shows error banners for HbA1c and AGP query failures - [ ] ProfilesView shows an error banner on failure instead of the no-data fallback - [ ] TypeScript compiles clean; lint passes ## Risks & Assumptions - If .error-banner already exists in index.css, skip adding it. - The "analytics" i18n section already exists; verify the key names do not conflict with existing keys.

title: Fix BFF domain models: use kotlin.uuid.Uuid and kotlinx.datetime.Instant instead of String
description: Timeline, TimelineMeasure, and TimelineTreatment domain models in kdiab-analyze use raw String for all identifiers (userId, id) and timestamps (measuredAt, treatedAt), losing type safety compared to upstream services that use kotlin.uuid.Uuid and kotlinx.datetime.Instant. Parse errors on malformed IDs silently produce wrong results.
design:
# OpenSpec: Fix BFF domain models — use Uuid and Instant (kdiab-8sb)

## Goal
TimelineMeasure and TimelineTreatment domain models use String for id, userId, and timestamps instead of kotlin.uuid.Uuid and kotlinx.datetime.Instant. Changing these to proper types makes parsing errors explicit and aligns with CLAUDE.md conventions.

## Context
- kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../domain/model/Timeline.kt: TimelineMeasure (id, userId, measuredAt as String) and TimelineTreatment (id, userId, treatedAt as String).
- kdiab-analyze/.../application/service/TimelineService.kt: Maps upstream DTOs (String fields) to domain objects. Currently passes strings through.
- kdiab-analyze/.../adapters/inbound/web/BffMapper.kt: Maps domain → @Serializable response DTOs which can stay as String.
- Upstream DTOs (MeasureDto, TreatmentDto) use String — unchanged.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes (response DTOs stay as String).

## Implementation Plan
1. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../domain/model/Timeline.kt — Add @file:OptIn(kotlin.uuid.ExperimentalUuidApi::class), imports kotlin.uuid.Uuid and kotlinx.datetime.Instant. Change:
   - TimelineMeasure: id: Uuid, userId: Uuid, measuredAt: Instant.
   - TimelineTreatment: id: Uuid, userId: Uuid, treatedAt: Instant.
2. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../application/service/TimelineService.kt — Update DTO→domain mapping:
   - Wrap Uuid.parse(dto.id), Uuid.parse(dto.userId), Instant.parse(dto.measuredAt/treatedAt) in runCatching { }.getOrNull() and use .filterNotNull() to silently drop malformed upstream entries.
   - Remove any String-based date comparison; use Instant comparison directly (>=, <=) for from/to filtering.
3. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/inbound/web/BffMapper.kt — Update domain→DTO mapping:
   - id = domain.id.toString(), userId = domain.userId.toString(), measuredAt/treatedAt = domain.measuredAt/treatedAt.toString().

## Test Plan

title: Add HTTP timeouts to TreatmentsClient and ProfilesClient (only MeasuresClient has them)
description: MeasuresClient has connect/request/socket timeout configuration but TreatmentsClient and ProfilesClient have no explicit timeout setup. A slow treatments or profiles upstream will block the BFF coroutine indefinitely, creating asymmetric failure modes and eventual thread pool exhaustion.
design:
# OpenSpec: Add explicit per-request timeouts to TreatmentsClient and ProfilesClient (kdiab-set)

## Goal
`TreatmentsClient` and `ProfilesClient` have no explicit timeout configuration in their HTTP calls. While the shared `HttpClient` in `Application.kt` installs `HttpTimeout` globally (5s connect, 10s request, 5s socket), the individual client files contain no timeout overrides — making the timeout policy invisible and easily broken if the `HttpClient` is replaced in tests. Add explicit per-request timeout overrides matching the global policy.

## Context
- `kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/…/Application.kt` (lines 27-29, 81-85): defines `HTTP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000L`, `HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000L`, `HTTP_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000L` and installs `HttpTimeout` on the shared `HttpClient`. All three clients share this `HttpClient`.
- `TreatmentsClient.kt`: single `httpClient.get()` call — no per-request `timeout { }` block.
- `ProfilesClient.kt`: single `httpClient.get()` call — no per-request `timeout { }` block.
- `MeasuresClient.kt`: paginated calls — also no per-request timeouts; not in scope for this issue.
- The timeout constants in Application.kt are `private const val` — not accessible from client files.

## Interface Changes
No API or external interface changes.

## Implementation Plan
1. `kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/adapters/outbound/http/TreatmentsClient.kt` — Add private timeout constants at the top of the file:
   ```kotlin
   private const val CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000L
   private const val REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000L
   private const val SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000L
   ```
   Inside the `httpClient.get(...)` builder block, add:
   ```kotlin
   timeout {
       connectTimeoutMillis = CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS
       requestTimeoutMillis = REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS
       socketTimeoutMillis = SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS
   }
   ```
2. `kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/adapters/outbound/http/ProfilesClient.kt` — Same: add private timeout constants and `timeout { }` block inside `httpClient.get()`.

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew :check --no-daemon` from `kdiab-analyze/` — Detekt clean, existing tests pass
- [ ] Verify `timeout { }` block uses `io.ktor.client.plugins.timeout` import (already available via `ktor-client-cio` dependency)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `TreatmentsClient` and `ProfilesClient` each have per-request `timeout { }` blocks
- [ ] Timeout values match the global policy (5s connect, 10s request, 5s socket)
- [ ] `./gradlew :check` passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- Per-request `timeout { }` overrides the global `HttpTimeout` plugin for that call. Using the same values means no behavioral change in production.
- The `io.ktor.client.plugins.timeout` function is available when `ktor-client-cio` is on the classpath — no new dependency needed.
- Detekt may warn about duplicate constants — suppress with `@Suppress("MagicNumber")` if needed.
close_reason: Per-request timeouts added to TreatmentsClient and ProfilesClient per OpenSpec

title: Fix unsafe TypeScript type assertions in kdiab-ui: AgpChart non-null percentiles, Error casts, TimeFormatContext useState
description: Three distinct unsafe patterns: (1) AgpChart uses d.p10!, d.p25!, d.p75!, d.p90! non-null assertions on nullable percentile fields after filtering only for d.median !== null; (2) ProfileList and AdminInsulinManager cast error as Error without type guards; (3) TimeFormatContext passes getInitialLocale function reference to useState instead of calling it (getInitialLocale()), causing stale initial state.
design:
# OpenSpec: Fix unsafe TypeScript type assertions (kdiab-8h5)

## Goal
Fix four distinct unsafe TypeScript patterns in kdiab-ui: non-null assertions on nullable AGP percentiles after only filtering for median, unsafe `error as Error` casts in ProfileList and AdminInsulinManager, and calling `useState(getInitialLocale)` (function reference) instead of `useState(getInitialLocale())` (explicit call) in TimeFormatContext.

## Context
- `kdiab-ui/src/features/analytics/AgpChart.tsx` lines 37–43: `filter(d => d.median !== null)` then uses `d.p10!`, `d.p25!`, `d.p75!`, `d.p90!`, `d.median!` — p10/p25/p75/p90 may still be null even when median is not.
- `kdiab-ui/src/features/profiles/ProfileList.tsx` line 100: `(error as Error).message` — error may not be an Error instance.
- `kdiab-ui/src/features/profiles/AdminInsulinManager.tsx` line 51: same `(error as Error).message` pattern.
- `kdiab-ui/src/context/TimeFormatContext.tsx` line 26: `useState<string>(getInitialLocale)` — function reference rather than explicit call.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes.

## Implementation Plan
1. `kdiab-ui/src/features/analytics/AgpChart.tsx` — Change the filter to require all 5 percentile fields to be non-null (d.median !== null && d.p10 !== null && d.p25 !== null && d.p75 !== null && d.p90 !== null), then remove the `!` non-null assertions in the map. TypeScript will narrow the type.
2. `kdiab-ui/src/features/profiles/ProfileList.tsx` line 100 — Replace `(error as Error).message` with `error instanceof Error ? error.message : t('common.unknownError')`
3. `kdiab-ui/src/features/profiles/AdminInsulinManager.tsx` line 51 — Same fix: `error instanceof Error ? error.message : t('common.unknownError')`
4. `kdiab-ui/src/context/TimeFormatContext.tsx` line 26 — Change `useState<string>(getInitialLocale)` to `useState<string>(getInitialLocale())`
5. `kdiab-ui/src/i18n/locales/en.json` — Add inside `"common"` section (create if missing): `"unknownError": "An unknown error occurred"`
6. `kdiab-ui/src/i18n/locales/de.json` — Add: `"unknownError": "Ein unbekannter Fehler ist aufgetreten"`

## Test Plan
- [ ] `npm run build` in `kdiab-ui/` — TypeScript compiles clean
- [ ] `npm run lint` — no lint errors

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AgpChart filter guards all 5 percentile fields; no non-null assertions on nullable types
- [ ] Error casts use `instanceof Error` guard in ProfileList and AdminInsulinManager
- [ ] TimeFormatContext uses `getInitialLocale()` call (not function reference)
- [ ] TypeScript compiles clean; lint passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- The narrowed type after the more restrictive filter must be inferred correctly by TypeScript. Check the generated API type for AgpHourlyData — if TypeScript cannot narrow through the filter predicate, use a type predicate function instead.
- `common.unknownError` key: check if a `"common"` namespace already exists in i18n files; if not, create it.
- Filtering out buckets with null p10/p25/p75/p90 may reduce chart data points; this is correct (incomplete data should not be rendered).
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec in isolated worktree

title: Validate JWT audience at BFF layer before forwarding tokens to upstream services
description: BffRoutes.kt forwards the Authorization header to upstream services without verifying the JWT audience includes the target service (measure/treatment/profile). A token issued only for the 'analyze' audience would be accepted by the BFF but rejected by upstreams with a 401, producing confusing cascading errors rather than a clear 403 at the BFF.
design:
# OpenSpec: Validate JWT audience at BFF before forwarding (kdiab-geg)

## Goal
BffRoutes.kt forwards the Authorization header without verifying the JWT includes measure, profile, and treatment audiences. Add audience verification in extractContext() and surface audiences in UserPrincipal.

## Context
- kdiab-analyze/.../plugins/Security.kt line 67: validates only analyze audience. UserPrincipal (lines 89-102) has no audiences field.
- kdiab-analyze/.../adapters/inbound/web/BffRoutes.kt extractContext() (lines 107-125): called on every BFF route. AuthorizationException → 403 via StatusPages.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes.

## Implementation Plan
1. kdiab-analyze/.../plugins/Security.kt — Add audiences: List<String> = emptyList() to UserPrincipal. In the validate block (line 80), pass audiences = credential.payload.audience ?: emptyList().
2. kdiab-analyze/.../adapters/inbound/web/BffRoutes.kt — In extractContext() after the canAccess check (around line 121), add:
   val required = listOf("measure", "profile", "treatment")
   val missing = required.filter { it !in principal!!.audiences }
   if (missing.isNotEmpty()) {
       throw AuthorizationException(
           "JWT is missing required upstream audiences: ${missing.joinToString(", ")}. " +
           "Configure your Keycloak client with audience mappers for all four services."
       )
   }

## Test Plan
- [ ] ./gradlew check --no-daemon from kdiab-analyze/ — all tests pass.
- [ ] Check existing test JWT setup: if tests use withAudience(jwtAudience) (only analyze), update test JWTs to include measure, profile, treatment audiences too.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] JWT with only analyze audience → 403 with descriptive message.
- [ ] JWT with all four audiences → proceeds normally.
- [ ] ./gradlew check passes.

## Risks & Assumptions
- Existing tests in kdiab-analyze/src/test/ likely use HMAC256 test JWTs that only have the analyze audience — must update test JWT helpers to include all four, or the new check will break tests.
- Read existing test JWT helpers before making changes to understand how to add the additional audiences.

title: Add circuit breaker to BFF upstream HTTP calls
description: kdiab-analyze has no circuit breaker (e.g. Resilience4j). When an upstream service (measures/treatments/profiles) is degraded, every BFF request waits for the full timeout before failing, exhausting the Ktor thread pool. A circuit breaker that opens after N failures would fail fast and protect the BFF.

title: Fix /readyz probe: verify upstream service availability before reporting ready
description: The /readyz endpoint in kdiab-analyze returns 200 OK without checking whether upstream services (measures, treatments, profiles) are reachable. A freshly started analyze container incorrectly signals ready while its dependencies are still starting, causing load balancers to route traffic before the BFF can actually serve requests.
design:
# OpenSpec: Fix /readyz probe to verify upstream availability (kdiab-8q2)

## Goal
kdiab-analyze's /readyz returns 200 OK without checking whether the three upstream services are reachable. Refactor Application.kt to have the readyz handler call /healthz on each upstream service and return 503 if any is unreachable.

## Context
- kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../Application.kt line 106: get("/readyz") { call.respond(HttpStatusCode.OK) } — no checks.
- The httpClient is created only in the else branch (production mode). In test mode (services passed as parameters), no httpClient exists.
- Upstream services expose /healthz (no auth, returns 200) — kdiab-measures line 79.
- Upstream URLs (measuresUrl, profilesUrl, treatmentsUrl) loaded in the else branch.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes.

## Implementation Plan
1. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../Application.kt — Refactor the if/else block to declare var healthClient: HttpClient? = null and var upstreamHealthUrls: List<String> = emptyList() before the if/else. In the else branch (production), after creating the HttpClient, set:
   healthClient = httpClient
   upstreamHealthUrls = listOf("$measuresUrl/healthz", "$profilesUrl/healthz", "$treatmentsUrl/healthz")
   Replace the readyz handler:
   get("/readyz") {
       val client = healthClient
       if (client == null || upstreamHealthUrls.isEmpty()) {
           call.respond(HttpStatusCode.OK)
       } else {
           val allReady = upstreamHealthUrls.all { url ->
               runCatching { client.get(url) { expectSuccess = false } }
                   .mapCatching { it.status.isSuccess() }
                   .getOrDefault(false)
           }
           if (allReady) call.respond(HttpStatusCode.OK)
           else call.respond(HttpStatusCode.ServiceUnavailable)
       }
   }
   Add import io.ktor.client.request.get if not present.

## Test Plan
- [ ] ./gradlew check --no-daemon from kdiab-analyze/ — existing tests pass (healthClient is null in test mode, readyz returns OK).
- [ ] Manual: start kdiab-analyze without upstreams → GET /readyz → 503.
- [ ] Manual: full stack → GET /readyz → 200.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /readyz returns 503 when any upstream /healthz is unreachable.
- [ ] /readyz returns 200 when all three upstreams are healthy.
- [ ] Test mode (services passed as parameters) still returns 200.

## Risks & Assumptions
- expectSuccess = false prevents the HttpClient from throwing on non-2xx responses.
- The existing httpClient already has timeout configuration — the same client can be reused for health checks.
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec in isolated worktree

title: Add retry logic to BFF HTTP clients for transient upstream failures
description: MeasuresClient, TreatmentsClient, and ProfilesClient have no retry policy — a single transient timeout or 5xx response immediately causes 502 Bad Gateway. Adding exponential backoff with 2-3 retries for idempotent GET requests would significantly improve resilience against brief upstream hiccups.
design:
# OpenSpec: Add retry logic to BFF HTTP clients for transient upstream failures (kdiab-lbx)

## Goal
The three BFF HTTP clients have no retry policy. A single transient 5xx or timeout produces an immediate 502. Install Ktor's HttpRequestRetry plugin on the shared HttpClient in Application.kt.

## Context
- kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../Application.kt lines 82-89: HttpClient(CIO) installs ContentNegotiation + HttpTimeout only. All three clients share this instance.
- MeasuresClient.kt: pagination loop calling httpClient.get() per page — no retry.
- TreatmentsClient.kt / ProfilesClient.kt: single httpClient.get(), throw UpstreamException on non-2xx.
- io.ktor.client.plugins.HttpRequestRetry is in ktor-client-core — no new dependency.
- 4xx responses (401/403) must NOT be retried.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes.

## Implementation Plan
1. `kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/Application.kt` — In the HttpClient(CIO) { ... } block, add after install(HttpTimeout):
   install(HttpRequestRetry) {
       maxRetries = 3
       retryIf { _, response -> response.status.value >= 500 }
       retryOnExceptionIf { _, cause ->
           cause is java.net.SocketTimeoutException ||
           cause is io.ktor.client.plugins.HttpRequestTimeoutException
       }
       exponentialDelay(base = 2.0, maxDelayMs = 8_000L)
   }
   Add import io.ktor.client.plugins.HttpRequestRetry if needed.

## Test Plan
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check from kdiab-analyze/ — all existing tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] HttpRequestRetry installed on the shared HttpClient.
- [ ] Retries only on 5xx and timeout exceptions; 4xx propagates immediately.
- [ ] Max 3 retries, exponential backoff base 2s, cap 8s.
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check passes.

## Risks & Assumptions
- io.ktor.client.plugins.HttpRequestRetry is in ktor-client-core in Ktor 3.x. No build.gradle.kts change needed.
- Each page GET in MeasuresClient pagination loop is retried independently — correct behavior.
- exponentialDelay() uses kotlinx.coroutines.delay — safe in coroutine context.
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec

# OpenSpec: Add DateTimeParseException and ExposedSQLException handlers to StatusPages (kdiab-705)

## Goal
kdiab-measures, kdiab-treatments, and kdiab-analyze StatusPages plugins do not handle DateTimeParseException/DateTimeFormatException or ExposedSQLException. An invalid from/to query param causes a 500 instead of 400. A DB unique constraint violation returns 500 instead of 409. kdiab-profiles/plugins/StatusPages.kt is the reference implementation.

## Context
- kdiab-profiles/.../plugins/StatusPages.kt: handles ExposedSQLException - SQL state '23505' -> 409, otherwise -> 500.
- kdiab-measures/.../plugins/StatusPages.kt: missing DateTimeParseException and ExposedSQLException handlers.
- kdiab-treatments/.../plugins/StatusPages.kt: missing DateTimeParseException and ExposedSQLException handlers. ConflictException IS already registered (line 33).
- kdiab-analyze/.../plugins/StatusPages.kt: missing DateTimeParseException handler only (no DB layer).
- Instant.parse() from kotlinx.datetime throws IllegalArgumentException for invalid format strings. In kotlinx.datetime 0.6+, it may throw DateTimeFormatException (a subclass of IllegalArgumentException). The existing IllegalArgumentException handler may already cover parse errors - verify the kotlinx.datetime version in libs.versions.toml.

## Interface Changes
HTTP status code change: invalid date param -> 400 (was 500); DB unique constraint -> 409 (was 500).

## Implementation Plan
1. Check libs.versions.toml for kotlinx.datetime version to determine if DateTimeFormatException is distinct from IllegalArgumentException.

2. kdiab-measures/.../plugins/StatusPages.kt
   - Add before the generic Throwable handler:
     exception<org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.core.exceptions.ExposedSQLException> { call, cause ->
         val sqlState = cause.sqlState
         if (sqlState == '23505') {
             logger.warn(cause) { 'Unique constraint violation' }
             call.respond(HttpStatusCode.Conflict,
                 ErrorResponse(HttpStatusCode.Conflict.value, cause.message ?: 'Conflict'))
         } else {
             logger.error(cause) { 'Database error (SQL state: $sqlState)' }
             call.respond(HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError,
                 ErrorResponse(HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError.value, 'Internal Server Error'))
         }
     }
   - If kotlinx.datetime throws a distinct DateTimeFormatException not covered by IllegalArgumentException, add handler mapping to 400.

3. kdiab-treatments/.../plugins/StatusPages.kt
   - Same ExposedSQLException handler as step 2.
   - Same DateTimeFormatException handler if needed.

4. kdiab-analyze/.../plugins/StatusPages.kt
   - Add DateTimeFormatException handler if distinct from IllegalArgumentException.

## Test Plan
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check --no-daemon from kdiab-measures/ - all checks pass
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check --no-daemon from kdiab-treatments/ - all checks pass
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check --no-daemon from kdiab-analyze/ - all checks pass
- [ ] Manual: GET /api/v1/users/{id}/measures?from=notadate -> 400 Bad Request

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Invalid date query param returns 400 in all three services
- [ ] DB unique constraint violation returns 409 in measures and treatments
- [ ] All three ./gradlew :backend:check pass

## Risks & Assumptions
- If Instant.parse() already throws IllegalArgumentException (covered by existing handler), only ExposedSQLException needs adding for measures/treatments, and no change needed for analyze.
- Follow the kdiab-profiles StatusPages.kt pattern exactly for ExposedSQLException.
close_reason: ExposedSQLException handler added to measures and treatments StatusPages; SQL state 23505 -> 409, else -> 500 (merged from worktree-agent-a405a5b2a78ae97a5)

# OpenSpec: Add ACTIVITY and HYPO_TREATMENT cases to TreatmentList renderDataSummary (kdiab-xb0)

## Goal
TreatmentList.tsx's renderDataSummary() switch falls through to JSON.stringify(d) for ACTIVITY and HYPO_TREATMENT treatment types. Both exist in the TreatmentType enum. Add human-friendly display cases for both.

## Context
- kdiab-ui/src/features/treatments/TreatmentList.tsx lines 20-58: renderDataSummary switch.
- Has cases for: BOLUS, CORRECTION_BOLUS, COMBO_BOLUS, BASAL, CARBS, TEMP_BASAL, EXERCISE, NOTE, PUMP_SUSPEND, SITE_CHANGE, SENSOR_INSERT, INSULIN_CHANGE.

- ACTIVITY data per openapi.yaml: {name: 'running', duration: 45, intensity: 'moderate'}.
- HYPO_TREATMENT data per openapi.yaml: {carbs: 15, reason: 'glucose below 70'}.

No interface changes - frontend display only.

   - After the 'case EXERCISE:' block (line 45), insert before 'case NOTE:':
     case 'ACTIVITY':
       return typeof d.duration === 'number'
         ? (typeof d.name === 'string' ? d.name + ': ' : '') + formatDuration(d.duration) + (typeof d.intensity === 'string' ? ' (' + d.intensity + ')' : '')
