title: Add nginx security headers to gateway and kdiab-ui: CSP, X-Frame-Options, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options
description: config/gateway/nginx.conf and kdiab-ui/nginx.conf both lack Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, HSTS, and X-Content-Type-Options headers, exposing the application to clickjacking, MIME-sniffing, and protocol downgrade attacks.
design:
# OpenSpec: Add nginx security headers (kdiab-94g)

## Goal
Both nginx configs (config/gateway/nginx.conf and kdiab-ui/nginx.conf) lack security headers. Add X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, and Content-Security-Policy.

## Context
- config/gateway/nginx.conf (lines 1-47): Routes requests to four frontend services. No security headers.
- kdiab-ui/nginx.conf (lines 1-41): Serves the kdiab-ui SPA. No security headers.
- kdiab-ui/src/index.css line 1 imports fonts from https://fonts.googleapis.com — CSP must allow fonts.gstatic.com.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes.

## Implementation Plan
1. config/gateway/nginx.conf — Add inside the server {} block before the location blocks:
   add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
   add_header X-Frame-Options "DENY" always;
   add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;
   add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' http://localhost:* https://localhost:*; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self' data: https://fonts.gstatic.com; img-src 'self' data:;" always;
2. kdiab-ui/nginx.conf — Add the same four headers inside the server {} block.

## Test Plan
- [ ] docker compose up --build → curl -I http://localhost:8080/measures/ includes all four headers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Both nginx configs emit all four security headers with always.
- [ ] CSP allows Google Fonts.

## Risks & Assumptions
- style-src 'unsafe-inline' required for React inline styles.
- connect-src http://localhost:* is intentionally broad for local dev.
- HSTS on HTTP is harmless.

description: The alert banner in MeasureList shows 'below 70 or above 250 mg/dL' regardless of the user's glucoseUnit setting. mmol/L users (3.9 / 13.9 mmol/L equivalent) see incorrect numerical thresholds, which is a patient safety concern for hypo/hyper recognition.

The glucoseUnit prop is declared in MeasureListProps but never destructured or used. ## Context - kdiab-ui/src/features/measures/MeasureList.tsx: - Line 30: glucoseUnit?: string in props interface. - Lines 125-129: component destructures { userId, canArchive, canDelete } - glucoseUnit dropped. - Line 266: hardcoded string with mg/dL values. - Lines 37-42: getGlucoseZone(valueMgDl) uses 70/180/250 mg/dL thresholds - correct (always mg/dL). - Lines 44-46: toMgDl() correctly converts mmol/L to mg/dL before zone lookup (correct). - i18n en.json: no existing key for the banner text. - App.tsx: passes glucoseUnit to several components but NOT to MeasureList. ## Interface Changes No API changes - frontend i18n and unit display only. ## Implementation Plan 1. kdiab-ui/src/features/measures/MeasureList.tsx - Destructure glucoseUnit in the component: { userId, glucoseUnit = 'mg/dL', canArchive, canDelete }. - Replace line 266 hardcoded string with i18n call: {showAlert && (
{t('list.glucoseAlertBanner', { low: glucoseUnit === 'mmol/L' ? '3.9' : '70', high: glucoseUnit === 'mmol/L' ? '13.9' : '250', unit: glucoseUnit, })}
)} 2. kdiab-ui/src/i18n/locales/en.json - inside 'list' section add: 'glucoseAlertBanner': 'Some readings are outside safe range (below {{low}} or above {{high}} {{unit}})' 3. kdiab-ui/src/i18n/locales/de.json - inside 'list': 'glucoseAlertBanner': 'Einige Messwerte liegen außerhalb des sicheren Bereichs (unter {{low}} oder über {{high}} {{unit}})' 4. kdiab-ui/src/App.tsx - find where is rendered and pass glucoseUnit={glucoseUnit}. ## Test Plan - [ ] npm run build in kdiab-ui/ - TypeScript compiles clean - [ ] npm run lint - no lint errors - [ ] Manual: sarah (mg/dL) - alert shows 'below 70 or above 250 mg/dL' - [ ] Manual: mike (mmol/L) - alert shows 'below 3.9 or above 13.9 mmol/L' ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Banner text uses i18n translation key - [ ] Banner shows correct numeric thresholds for the user's glucoseUnit - [ ] TypeScript compiles clean; lint passes ## Risks & Assumptions - mmol/L thresholds: 70/18.018 = 3.9; 250/18.018 = 13.9. - Check App.tsx for where MeasureList is rendered to confirm glucoseUnit is available.

## Goal

title: SSO across all kdiab frontends: silent re-auth via shared Keycloak session
description:
When a user is already logged into one kdiab frontend (e.g. kdiab-measures) and navigates to another (e.g. kdiab-analyze), they are prompted to log in again. The existing Keycloak session should be reused silently — the user should land directly in the new service without a login screen.

## Background

All four frontends are OIDC public clients in the same Keycloak realm (`kdiab`). Keycloak maintains a realm-level SSO session cookie (`KEYCLOAK_SESSION`) in the browser after the first login. Any subsequent authorization request from a different client in the same realm can use `prompt=none` to silently exchange the session cookie for a new token without user interaction.

`react-oidc-context` (used by all four frontends) wraps `oidc-client-ts`, which supports silent renew and silent sign-in via a hidden iframe or redirect. The library exposes `signinSilent()` for this purpose.

## Goal

Each frontend should attempt a silent sign-in on startup before showing a login button. If the user already has an active Keycloak session from any other kdiab client, they are authenticated immediately. Only if silent sign-in fails (no existing session, expired session) should the explicit login screen be shown.

## Implementation hints

`react-oidc-context` `AuthProvider` accepts an `onSigninCallback` and supports automatic silent sign-in. The key config additions per frontend:

```tsx
<AuthProvider
  ...
  automaticSilentRenew={true}
  silentRequestTimeoutInSeconds={5}
>
```

On startup, after `useAuth` returns `!auth.isAuthenticated && !auth.isLoading`, call `auth.signinSilent()` before falling back to `auth.signinRedirect()`. This requires a `silent_redirect_uri` pointing to a minimal HTML page that calls `oidc-client-ts`' `signinSilentCallback()`.

Each frontend needs:
1. `public/silent-renew.html` — silent callback page (standard oidc-client-ts boilerplate)
2. `VITE_OIDC_SILENT_REDIRECT_URI` env var (or hardcoded `/silent-renew.html` relative path)
3. `silentRequestTimeoutInSeconds` added to `AuthProvider`
4. Startup logic: try `signinSilent()` first, redirect to login only on failure

## Acceptance criteria

title: Add kdiab-nightscout service: Nightscout-compatible API adapter
description: Create a new kdiab-nightscout service (stateless, like BFF) that exposes a Nightscout-compatible REST API (POST /api/v1/entries, POST /api/v1/treatments, GET equivalents) and maps incoming Nightscout-formatted data (sgv/mbg/trend Nightscout field names, Nightscout treatment types) to kdiab's canonical value/unit schema before forwarding to kdiab-measures and kdiab-treatments via their HTTP APIs. This allows Nightscout-compatible CGM devices, pumps, and apps (Loop, AndroidAPS, xDrip+) to push data directly into the kdiab platform without any client-side transformation.

title: Fix token XSS exposure in kdiab-bff tokenProvider.ts
description: kdiab-bff/frontend/src/api/tokenProvider.ts stores the access token in a module-level variable accessible to any code in the JS bundle. If any dependency or injected script runs, it can read the token. Scope the token variable to request callbacks only, or use a secure closure pattern.

title: Add missing security headers to BFF, treatments, measures nginx.conf
description: Only kdiab-profiles nginx.conf has full security headers. The BFF, treatments, and measures frontends are missing X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, X-XSS-Protection, Referrer-Policy, and Content-Security-Policy headers. These are required for WCAG and general web security hygiene.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 2f9f7bd. All four backend quality gates pass.

title: Add empty roles validation to JWT Security.kt in all services
description: Security.kt in all four services extracts roles from the JWT but does not validate that at least one valid role (PATIENT, DOCTOR, ADMIN) is present. A token with no roles passes authentication. Add a check that rejects tokens with empty or unrecognised role sets.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 2f9f7bd. All four backend quality gates pass.

title: Fix Keycloak webOrigins wildcard — whitelist specific origins
description: keycloak-realm.json has webOrigins: ['*'] for public clients, allowing any origin. This allows CORS attacks if Keycloak is exposed. Should be replaced with explicit origin list (e.g. http://localhost:3000, http://localhost:3001, http://localhost:3002, http://localhost:3003).
close_reason: Implemented and committed

title: Remove hardcoded JDBC URL defaults from application.conf
description: kdiab-profiles and kdiab-treatments application.conf files have hardcoded fallback JDBC URLs (jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/...) that would silently connect to a local DB if DATABASE_URL env var is not set. Production deployments could accidentally use the wrong DB. Remove defaults and require the env var explicitly.

title: Enforce PKCE for all public OIDC clients in Keycloak
description: Public OIDC clients (measures-frontend, profiles-frontend, treatments-frontend, bff-frontend) in keycloak-realm.json should have pkceCodeChallengeMethod set to S256. Without PKCE, authorization code interception attacks are possible.
close_reason: Implemented and committed

title: Fix unsafe Record<string,unknown> access in MeasureList and TreatmentList
description: MeasureList.tsx casts measure.data as Record<string,unknown> then accesses d.trend, d.value, d.sgv without type guards. TreatmentList.tsx does the same for d.insulin, d.duration, d.carbs. If a field is missing or has an unexpected type, the code may display undefined or cause a runtime error. Fix: add explicit type guards before each field access (typeof d.trend === 'string'), use optional chaining and nullish coalescing throughout, and consider defining typed payload interfaces per measure/treatment type.

title: Fix Profile status string type in generated API client and remove as-string casts
description: The generated API client types Profile.status as string instead of a string literal union type 'ACTIVE' | 'DRAFT' | 'PROPOSED' | 'ARCHIVED'. This forces developers to write unsafe casts: (p.status as string || '') === 'PROPOSED'. This pattern appears 5+ times in ProfileList.tsx and ProfileHistory.tsx. Fix: update the OpenAPI spec to define ProfileStatus as an enum (not a plain string), regenerate the TypeScript client, and remove all as-string casts to use type-safe comparisons directly.

title: Add status column to kdiab-treatments table and domain model

design:
# OpenSpec: Add status column to kdiab-treatments table and domain model (kdiab-yd5)

## Goal
kdiab-treatments has no status field — deletions are hard deletes. Adding ACTIVE/ARCHIVED status (mirroring kdiab-measures) enables soft-delete via archive, preserves history, and unblocks doctor audit trails.

## Context
- `kdiab-treatments/src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/001-ddl.yaml`: treatments table has no status column (last changeset id is 004 — audit_logs table).
- `domain/model/Treatment.kt`: data class has no status field; no TreatmentStatus enum.
- `infrastructure/persistence/ExposedTreatmentRepository.kt`: TreatmentsTable has no status column; findByUserId has no status filter.
- `application/service/TreatmentService.kt`: no archive method.
- `adapters/inbound/web/TreatmentRoutes.kt`: only delete endpoint (hard-delete POST body with IDs); no archive endpoint.
- `api/openapi.yaml`: TreatmentResponse has no status field; list endpoint has no status query param.
- Reference pattern: kdiab-measures MeasureStatus enum, MeasuresTable.status = varchar("status", 50).default("ACTIVE"), archiveAll(ids, userId), and status filter in findByUserId.

## Interface Changes
- api/openapi.yaml: Add status: string (ACTIVE | ARCHIVED) to TreatmentResponse. Add optional status query param to GET /users/{userId}/treatments (default ACTIVE). Add POST /users/{userId}/treatments/archive endpoint (same body shape as delete).
- Domain: new TreatmentStatus enum (ACTIVE, ARCHIVED). Treatment data class gains status: TreatmentStatus = TreatmentStatus.ACTIVE.
- DB: new status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'ACTIVE' column; new idx_treatments_status index.

## Implementation Plan
1. `kdiab-treatments/src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/001-ddl.yaml` — Add changeset id=005 adding status column with defaultValue=ACTIVE and idx_treatments_status index.
2. `kdiab-treatments/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/treatments/domain/model/Treatment.kt` — Add enum class TreatmentStatus { ACTIVE, ARCHIVED }. Add status: TreatmentStatus = TreatmentStatus.ACTIVE to Treatment data class.
3. `kdiab-treatments/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/treatments/domain/repository/TreatmentRepository.kt` — Add status: TreatmentStatus = TreatmentStatus.ACTIVE param to findByUserId. Add suspend fun archiveAll(ids: List<Uuid>, userId: Uuid): Unit.
4. `kdiab-treatments/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/treatments/infrastructure/persistence/ExposedTreatmentRepository.kt` — Add status = varchar("status", 50).default("ACTIVE") to TreatmentsTable. Add status filter to findByUserId. Add archiveAll updating status to ARCHIVED.
5. `kdiab-treatments/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/treatments/application/service/TreatmentService.kt` — Add archiveTreatments(ids, userId). Thread status param through getTreatments.
6. `kdiab-treatments/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/treatments/adapters/inbound/web/TreatmentMapper.kt` — Add status = domain.status.name to toApi().
7. `kdiab-treatments/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/treatments/adapters/inbound/web/TreatmentRoutes.kt` — Extract optional status query param (default ACTIVE). Add POST /users/{userId}/treatments/archive route with same access control as delete.
8. `kdiab-treatments/api/openapi.yaml` — Add status to TreatmentResponse. Add status query param to GET list. Add POST /users/{userId}/treatments/archive operation.

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit: archiveTreatments updates status; findByUserId(status=ACTIVE) excludes ARCHIVED.
- [ ] Integration: POST archive sets row status=ARCHIVED; GET list excludes archived row.
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check from kdiab-treatments/.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Liquibase changeset id=005 adds status column with default ACTIVE.
- [ ] GET /treatments returns only ACTIVE by default.
- [ ] POST /treatments/archive sets status to ARCHIVED.
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check passes.

## Risks & Assumptions
- Changeset id=005 is next after id=004. Confirmed by reading 001-ddl.yaml.
- H2 integration tests work because the status column has a DEFAULT value.
- Hard-delete endpoint remains unchanged.
close_reason: ACTIVE/ARCHIVED status column added to treatments; archive endpoint added; quality gate passed (45 tests)

title: Replace alert() with inline form validation errors in all modals

This is especially jarring on mobile. Fix: remove all alert() calls from form submission handlers. Display validation errors inline: below each field using react-hook-form fieldState.error, and a summary error banner at the top of the form (role='alert') listing all validation failures. Applies to AddMeasureModal, AddTreatmentModal, and any other forms using alert().

title: Fix TIR threshold labels: show mmol/L values when user unit preference is mmol/L
description: TimeInRangeBar.tsx displays zone labels using hardcoded mg/dL thresholds (< 70, 70-180, 180-250, > 250) even when the user's glucose_unit JWT claim is mmol/L. A mmol/L user sees 'Below (< 70)' but their readings are in mmol/L, so the number '70' is meaningless and confusing. Fix: read glucoseUnit from the user context and convert displayed thresholds: 70 mg/dL → 3.9 mmol/L, 180 → 10.0, 250 → 13.9. Pass glucoseUnit as a prop to TimeInRangeBar and convert all threshold labels accordingly.

title: Add prominent patient-viewing banner for doctors in BFF and measures frontends

A doctor could forget they are viewing patient Sarah's timeline instead of their own. The banner must remain visible while scrolling.

title: Replace window.confirm() with custom confirmation modals for destructive actions
description: Multiple list components use window.confirm() for archive/delete confirmation (MeasureList, TreatmentList). close_reason: Implemented in kdiab-ui SPA (commit ad79378)

title: Fix WCAG 2.1 AA colour-only violations: TIR bar patterns and timeline treatment shapes
description: Two components fail WCAG 2.1 AA Success Criterion 1.4.1 (colour not sole means of conveying information): (1) TimeInRangeBar.tsx uses only CSS colour variables to differentiate 4 TIR zones with no pattern, texture, or text label directly on each bar segment; (2) TimelineChart.tsx renders all treatments as identical scatter points with only colour distinguishing bolus/carbs/corrections. title: Add full modal accessibility: role=dialog aria-modal Escape key and focus trap

This violates WCAG 2.1 AA Success Criterion 2.1.2 (no keyboard trap). design:
# OpenSpec: Add edit endpoint for measures and treatments (kdiab-bfl)

## Goal
Patients currently must delete and recreate entries to fix typos. Add PUT endpoints to kdiab-measures and kdiab-treatments allowing update of the data payload and timestamp (type and userId are immutable). Add an Edit button in MeasureList and TreatmentList that opens the existing Add modal pre-filled.

## Context
- kdiab-measures/.../adapters/inbound/web/MeasureRoutes.kt — no PUT route; access control via checkReadAccess
- kdiab-measures/.../application/service/MeasureService.kt — no updateMeasure method
- kdiab-measures/.../domain/repository/MeasureRepository.kt — no update method
- kdiab-measures/.../infrastructure/persistence/ExposedMeasureRepository.kt — archive uses MeasuresTable.update({ id eq x and userId eq y }) { ... } — same pattern for update
- kdiab-ui/src/features/measures/AddMeasureModal.tsx — create-only; no initialValue prop
- kdiab-ui/src/api/measuresApi.ts — no updateMeasure method
- Same gap in treatments stack

## Interface Changes
- kdiab-measures/api/openapi.yaml: Add PUT /users/{userId}/measures/{measureId} with UpdateMeasureRequest { measuredAt: string, data: object }. Response is MeasureResponse.
- kdiab-treatments/api/openapi.yaml: Add PUT /users/{userId}/treatments/{treatmentId} with UpdateTreatmentRequest { treatedAt: string, data: object, notes: string? }. Response is TreatmentResponse.
- No DB schema changes.

### kdiab-measures backend

# OpenSpec: Extend BffE2ETest with AGP, 403, and upstream-error scenarios (kdiab-upw)

## Goal
`kdiab-analyze/src/e2e-test/…/BffE2ETest.kt` already tests the happy-path timeline, HbA1c, profiles-list, and 401 flows. Add four missing scenarios: AGP hourly-bucket verification, PATIENT 403 on another user's data, DOCTOR 403 on non-assigned patient, and upstream failure returning 200 with `errors` list (depends on kdiab-4c7 supervisorScope).

## Context

**Current state:**
- `BffE2ETest.kt` exists with `given("a patient with CGM, BOLUS, and profile data")` block containing when-timeline, when-hba1c, when-profiles, when-401 tests.
- AGP endpoint: `GET /api/v1/users/{userId}/analytics/agp?from=…&to=…` returns `AgpResponse` with `hourlyBuckets: List<AgpBucket>` (24 entries, one per UTC hour).
- JWT helper already present — reuse for PATIENT (sarah), DOCTOR (dr_house with allowedPatients=[sarah]), and DOCTOR without sarah.
- `supervisorScope` from kdiab-4c7 must land first for the upstream-error test.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes — tests only.

## Implementation Plan

Add inside the existing `given` block in `BffE2ETest.kt`:

1. AGP test: mock measures returns 10 CGM at hour 10 UTC; GET /analytics/agp; assert 24 buckets, bucket[10].count==10, bucket[10].p50!=null, bucket[0].count==0.

2. PATIENT 403: use sarah's token but request mike's userId in path; assert status==403.

3. DOCTOR 403: use dr_cameron's token (not assigned to sarah), request sarah's data; assert status==403.

4. Upstream error → 200 + errors: MockEngine measures path → 500; GET /timeline; assert status==200, body.measures.isEmpty(), body.errors.isNotEmpty().

- [ ] `./gradlew :check --no-daemon` — full quality gate green

- [ ] PATIENT 403 on another user's data
- [ ] DOCTOR 403 on non-assigned patient's data
- [ ] Upstream error: 200 with `errors` non-empty (requires kdiab-4c7 complete)

# OpenSpec: BFF integration tests with mock upstream Ktor servers (kdiab-yly)

## Goal
kdiab-analyze/src/integration-test/ and src/e2e-test/ are empty. Add integration tests exercising the BFF HTTP layer with MockEngine-backed HTTP clients (testing real MeasuresClient/TreatmentsClient/ProfilesClient JSON parsing), and BehaviorSpec-style e2e tests for full user journeys.

IMPORTANT: kdiab-4c7 (supervisorScope) must be implemented first — the partial-failure tests depend on it.

## Context

Test infrastructure already in place:
- build.gradle.kts — integrationTest and e2eTest suites configured; check depends on both; e2eTest has kotest dependencies.
- Application.module(timelineService?, analyticsService?, profilesService?) — accepts pre-built services for test injection.
- JWT pattern: HMAC256 with jwt.test=true — same as existing BffRoutesTest.kt.
- Existing BffRoutesTest.kt tests status codes only; integration tests add response body verification.

MockEngine approach (pseudo-code):
  val mockEngine = MockEngine { req ->
    when {
      req.url.encodedPath.contains("measures") -> respond(measuresJson, HttpStatusCode.OK, headersOf("Content-Type", "application/json"))
      req.url.encodedPath.contains("treatments") -> respond(treatmentsJson, HttpStatusCode.OK, headersOf("Content-Type", "application/json"))
      else -> respond("[]", HttpStatusCode.OK)
    }
  }
  val httpClient = HttpClient(mockEngine) { install(ContentNegotiation) { json() } }
  val measuresClient = MeasuresClient(httpClient, "http://mock-measures")
  val treatmentsClient = TreatmentsClient(httpClient, "http://mock-treatments")
  val timelineService = TimelineService(measuresClient, treatmentsClient)
Then: testApplication { application { module(timelineService = timelineService, ...) } }

Check if ktor-client-mock is already in libs.versions.toml. If not, add testImplementation(libs.ktor.client.mock) to both integrationTest and e2eTest dependencies in build.gradle.kts.

No interface changes — tests only.

1. kdiab-analyze/src/integration-test/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/adapters/inbound/web/BffTimelineIntegrationTest.kt (new)

   - Mock returns one CGM measure at 2024-01-15T10:00:00Z (within [2024-01-01, 2024-01-31]) and one at 2023-12-31T10:00:00Z (outside range).
   - Tests:
     a) Response body contains exactly one measure (the in-range one) — deserialize via Json.decodeFromString<TimelineResponse>
     b) Response treatments list contains expected treatment
     c) When measures MockEngine returns 500: response status 200, measures empty, errors contains "measures:"
     d) When treatments MockEngine returns 500: treatments empty, errors populated

2. kdiab-analyze/src/integration-test/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/adapters/inbound/web/BffAnalyticsIntegrationTest.kt (new)
   - Build AnalyticsService with MockEngine-backed MeasuresClient returning 10 CGM readings at 120.0 mg/dL, all at 2024-01-15T10:xx:00Z (hour 10 UTC).
   - Tests:
     a) GET /hba1c: readingCount=10, hba1c approx 5.82 (120+46.7)/28.7, tir.inRangeCount=10
     b) GET /hba1c with empty measures: readingCount=0, hba1c null

     when GET /analytics/hba1c: hba1c computed correctly

title: Handle partial upstream failure in BFF TimelineService with supervisorScope
description: TimelineService uses coroutineScope { async { measuresClient } async { treatmentsClient } }. If either upstream throws UpstreamException, the entire timeline request fails even if the other service succeeded. Fix: switch to supervisorScope and wrap each async in runCatching; return a degraded Timeline with the available data and an errors list indicating which service failed. Update the OpenAPI response schema to include an optional errors field.
design:
# OpenSpec: Partial upstream failure in TimelineService with supervisorScope (kdiab-4c7)

## Goal
TimelineService.getTimeline() uses coroutineScope { async {} } for parallel upstream calls. If either the measures or treatments service fails with UpstreamException, the whole timeline request returns 502. Switch to supervisorScope so a single upstream failure returns the available data plus an errors list indicating which service(s) failed.

## Context

Current state:
- kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/application/service/TimelineService.kt line 22: = coroutineScope { — a single child failure cancels all siblings.
- kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/domain/model/Timeline.kt — Timeline(measures, treatments), no errors field.
- kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/adapters/inbound/web/BffMapper.kt — TimelineResponse has measures and treatments only; Timeline.toResponse() maps both lists.
- kdiab-analyze/api/openapi.yaml — TimelineResponse schema has required: [measures, treatments] with no errors field.
- StatusPages.kt maps UpstreamException to 502. After this fix, timeline will never throw UpstreamException — it always returns 200 with partial data.

## Interface Changes
kdiab-analyze/api/openapi.yaml — add optional errors array to TimelineResponse:
    TimelineResponse:
      type: object
      required: [measures, treatments]
      properties:
        measures:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/TimelineMeasure'
        treatments:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/TimelineTreatment'
        errors:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
          description: Non-empty when one or more upstream services were unavailable.

## Implementation Plan

1. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/domain/model/Timeline.kt — Add val errors: List<String> = emptyList() to the Timeline data class.

2. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/application/service/TimelineService.kt — Replace coroutineScope with supervisorScope; wrap each async result in runCatching. Build errors list from failures, pass to Timeline constructor.

3. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/adapters/inbound/web/BffMapper.kt — Add val errors: List<String> = emptyList() to TimelineResponse, include in Timeline.toResponse().

4. kdiab-analyze/api/openapi.yaml — Update TimelineResponse schema as shown above.

5. kdiab-analyze/src/test/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/application/service/TimelineServiceTest.kt — Add three tests: both fail, measures fails, treatments fails.

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit: TimelineServiceTest — existing tests still pass; new partial-failure tests pass
- [ ] ./gradlew :check --no-daemon from kdiab-analyze/ — all checks green

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Both upstreams succeed: response unchanged, errors empty
- [ ] Measures fails: 200 with treatments data and errors containing measures entry
- [ ] Treatments fails: 200 with measures data and errors containing treatments entry
- [ ] ./gradlew :check passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- supervisorScope does not propagate child failures — safe to use here.
- Forward-compatible: empty errors list means no degradation.
close_reason: Implemented: supervisorScope + errors field in Timeline and TimelineResponse

title: Add safeguard against unbounded memory in MeasuresClient pagination loop
description: MeasuresClient.getMeasures() loops while result.size < totalCount, accumulating all pages in memory. For a user with years of CGM data (e.g. 5 years * 288 readings/day = ~525k measures), this causes OOM. Fix: add a hard cap (e.g. check(totalCount <= 50_000) { 'Too many measures: ' }) or change the BFF to accept from/to date parameters and pass them through to the upstream service to limit the result set before pagination.

title: Forward X-Correlation-ID from BFF to all upstream service calls
description: The BFF correctly generates/extracts X-Correlation-ID from inbound requests (Logging.kt CallId plugin) and binds it to MDC. But MeasuresClient, ProfilesClient, and TreatmentsClient do not forward it in outbound HTTP calls. Distributed tracing is broken: a single user request cannot be linked across BFF + measures + profiles + treatments logs. Fix: pass correlationId parameter to all client methods and add it as a header on every httpClient.get() call.
design:
# OpenSpec: Forward X-Correlation-ID from BFF to upstream services (kdiab-nf3)

## Goal
The BFF extracts `X-Correlation-ID` from every inbound request (via Ktor's `CallId` plugin) and
binds it to SLF4J MDC for local logging — but never forwards it to `MeasuresClient`,
`ProfilesClient`, or `TreatmentsClient`. Distributed tracing is broken: a single user request
cannot be correlated across BFF + measures + profiles + treatments logs. This spec threads the
correlation ID through every layer using the same pattern already used for the `authorization`
header.

## Context

### How authorization is currently forwarded (pattern to replicate)
- `BffRoutes.kt` extracts `Authorization` header into `RequestContext.authorization: String`
- Route handlers pass `authorization` to service methods
- Service methods pass it to client methods
- Client methods set `header(HttpHeaders.Authorization, authorization)` on every HTTP request

### Correlation ID availability
- `Logging.kt` installs `CallId { header("X-Correlation-ID"); generate { UUID.randomUUID() } }`
- Downstream: `call.callId: String?` — always non-null after `generate {}` is configured
- Null-safety: use `call.callId ?: ""` as a safe default (generate always fires in practice)

### Files that need changing

**Inbound:**
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/adapters/inbound/web/BffRoutes.kt`

**Application services:**
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/application/service/TimelineService.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/application/service/AnalyticsService.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/application/service/ProfilesService.kt`

**Outbound HTTP clients:**
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/adapters/outbound/http/MeasuresClient.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/adapters/outbound/http/ProfilesClient.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/adapters/outbound/http/TreatmentsClient.kt`

**Tests:**
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../service/TimelineServiceTest.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../service/AnalyticsServiceTest.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../http/MeasuresClientTest.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../http/ProfilesClientTest.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../http/TreatmentsClientTest.kt`

## Interface Changes
No OpenAPI contract changes — `X-Correlation-ID` is a transparent infrastructure header, not part
of the application API.

Function signatures change (internal only):
- `getMeasures(userId, authorization)` → `getMeasures(userId, authorization, correlationId)`
- `getProfiles(userId, authorization)` → `getProfiles(userId, authorization, correlationId)`
- `getTreatments(userId, authorization)` → `getTreatments(userId, authorization, correlationId)`
- Same threading through all service methods.

## Implementation Plan

**Step 1** — `BffRoutes.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `RequestContext`; extract via
`call.callId ?: ""` in `extractContext()`; pass to all six service-method call sites:
`timelineService.getTimeline(...)`, `analyticsService.getHba1c(...)`, `analyticsService.getAgp(...)`,
`profilesService.getProfiles(...)`.

**Step 2** — `TimelineService.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getTimeline(...)` signature;
forward to `measuresClient.getMeasures(...)` and `treatmentsClient.getTreatments(...)`.

**Step 3** — `AnalyticsService.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getHba1c(...)`, `getAgp(...)`,
and the private `fetchCgmReadings(...)` helper; forward to `measuresClient.getMeasures(...)`.

**Step 4** — `ProfilesService.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getProfiles(...)`; forward to
`profilesClient.getProfiles(...)`.

**Step 5** — `MeasuresClient.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getMeasures(...)`; add
`header("X-Correlation-ID", correlationId)` to every `httpClient.get()` call (both the loop
iterations in the paginated implementation).

**Step 6** — `ProfilesClient.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getProfiles(...)`; add
`header("X-Correlation-ID", correlationId)` to the `httpClient.get()` call.

**Step 7** — `TreatmentsClient.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getTreatments(...)`; add
`header("X-Correlation-ID", correlationId)` to the `httpClient.get()` call.

**Step 8** — `MeasuresClientTest.kt`: Add `correlationId = "test-cid"` to all `getMeasures()`
calls; add a test `getMeasures sends X-Correlation-ID header` that captures request headers with
`MockEngine` and asserts `"X-Correlation-ID" == "test-cid"`.

**Step 9** — `ProfilesClientTest.kt`: Same as Step 8 for `getProfiles`.

**Step 10** — `TreatmentsClientTest.kt`: Same as Step 8 for `getTreatments`.

**Step 11** — `AnalyticsServiceTest.kt`: Add `correlationId = ""` to all service-method calls.

**Step 12** — `TimelineServiceTest.kt`: Add `correlationId = ""` to all service-method calls.

(Check for `ProfilesServiceTest.kt` — add `correlationId = ""` if it exists.)

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit: new header-forwarding test in each of the three client test files verifies that
  `X-Correlation-ID` with the supplied value is sent on every upstream request
- [ ] Unit: existing AnalyticsServiceTest and TimelineServiceTest compile and pass with updated signatures
- [ ] Quality gate: `cd kdiab-bff && ./gradlew :backend:check` — all tests green, Detekt clean, Kover ≥ 80%

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every outbound HTTP call from BFF to kdiab-measures, kdiab-profiles, kdiab-treatments carries
  `X-Correlation-ID` header equal to the value extracted from the inbound request (or a
  generated UUID when the client did not supply one)
- [ ] New unit tests in MeasuresClientTest, ProfilesClientTest, TreatmentsClientTest confirm the
  header is present and correctly valued
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check` passes with no regressions

## Risks & Assumptions
- `call.callId` is always non-null after `generate {}` is configured — using `?: ""` as a
  defensive fallback only; in practice the empty string path will never be taken.
- No changes needed to upstream services (measures, profiles, treatments) — they already accept
  `X-Correlation-ID` via their own `Logging.kt` CallId plugin configuration.
- No OpenAPI schema changes, no frontend changes, no DB changes.

title: Add HTTP connect/request/socket timeouts to BFF HttpClient
description: BFF Application.kt instantiates an HttpClient with CIO engine but no timeout configuration. If any upstream service hangs, the BFF request blocks indefinitely, exhausting the Ktor dispatcher thread pool and cascading failure to all concurrent requests. Fix: install HttpTimeout plugin with connectTimeoutMillis=5000, requestTimeoutMillis=10000, socketTimeoutMillis=5000 in the HttpClient block in Application.kt.
close_reason: Implemented per spec

title: Add audit logging for doctor access to patient data
description: There is no audit trail when a doctor reads or writes patient data (views timeline, proposes profile, views analytics). This is required for HIPAA/GDPR compliance. Every doctor read/write must log: timestamp, doctorId, patientId, action (viewed-timeline, proposed-profile, viewed-analytics), and IP/user-agent. Store in an immutable audit table. Expose read-only audit log endpoint for admins. Affects all four backend services.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add SerializationException and JsonConvertException handlers to all StatusPages
description: When call.receive<T>() is called on malformed JSON, Ktor throws SerializationException or JsonConvertException. None of the four services' StatusPages plugins catch these. They propagate as unhandled exceptions and return a non-JSON 500 instead of a structured 400 ErrorResponse. Fix: add exception<SerializationException> and exception<JsonConvertException> handlers to all four StatusPages.kt files returning HttpStatusCode.BadRequest with ErrorResponse.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 2f9f7bd. All four backend quality gates pass.

design:
# OpenSpec: Add integration and e2e tests for kdiab-measures backend (kdiab-bim)

## Goal
kdiab-measures has comprehensive unit tests but zero integration or e2e tests. The integrationTest and e2eTest source sets are registered in Gradle but empty. Add LiquibaseTestHelper, ExposedMeasureRepositoryTest, and MeasureE2ETest following kdiab-profiles patterns, covering all repository methods and the full CRUD + auth lifecycle via Ktor test application.

## Context
- kdiab-measures/src/integration-test/kotlin/ — directory exists, no files
- kdiab-measures/src/e2e-test/kotlin/ — directory exists, no files
- build.gradle.kts: both suites configured; e2eTest has kotest.runner.junit5, kotest.assertions.core, ktor.client.content.negotiation, ktor.server.test.host
- ExposedMeasureRepository and AuditLogsTable are already excluded from Kover
- Application.module(measureService?, auditLogRepository?, initDatabase?) accepts injected dependencies
- Liquibase: db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml includes changes/001-ddl.yaml; changeset 003 is PostgreSQL-only (skipped by H2); no seed data
- Reference: kdiab-profiles/src/integration-test/kotlin/.../LiquibaseTestHelper.kt and ExposedInsulinRepositoryTest.kt
- Measure domain: id, userId, measuredAt, createdAt, type (MeasureType), source (MeasureSource), data (JsonObject), status (MeasureStatus, default ACTIVE)
- Repository methods: save, findByUserId(userId, page, size, from?, to?), countByUserId, findByUserIdAndType, archive(ids, userId), deleteAll(ids, userId)

## Interface Changes
No interface changes — tests only.

## Implementation Plan

1. kdiab-measures/src/integration-test/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/measures/infrastructure/persistence/LiquibaseTestHelper.kt (new)
   - setup(dbName: String): Database — H2 in-memory with MODE=PostgreSQL;DATABASE_TO_LOWER=TRUE;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1, runs Liquibase from db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml
   - cleanData(db: Database) — DELETE FROM audit_logs; DELETE FROM measures (order matters for FK if any)

2. kdiab-measures/src/integration-test/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/measures/infrastructure/persistence/ExposedMeasureRepositoryTest.kt (new)
   JUnit5, runBlocking, @BeforeTest calls cleanData. Tests:
   - save — inserts and returns CGM measure with all fields matching input
   - findByUserId — 2 for userA, 1 for userB; findByUserId(userA, page=0, size=10) returns exactly 2
   - findByUserId pagination — save 5; page 0 size 3 returns 3; page 1 size 3 returns 2
   - findByUserId from/to filter — save at T-2d, T-1d, T+1d; from=T-1.5d to=T+0.5d returns exactly the T-1d one
   - findByUserIdAndType — CGM + BGM for same user; findByUserIdAndType(CGM) returns 1
   - archive — save measure, archive it; verify status becomes ARCHIVED
   - deleteAll — save 2, deleteAll(ids=[id1], userId); findByUserId returns 1

3. kdiab-measures/src/e2e-test/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/measures/adapters/inbound/web/e2e/MeasureE2ETest.kt (new)
   Kotest BehaviorSpec, full Ktor + H2:
   given("a running Measures Service") {
     when("a patient manages their CGM measures") {
       then("they can create, list (type/date filter), archive, delete") {
         testApplication {
           environment { config = MapApplicationConfig(
             "jwt.domain" to ISSUER, "jwt.audience" to "measure", "jwt.realm" to "kdiab-measures",
             "jwt.secret" to JWT_SECRET, "jwt.test" to "true",
             "storage.driverClassName" to "org.h2.Driver",
             "storage.jdbcUrl" to "jdbc:h2:mem:e2e_measures;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1;MODE=PostgreSQL;DATABASE_TO_LOWER=TRUE",
             "storage.username" to "root", "storage.password" to "password",
             "storage.maximumPoolSize" to "3", "storage.isAutoCommit" to "false",
             "storage.transactionIsolation" to "TRANSACTION_REPEATABLE_READ"
           ) }
           application { module() }
           // 1. List -> empty; 2. POST create CGM -> 201; 3. List -> 1 item
           // 4. List ?type=BGM -> 0 items; 5. Archive -> 200; 6. List -> 0; 7. DELETE -> 200
         }
       }
     }
     when("a patient tries to access another user's measures") {
       then("they receive 403") { /* sarah token -> mike's userId -> 403 */ }
     }
     when("a request has no auth token") {
       then("they receive 401") { }
     }
   }

## Test Plan
- [ ] ./gradlew :integrationTest --no-daemon from kdiab-measures/ — all repository tests pass
- [ ] ./gradlew :e2eTest --no-daemon — e2e tests pass
- [ ] ./gradlew :check --no-daemon — Kover >= 80%, Detekt clean, all tests green

## Acceptance Criteria

# OpenSpec: Integration and e2e tests for kdiab-treatments backend (kdiab-no1)

## Goal
kdiab-treatments has comprehensive unit tests but zero integration or e2e tests. Add ExposedTreatmentRepositoryTest (real H2 + Liquibase) and TreatmentE2ETest (full Ktor app + H2, BehaviorSpec) to exercise the complete CRUD lifecycle and role-based access controls, following the kdiab-profiles test patterns exactly.

## Context

Current test coverage:
- src/test/kotlin/ — routes (auth/RBAC matrix), service, mapper, domain, ApplicationTest.
- src/integration-test/kotlin/ — empty (directories exist, no files).
- src/e2e-test/kotlin/ — empty.
- build.gradle.kts — both suites configured; check depends on both; e2eTest depends on Kotest. integrationTest extends implementation and testImplementation configurations. ExposedTreatmentRepository is excluded from Kover — integration tests provide its coverage.

DB schema (single table, no FK children):
  treatments(id UUID PK, user_id UUID, treated_at TIMESTAMPTZ, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ, type VARCHAR(50), data JSONB, notes TEXT)
Liquibase root: db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml (changesets 001-003). Changeset 003 is PostgreSQL-only (index) — H2 skips it safely. No seed data — cleanData() is simply DELETE FROM treatments.

Application.module(treatmentService?, initDatabase?) signature:
- initDatabase=true (default) reads storage.* config — supply H2 JDBC URL in e2e test config.

Reference: kdiab-profiles LiquibaseTestHelper pattern — H2 in-memory with MODE=PostgreSQL;DATABASE_TO_LOWER=TRUE, unique dbName per test class, targeted DELETE statements for cleanup.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes — tests only.

## Implementation Plan

1. kdiab-treatments/src/integration-test/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/treatments/infrastructure/persistence/LiquibaseTestHelper.kt (new)
   Adapt from kdiab-profiles LiquibaseTestHelper:
   - Changelog path: "db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml"
   - cleanData(db): exec("DELETE FROM treatments") only
   - Same setup(dbName) pattern: H2 in-memory with MODE=PostgreSQL;DATABASE_TO_LOWER=TRUE
   - Use USER="root", PASSWORD=""

2. kdiab-treatments/src/integration-test/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/treatments/infrastructure/persistence/ExposedTreatmentRepositoryTest.kt (new)
   JUnit5 tests with @BeforeTest setup. All tests use runBlocking.
   lateinit var db: Database, lateinit var repository: ExposedTreatmentRepository
   @BeforeTest: db = LiquibaseTestHelper.setup("treatments_repo"); LiquibaseTestHelper.cleanData(db); repository = ExposedTreatmentRepository()
   
   Tests (use transaction(db) to bind Exposed to test DB):
   - save: insert BOLUS with known id+userId, verify returned Treatment equals input
   - findByUserId: save two for userA, one for userB; findByUserId(userA) returns exactly two ordered by treatedAt DESC
   - findByUserIdAndType: save BOLUS + CARBS for same user; findByUserIdAndType(BOLUS) returns one; findByUserIdAndType(CARBS) returns one
   - deleteAll matching userId: save two, delete one by id for correct userId; findByUserId returns one
   - deleteAll wrong userId: delete with wrong userId; findByUserId returns original count (no rows deleted)
   
   NOTE: ExposedTreatmentRepository uses suspendTransaction which uses thread-local DB binding.
   To bind to the test DB, set the Exposed Database.connect() before creating the repository,
   or pass the db as a parameter. Look at how kdiab-profiles does it in ExposedInsulinRepositoryTest.

3. kdiab-treatments/src/e2e-test/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/treatments/adapters/inbound/web/e2e/TreatmentE2ETest.kt (new)
   Kotest BehaviorSpec, full Ktor app + H2:
   Constants: ISSUER="http://localhost:8081/realms/kdiab-treatments", AUDIENCE="treatment", JWT_SECRET="test-secret-for-e2e-tests", SARAH_ID="11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", MIKE_ID="22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222"
   
   fun generateToken(userId: String, roles: List<String>, allowedPatients: List<String> = emptyList()): String
   
   val e2eConfig = MapApplicationConfig(
     "jwt.domain" to ISSUER,
     "jwt.audience" to AUDIENCE,
     "jwt.realm" to "kdiab-treatments",
     "jwt.secret" to JWT_SECRET,
     "jwt.test" to "true",
     "storage.driverClassName" to "org.h2.Driver",
     "storage.jdbcUrl" to "jdbc:h2:mem:e2e_treatments;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1;MODE=PostgreSQL;DATABASE_TO_LOWER=TRUE",
     "storage.username" to "root",
     "storage.password" to "password",
     "storage.maximumPoolSize" to "3",
     "storage.isAutoCommit" to "false",
     "storage.transactionIsolation" to "TRANSACTION_REPEATABLE_READ"
   )
   
   given("a running Treatments Service"):
     when("a patient manages their BOLUS treatments"):
       then("they can create, list with type filter, and delete a treatment"):
         testApplication {
           environment { config = e2eConfig }
           application { module() }
           val client = createClient { install(ContentNegotiation) { json() } }
           val sarahToken = generateToken(SARAH_ID, listOf("PATIENT"))
           // 1. List empty: GET /api/v1/users/SARAH_ID/treatments -> 200, empty array
           // 2. Create BOLUS: POST -> 201
           // 3. List: GET -> 200, 1 treatment with type=BOLUS
           // 4. Type filter CARBS: GET ?type=CARBS -> 200, empty array
           // 5. Delete: POST /delete with treatmentId -> 200
           // 6. List: GET -> 200, empty array
         }
     when("a patient tries to access another user's treatments"):
       then("they receive 403"):
         // sarah token, GET /api/v1/users/MIKE_ID/treatments -> 403
     when("a request has no auth token"):
       then("they receive 401"):
         // no bearer, GET /api/v1/users/SARAH_ID/treatments -> 401

## Test Plan
- [ ] ./gradlew :integrationTest --no-daemon from kdiab-treatments/ — 5 repository tests pass
- [ ] ./gradlew :e2eTest --no-daemon — e2e tests pass

- [ ] E2e test verifies 401 on missing auth token

- No seed data — cleanData() needs only DELETE FROM treatments.

title: Replace eclipse-temurin Docker Hub base images with GHCR equivalents
description: All four backend Dockerfiles use eclipse-temurin:21-jdk-alpine and eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine from Docker Hub. Unauthenticated Podman/Docker pulls hit the Docker Hub rate limit (429 toomanyrequests), blocking builds. Switch to the same images hosted on GitHub Container Registry which has no pull rate limits.
design:
# OpenSpec: Replace eclipse-temurin Docker Hub base images with GHCR equivalents

## Goal
Replace docker.io/library/eclipse-temurin base images in all four backend Dockerfiles with ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk and ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jre from GitHub Container Registry, which has no pull rate limits. Also update dependabot.yml so it tracks the new image names.

## Context
All four backend Dockerfiles are structurally identical, using a two-stage build:
- Stage 1 (builder): FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk-alpine AS builder — pulls from docker.io, rate-limited
- Stage 2 (runtime): FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine — pulls from docker.io, rate-limited

Affected files:
- kdiab-measures/backend/Dockerfile
- kdiab-profiles/backend/Dockerfile
- kdiab-treatments/backend/Dockerfile
- kdiab-bff/backend/Dockerfile
- .github/dependabot.yml — has ignore: eclipse-temurin >= 22 in four docker sections; must be updated to new image names

## Interface Changes
No interface changes. Pure infrastructure change.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1 — Verify GHCR Alpine tags exist
Before editing, pull-test the candidate images:
  podman pull ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk:21-alpine
  podman pull ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jre:21-alpine
If either pull fails, fall back to the Ubuntu-slim tag (:21) for that image.
IMPORTANT: if falling back to Ubuntu image, addgroup -S/adduser -S (BusyBox/Alpine syntax) in the runtime stage must change to groupadd -r/useradd -r -g ktor ktor (GNU/Linux syntax).

### Step 2 — Update all four Dockerfiles
In each Dockerfile make exactly two FROM substitutions:
  FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk-alpine AS builder
  → FROM ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk:21-alpine AS builder

  FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine
  → FROM ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jre:21-alpine

No other lines change (assuming Alpine tags exist and are confirmed in step 1).

### Step 3 — Update .github/dependabot.yml
The four package-ecosystem: docker entries for backend dirs currently ignore eclipse-temurin. Replace each with the two new image names:
  ignore:
    - dependency-name: temurin21-jdk
      versions: ['>= 22']
    - dependency-name: temurin21-jre
      versions: ['>= 22']

### Step 4 — Smoke-build one image
  cd /home/triplem/projects/kdiab
  BUILDAH_FORMAT=docker podman build -f kdiab-bff/backend/Dockerfile kdiab-bff -t test-bff-backend
Confirm exit code 0 and no rate-limit errors. Clean up: podman rmi test-bff-backend.

### Step 5 — Commit and close issue
Commit message: fix(docker): replace eclipse-temurin Docker Hub images with GHCR equivalents
Then: bd close kdiab-78y

## Test Plan
- [ ] podman pull ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk:21-alpine succeeds with no rate-limit error
- [ ] podman pull ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jre:21-alpine succeeds
- [ ] podman build of kdiab-bff backend exits 0
- [ ] No unit tests affected — pure Dockerfile/YAML change

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All four backend Dockerfiles reference ghcr.io/adoptium/* images only
- [ ] podman compose up --build succeeds from a clean-cache state
- [ ] dependabot.yml ignore rules reference the new image names
- [ ] No functional change to the running application

## Risks & Assumptions
- ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk:21-alpine may not exist → fall back to :21 (Ubuntu-slim); agent must verify with pull-test first
- If Ubuntu fallback needed: Alpine addgroup -S/adduser -S syntax must change to GNU equivalents
- Adoptium GHCR images are the same JDK build as Docker Hub eclipse-temurin (same upstream source)
close_reason: User rejected GHCR approach before any files were changed. No implementation occurred.

title: kdiab-bff: Backend-for-Frontend with analytics dashboard
description: New kdiab-bff service aggregating measures, treatments, and profiles into a unified analytics frontend. Features: combined CGM+treatment timeline chart, HbA1c/TIR analytics, AGP (ambulatory glucose profile by hour), profiles viewer. Stack: Kotlin/Ktor backend (stateless, HTTP clients to upstream services), React+Recharts frontend. Ports: backend 8083, frontend 3003.
close_reason: kdiab-bff service fully implemented: backend (services, routes, HTTP clients, domain, plugins, Application.kt, Dockerfile) and frontend (App.tsx, Tab nav, TimelineChart, AgpChart, HbA1cCard, TimeInRangeBar, ProfilesTable, i18n, Recharts)

title: Add CLAUDE.md files for kdiab-calc and kdiab-carbs services
description: Both new services lack CLAUDE.md, meaning agents working in those directories have no service-specific guidance about ports, purpose, package structure, environment variables, or design decisions — unlike every other service in the monorepo.

title: Add CSP support and nosniff headers to kdiab-profiles CLAUDE.md — fix stale frontend/ directory reference
description: kdiab-profiles/CLAUDE.md Repository Structure section still shows 'frontend/ # React/TypeScript SPA (Vite)' but the directory was deleted when frontends were consolidated into kdiab-ui. The section should be removed or updated to reference kdiab-ui.

title: Write ADRs for kdiab-common extraction, kdiab-calc service, and kdiab-carbs service
description: Three significant architectural decisions have no ADR: extracting shared Ktor plugins and domain types into kdiab-common Gradle library, adding kdiab-calc as a stateless dose-calculator service, and adding kdiab-carbs as a food database service. All materially change the monorepo structure and deployment topology. docs/adr/ already has numbered ADRs through ADR-007.

title: Update ADR-003 to reflect shared gradle/libs.versions.toml replacing per-service catalogs
description: ADR-003 explicitly says the design 'Rejected' sharing a version catalog and that services evolved independently. Yet every service's settings.gradle.kts now references from(files('../gradle/libs.versions.toml')). The ADR should be updated to record this superseding decision and its rationale.

title: Enable noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes in tsconfig.app.json
description: tsconfig enables strict but omits noUncheckedIndexedAccess (would catch unsound ! assertions on array elements like cgmData[lo].value! in TimelineChart.tsx:116) and exactOptionalPropertyTypes (would flag optional-vs-undefined conflation in API interfaces like validFrom?: string | null).

title: Add data quality / sensor wear day indicator to AGP chart
description: AgpChart renders whenever the API returns data regardless of sensor wear days or reading density. The backend sends a warning string and readingCount exists in the API type but neither is displayed. Short or patchy data can produce a misleading AGP silently.

title: Display HbA1c reading count from API response to indicate estimate reliability
description: The readingCount property from /analytics/hba1c is present in the Hba1cResponse type in analyzeApi.ts but is never passed to or displayed in HbA1cCard. Clinicians cannot tell whether the HbA1c estimate is based on 100 or 10,000 readings, which significantly affects its reliability.

title: Add Level 2 hypoglycemia (<54 mg/dL) segment to TIR breakdown
description: TimeInRangeBar lumps all sub-70 mg/dL values into a single belowCount category. Standard ADA/EASD ambulatory glucose profile consensus requires separately displaying time < 54 mg/dL (very low/Level 2 hypo) — the clinically critical severe hypoglycemia threshold.

title: Wire koverVerify into check task for kdiab-measures, kdiab-treatments, kdiab-profiles
description: Only kdiab-analyze and kdiab-calc explicitly dependsOn('koverVerify') in the check task. The other three services declare an 80% minimum bound but verification is never enforced during ./gradlew check, meaning coverage can silently drop below the threshold.

title: Add ConnectException to BFF retry policy for transient upstream unavailability
description: kdiab-analyze Application.kt retryOnExceptionIf only catches SocketTimeoutException and HttpRequestTimeoutException. A ConnectException (brief container restart of an upstream service) propagates immediately as a 502 without exhausting the configured retry budget.

title: Add proxy_connect_timeout and proxy_read_timeout directives to nginx config
description: Neither nginx config (config/gateway/nginx.conf nor kdiab-ui/nginx.conf) sets proxy timeout directives. Absent explicit timeouts, nginx uses 60-second defaults, meaning a hung backend ties up an nginx worker indefinitely and can cascade into connection pool exhaustion.

title: Filter BFF HTTP retry policy to GET-only methods
description: kdiab-analyze Application.kt retryIf { _, response -> response.status.value >= 500 } applies to every HTTP method on the shared HttpClient. If a future write endpoint is added, it will be retried on 5xx risking duplicate writes. Should be filtered to safe (GET) methods only.

title: Update Docker Compose healthchecks to probe /readyz instead of /healthz
description: All depends_on: condition: service_healthy blocks use /healthz (liveness) but services implement a meaningful /readyz endpoint (PostgreSQL SELECT 1 for DB-backed services, upstream fanout for BFF). Using /healthz confirms only that the JVM is alive, not that the DB connection pool or upstream dependencies are ready, causing race-condition failures during initial stack startup.

title: Tighten Content Security Policy — restrict connect-src and remove style-src unsafe-inline
description: nginx CSP permits connect-src 'self' http://localhost:* https://localhost:* (any localhost port — meaningless in deployed browser context) and style-src 'unsafe-inline' (enables CSS injection). A production CSP should pin exact API origins and replace inline styles with hashes or nonces.

title: Restrict /metrics endpoint — currently unauthenticated on the same port as the API
description: The Dropwizard metrics route (GET /metrics) in all services has no authenticate{} block, so any client that reaches the service port receives JVM thread states, GC counts, and request timings without authentication. Either require authentication, bind to a separate internal port, or restrict by IP.

title: Validate X-Forwarded-For via Ktor ForwardedHeaders plugin before trusting in audit log
description: Doctor access is audited by reading the raw X-Forwarded-For header directly without Ktor's ForwardedHeaders plugin or a trusted-proxy allowlist in kdiab-measures, kdiab-treatments, and kdiab-profiles AuditRoutes. Any client can spoof the recorded IP address, undermining forensic value.

title: Upgrade Keycloak from 23.0 to current LTS version
description: Keycloak 23.0 was released in late 2023 and has received multiple CVE fixes in versions 24-26. The pinned tag without floating updates means security patches are never applied and the IAM layer handling all PHI authentication runs known-vulnerable code.

title: Change kdiab-calc swagger.enabled default to false in application.conf
description: kdiab-calc has swagger.enabled = true as the hard-coded default, meaning every deployment that omits SWAGGER_ENABLED=false ships an interactive API explorer. All other services default to false and require explicit opt-in.

title: Add Keycloak production-mode compose profile for staging and production deployments
description: All compose stacks use 'command: start-dev --import-realm' which disables TLS, enables admin REST without IP restrictions, uses embedded H2 for Keycloak's own data, and turns off production hardening. A separate compose override or profile using 'start' mode with an external PostgreSQL Keycloak DB should be provided.

title: Add success toast/confirmation after treatment and measure save
description: After handleSaveTreatment or handleSaveMeasure succeeds the modal closes silently with no toast or snackbar. With insulin entries this creates doubt about whether the dose was recorded, leading to duplicate entries. All other destructive/write operations (delete, archive) show confirmation.

title: Add server-side pagination to TreatmentList
description: TreatmentList calls listTreatments with no page/size parameters and renders the full result. After months of daily use this becomes a very large payload and an unscrollable table. MeasureList already has proper pagination — TreatmentList should match.

title: Replace raw enum names with human-readable labels in DoseCalculator trend dropdown
description: The CGM trend select renders API enum values like DOUBLE_UP and FORTY_FIVE_DOWN directly as option text. i18n keys for human-readable labels (Rising rapidly, 45° down) exist in the translation files but are not applied here. This safety-critical input is confusing to patients.

title: Add ACTIVE/ARCHIVED status to FoodEntry to match measure/treatment lifecycle
description: FoodEntry supports only hard-delete with no soft-delete mechanism. Measures and treatments use an ACTIVE/ARCHIVED status for recoverability. This inconsistency means accidentally deleted food entries are permanently unrecoverable, unlike all other mutable clinical data in the platform.

title: Wrap parseSegmentTime in runCatching and throw BusinessValidationException on malformed input
description: DoseCalculationService.parseSegmentTime splits on ':' and calls toInt() with no error handling. A malformed startTime from the upstream profile API (empty string, missing colon) propagates as IndexOutOfBoundsException or NumberFormatException returning a bare 500 instead of a meaningful error.

title: Dispatch readyz JDBC probe to Dispatchers.IO — currently blocks Netty I/O thread
description: The /readyz route in kdiab-measures, kdiab-treatments, kdiab-profiles, and kdiab-carbs calls synchronous Exposed transaction { exec('SELECT 1') } directly in a coroutine route handler without withContext(Dispatchers.IO), blocking the Netty event-loop thread and potentially starving other requests under load.

title: Unify Instant type — kdiab-analyze uses kotlinx.datetime.Instant while all other services use kotlin.time.Instant
description: kdiab-analyze domain model (Timeline.kt, AnalyticsService.kt, TimelineService.kt) imports kotlinx.datetime.Instant throughout, while all five upstream services use kotlin.time.Instant uniformly. This prevents safe sharing of temporal utilities through kdiab-common and creates a confusing two-type system.

title: Add MAX_TREATMENTS safety guard to TreatmentsClient pagination loop
description: MeasuresClient has a MAX_MEASURES=50,000 check() guard to abort on pathological datasets. TreatmentsClient has no equivalent limit, so a user with a very large treatment history will loop indefinitely until memory is exhausted.

title: Reuse DefaultApi/HttpClient instances in outbound HTTP clients — currently recreated per call
description: Every getMeasures/getTreatments/getProfiles invocation in kdiab-analyze and kdiab-calc creates a new DefaultApi() which wraps the engine in a fresh HttpClient and installs plugins on it. The client should be constructed once at injection time; only the Authorization token header should vary per request.

title: Add pagination to ProfilesClient — currently truncates at first 50 profiles
description: ProfilesClient.getProfiles issues a single page-0 request for 50 items and ignores totalCount. Unlike MeasuresClient and TreatmentsClient which paginate to exhaustion, patients with long profile histories receive incomplete TIR threshold data on the HbA1c and AGP endpoints.

title: Add getActiveAndArchivedProfiles to ProfileService and use it in kdiab-analyze
description: ProfileService only has getProfiles() which returns all profiles and lets callers filter. kdiab-analyze's ProfilesService fetches all profiles then filters for ACTIVE and ARCHIVED in memory. Add a dedicated getActiveAndArchivedProfiles(userId, from, to) method to kdiab-profiles ProfileService that queries the DB with a status IN (ACTIVE, ARCHIVED) clause. Add a corresponding endpoint or extend the existing GET /profiles endpoint with a status[]=ACTIVE&status[]=ARCHIVED multi-value query param. Update kdiab-analyze's ProfilesClient to use the filtered endpoint rather than fetching all and discarding DRAFT/PROPOSED profiles.
design:
# OpenSpec: Add getActiveAndArchivedProfiles to ProfileService and use it in kdiab-analyze (kdiab-lsyd)

## Goal
`kdiab-analyze`'s `ProfilesService` fetches ALL profiles from kdiab-profiles then discards DRAFTs and PROPOSED ones in memory. This wastes bandwidth and couples the analysis layer to kdiab-profiles' internal status taxonomy. Add a repository method + service method in kdiab-profiles that returns only ACTIVE and ARCHIVED profiles. Add a `statuses` query parameter to the GET /profiles endpoint. Update kdiab-analyze's `ProfilesClient` to pass `status=ACTIVE&status=ARCHIVED` and remove the in-memory filter.

## Context

### kdiab-profiles backend
- `domain/repository/ProfileRepository.kt` — `findAllByUserId(userId, page, size)` has no status filter
- `infrastructure/persistence/ExposedProfileRepository.kt` — `findAllByUserId` does `selectAll().where { userId eq ... }` (no status filter, line ~102)
- `application/service/ProfileService.kt` — `getProfiles(userId, page, size)` delegates to `findAllByUserId`
- `adapters/inbound/web/ProfileRoutes.kt` — GET handler calls `profileService.getProfiles(userId, page, size)`
- `api/openapi.yaml` — `GET /users/{userId}/profiles` currently has `page` and `size` params only

### kdiab-analyze
- `adapters/outbound/http/ProfilesClient.kt` — calls `api.listProfiles(userId, page=0, size=50)` (generated jvm-ktor client)
- `application/service/ProfilesService.kt` — calls `profilesClient.getProfiles(...)` then filters `.filter { it.status == ACTIVE || it.status == ARCHIVED }`
- `kdiab-analyze/api/upstream/profiles` generated types — `DefaultApi.listProfiles()` method signature

## Interface Changes

### kdiab-profiles/api/openapi.yaml
Add optional `status` query parameter (multi-value) to `GET /users/{userId}/profiles`:
```yaml
- name: status
  in: query
  required: false
  style: form
  explode: true
  schema:
    type: array
    items:
      type: string
      enum: [ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, DRAFT, PROPOSED]
```
Response schema unchanged. No DB schema change.

### kdiab-analyze generated client
After updating the profiles openapi.yaml, re-run `generateProfilesModels` in kdiab-analyze to pick up the new `status` parameter in the generated `DefaultApi.listProfiles()` signature.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: kdiab-profiles backend

1. **`kdiab-profiles/api/openapi.yaml`** — add `status` multi-value query param to `GET /users/{userId}/profiles` (see Interface Changes above). Run `./gradlew openApiGenerate` to regenerate the Ktor server stubs.

2. **`ProfileRepository.kt`** — add method:
   ```kotlin
   suspend fun findByStatuses(userId: Uuid, statuses: List<ProfileStatus>, page: Int = 0, size: Int = 50): List<Profile>
   ```

3. **`ExposedProfileRepository.kt`** — implement `findByStatuses`:
   ```kotlin
   override suspend fun findByStatuses(userId: Uuid, statuses: List<ProfileStatus>, page: Int, size: Int): List<Profile> =
       withContext(ioDispatcher) {
           suspendTransaction {
               Profiles.innerJoin(ProfileStatuses)
                   .selectAll()
                   .where {
                       (Profiles.userId eq userId.toJavaUuid()) and
                       (ProfileStatuses.status inList statuses.map { it.name })
                   }
                   .orderBy(Profiles.createdAt, SortOrder.DESC)
                   .limit(size).offset((page * size).toLong())
                   .map { it.toProfile() }
           }
       }
   ```
   Read the existing `findAllByUserId` implementation first to understand the table join pattern.

4. **`ProfileService.kt`** — add:
   ```kotlin
   suspend fun getActiveAndArchivedProfiles(userId: Uuid, page: Int = 0, size: Int = 50): PagedProfiles {
       val statuses = listOf(ProfileStatus.ACTIVE, ProfileStatus.ARCHIVED)
       val items = profileRepository.findByStatuses(userId, statuses, page, size)
       val total = items.size.toLong()  // or add countByStatuses if needed
       return PagedProfiles(items = items, page = page, size = size, totalCount = total)
   }
   ```

5. **`ProfileRoutes.kt`** — in the GET /profiles handler, read the `status` query parameter:
   ```kotlin
   val requestedStatuses = call.parameters.getAll("status")
       ?.mapNotNull { runCatching { ProfileStatus.valueOf(it.uppercase()) }.getOrNull() }
   val result = if (requestedStatuses.isNullOrEmpty()) {
   ```

# OpenSpec: Centralize Gradle version catalog into a single root libs.versions.toml (kdiab-hd8i)

## Goal
Each of the six backend services has its own `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. Consolidate them into a single `gradle/libs.versions.toml` at the monorepo root. Each service's `settings.gradle.kts` is updated to reference the root catalog via `dependencyResolutionManagement`. Per-service toml files are deleted. This guarantees version alignment and eliminates drift (e.g. Ktor 3.4.2 in measures vs 3.0.3 in analyze).

## Context

### Current state
Each service (kdiab-measures, kdiab-profiles, kdiab-treatments, kdiab-carbs, kdiab-calc, kdiab-analyze) has:
- `gradle/libs.versions.toml` — unique per service, versions may differ
- `settings.gradle.kts` — minimal (just `pluginManagement` + `rootProject.name`)

### kdiab-measures/gradle/libs.versions.toml is the canonical reference
It has the most complete and up-to-date entries. Use it as the base for the merged file, but also read all other services' toml files and merge in any entries that are missing. Keep the highest version for any conflicting entry.

### Additional libs needed in root toml
- kdiab-analyze uses Ktor client (CIO, content-negotiation) + openapi-generator client — confirm these are present
- kdiab-calc has same dependency set as analyze (no DB)
- kdiab-profiles, kdiab-treatments, kdiab-carbs have DB deps (Exposed, HikariCP, Liquibase, H2)

## Interface Changes
None (build-system only change).

## Implementation Plan

1. Read all 6 per-service `gradle/libs.versions.toml` files to identify any entries not in kdiab-measures version. Also read `kdiab-analyze/gradle/libs.versions.toml` and `kdiab-calc/gradle/libs.versions.toml` since they have Ktor client entries.

2. Create `/home/triplem/projects/kdiab/gradle/libs.versions.toml` — merged, deduplicated catalog. Use kdiab-measures as the base; add missing entries from other services. For the `[libraries]` section, also add:
   - `ktor-client-cio` (for analyze/calc)
   - `ktor-client-mock` (for tests in analyze/calc)
   Any libs already present with a version ref keep that ref.

3. Update each service's `settings.gradle.kts` to add:
```kotlin
dependencyResolutionManagement {
    versionCatalogs {
        create("libs") {
            from(files("../gradle/libs.versions.toml"))
        }
    }
}
```
   Services: kdiab-measures, kdiab-profiles, kdiab-treatments, kdiab-carbs, kdiab-calc, kdiab-analyze.

4. Delete each per-service `gradle/libs.versions.toml`:
   ```bash
   git rm kdiab-measures/gradle/libs.versions.toml
   git rm kdiab-profiles/gradle/libs.versions.toml
   git rm kdiab-treatments/gradle/libs.versions.toml
   git rm kdiab-carbs/gradle/libs.versions.toml
   git rm kdiab-calc/gradle/libs.versions.toml
   git rm kdiab-analyze/gradle/libs.versions.toml
   ```
   Keep the `gradle/` directories themselves (they contain gradle-wrapper.jar and gradle-wrapper.properties).

5. Verify each service builds:
   ```bash
   cd kdiab-measures && ./gradlew dependencies --configuration compileClasspath 2>&1 | head -5
   ```

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew check` from each of the 6 services — BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- [ ] `ls /home/triplem/projects/kdiab/gradle/libs.versions.toml` — file exists
- [ ] `ls kdiab-measures/gradle/libs.versions.toml` — file does NOT exist

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Single `gradle/libs.versions.toml` exists at monorepo root
- [ ] All 6 per-service toml files deleted
- [ ] All 6 service `./gradlew check` pass

## Risks & Assumptions
- Each service's Gradle wrapper is independent — they each have their own `gradlew`. The settings change uses `files("../gradle/libs.versions.toml")` relative to the service root.
- If a service's `gradle/` directory becomes empty after deleting the toml, Gradle still needs `gradle-wrapper.jar` and `gradle-wrapper.properties` there — do not delete the directory.

title: Make JSON pretty-print configurable per environment
description: All services install ContentNegotiation with a hardcoded Json{} config. Add a json.prettyPrint boolean to each service's application.conf (default false, overridable via JSON_PRETTY_PRINT env var). In dev docker-compose files set JSON_PRETTY_PRINT=true so responses are human-readable during development. In root docker-compose (prod-like) leave it unset (false). The change touches Application.kt in each service and the relevant docker-compose files.
design:
# OpenSpec: Make JSON pretty-print configurable per environment (kdiab-gjvk)

## Goal
All five backend services hardcode `prettyPrint = false` in their `Application.kt`. Add a `json.prettyPrint` config key (boolean, default false) readable from `application.conf` and overridable via a `JSON_PRETTY_PRINT` environment variable. Set `JSON_PRETTY_PRINT=true` in each service's standalone `docker-compose.yml` so developers see readable JSON responses without changing production config.

## Context

### Services and their Application.kt locations
- `kdiab-measures/src/main/kotlin/.../Application.kt` — `install(ContentNegotiation) { json(Json { prettyPrint = false; ignoreUnknownKeys = true }) }`
- `kdiab-profiles/src/main/kotlin/.../Application.kt` — same pattern
- `kdiab-treatments/src/main/kotlin/.../Application.kt` — same pattern
- `kdiab-carbs/src/main/kotlin/.../Application.kt` — same pattern
- `kdiab-calc/src/main/kotlin/.../Application.kt` — uses a local `val json = Json { prettyPrint = false ... }`
- `kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../Application.kt` — uses a local `val json = Json { prettyPrint = false ... }` shared between server ContentNegotiation and HttpClient

### application.conf locations (one per service)
- `kdiab-<service>/src/main/resources/application.conf`

### docker-compose.yml (standalone per-service)
Each service directory has a `docker-compose.yml` that starts the service with its own Keycloak + Postgres.

## Interface Changes
None (runtime-only behavior change).

## Implementation Plan

### Each of the 5 services — repeat these 3 steps:

**Step A: application.conf** — add at the end:
```hocon
json {
  prettyPrint = false
  prettyPrint = ${?JSON_PRETTY_PRINT}
}
```

**Step B: Application.kt** — read the flag and wire into ContentNegotiation:
```kotlin
val prettyPrint = environment.config.propertyOrNull("json.prettyPrint")
    ?.getString()?.toBoolean() ?: false
// ...
install(ContentNegotiation) {
    json(Json {
        this.prettyPrint = prettyPrint
        ignoreUnknownKeys = true
    })
}
```
For kdiab-analyze and kdiab-calc that share the Json instance with the HttpClient, apply `prettyPrint` only to the server-side Json instance, not the client-side one (client JSON should never pretty-print upstream requests).

**Step C: docker-compose.yml** (standalone per-service) — add env var to the backend service:
```yaml
environment:
  JSON_PRETTY_PRINT: "true"
```
Do NOT add this to the root `docker-compose.yml` (that file represents the prod-like stack).

### Services to update (5 total):
1. kdiab-measures — Steps A, B, C
2. kdiab-profiles — Steps A, B, C
3. kdiab-treatments — Steps A, B, C
4. kdiab-carbs — Steps A, B, C
5. kdiab-calc — Steps A, B, C
6. kdiab-analyze — Steps A, B (the shared Json in Application.kt has a `val json = Json {...}` block; add `prettyPrint` only to the server Json); Step C

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew check` in each service — BUILD SUCCESSFUL (Application test still passes)
- [ ] Verify: with `JSON_PRETTY_PRINT=true`, response body contains newlines; with `false`, it does not

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `application.conf` in all 6 services has `json.prettyPrint` with env var override
- [ ] `Application.kt` in all 6 services reads and applies the flag
- [ ] Root `docker-compose.yml` has no `JSON_PRETTY_PRINT` entry
- [ ] Quality gates pass

## Risks & Assumptions
- kdiab-analyze shares a `Json` instance between server and HTTP client. Do not apply `prettyPrint=true` to the client Json — upstream services would need to parse pretty-printed request bodies.
- The test suites use `application.conf` from `src/test/resources/` which may not have the `json` block; that's fine since `propertyOrNull` returns null → defaults to false.

## Goal

2. docs/adr/ADR-004-bff-stateless-aggregator.adoc — kdiab-analyze as stateless BFF. Status: Accepted. Context: 4 services need unified analytics view. Decision: dedicated stateless aggregator service, no DB, forwards JWT. Consequences: horizontal scaling, no caching layer.
3. docs/adr/ADR-005-api-first-openapi-codegen.adoc — API-first design with OpenAPI codegen. Status: Accepted. Context: frontend and backend must stay in sync. # OpenSpec: Add HikariCP connection timeout, idle timeout, and leak detection (kdiab-fay)

In HikariConfig().apply, before validate(), set: this.connectionTimeout = CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS, this.idleTimeout = IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, this.maxLifetime = MAX_LIFETIME_MS, this.leakDetectionThreshold = LEAK_DETECTION_THRESHOLD_MS.
