title: Convert /metrics endpoint from custom text format to Prometheus exposition format
description: kdiab-analyze's Metrics.kt returns metrics in a custom plain-text format (line 43) that is incompatible with standard Prometheus scrapers and Grafana. Switching to the Prometheus exposition format (using Micrometer or DropwizardMetrics-Prometheus bridge) would enable standard monitoring stack integration.
design:
# OpenSpec: Prometheus exposition format for /metrics (kdiab-9yu)

## Goal
Replace the custom plain-text metrics format in `Metrics.kt` with the standard Prometheus exposition format so Prometheus scrapers and Grafana can ingest the endpoint without a custom parser.

## Context
- `kdiab-analyze/.../plugins/Metrics.kt` — current format: `"$name ${gauge.value}\n"` with no `# TYPE` or `# HELP` lines. Content-Type is `text/plain`.
- Dropwizard metric types: gauges, counters, meters, timers. All available via `registry.*`.
- Prometheus format spec: each metric block has optional `# HELP`, mandatory `# TYPE`, then `name value [timestamp]`. Metric names must match `[a-zA-Z_:][a-zA-Z0-9_:]*` (dots and hyphens must be replaced with underscores).

## Interface Changes
- `GET /metrics` response body format changes from custom text to Prometheus exposition format.
- `Content-Type` changes to `text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8`.

## Implementation Plan
1. `Metrics.kt` — Add helper function `sanitize(name: String): String = name.replace(Regex("[^a-zA-Z0-9_:]"), "_")`.
2. `Metrics.kt` — Replace the `get("/metrics")` handler body:
   ```kotlin
   val sb = StringBuilder()
   registry.gauges.forEach { (name, gauge) ->
       val n = sanitize(name)
       runCatching {
           sb.appendLine("# TYPE $n gauge")
           sb.appendLine("$n ${gauge.value}")
       }
   }
   registry.counters.forEach { (name, counter) ->
       val n = sanitize(name)
       sb.appendLine("# TYPE ${n}_total counter")
       sb.appendLine("${n}_total ${counter.count}")
   }
   registry.meters.forEach { (name, meter) ->
       val n = sanitize(name)
       sb.appendLine("# TYPE ${n}_total counter")
       sb.appendLine("${n}_total ${meter.count}")
       sb.appendLine("# TYPE ${n}_rate1m gauge")
       sb.appendLine("${n}_rate1m ${meter.oneMinuteRate}")
   }
   registry.timers.forEach { (name, timer) ->
       val n = sanitize(name)
       val snap = timer.snapshot
       sb.appendLine("# TYPE ${n}_count counter")
       sb.appendLine("${n}_count ${timer.count}")
       sb.appendLine("# TYPE ${n}_p50_seconds gauge")
       sb.appendLine("${n}_p50_seconds ${snap.median / 1_000_000.0}")
       sb.appendLine("# TYPE ${n}_p95_seconds gauge")
       sb.appendLine("${n}_p95_seconds ${snap.get95thPercentile() / 1_000_000.0}")
       sb.appendLine("# TYPE ${n}_p99_seconds gauge")
       sb.appendLine("${n}_p99_seconds ${snap.get99thPercentile() / 1_000_000.0}")
   }
   call.respondText(sb.toString(), ContentType.parse("text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8"))
   ```
   Note: Dropwizard timer snapshot values are in nanoseconds; convert to seconds by dividing by 1_000_000_000. Confirm unit by checking DropwizardMetrics snapshot docs — if milliseconds, divide by 1000.

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew :kdiab-analyze:backend:check`
- [ ] Manual: `curl http://localhost:8084/metrics` shows `# TYPE` lines and sanitized names

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All metric names contain only `[a-zA-Z0-9_:]`
- [ ] Each metric block has a `# TYPE` line
- [ ] Content-Type is `text/plain; version=0.0.4`
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec: Prometheus exposition format with TYPE lines and sanitized metric names

# OpenSpec: Fix inconsistent Instant types in BFF (kdiab-5ra)

## Goal
TimelineService imports java.time.Instant while AnalyticsService and BffRoutes use kotlinx.datetime.Instant. The CLAUDE.md convention mandates kotlinx.datetime.Instant in application/ code. Switching TimelineService also changes the exception type for from/to parsing from DateTimeParseException (unhandled → 500) to IllegalArgumentException (handled by StatusPages → 400).

## Context
- `kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../application/service/TimelineService.kt` line 10: `import java.time.Instant` — violates project convention
  - Lines 23–24: `val fromInstant = Instant.parse(from)` and `val toInstant = Instant.parse(to)` — throws java.time.format.DateTimeParseException (not caught → 500)
  - Lines 42, 59: `runCatching { Instant.parse(...) }.getOrNull()` — already safe
- AnalyticsService line 8: `import kotlinx.datetime.Instant` — correct
- BffRoutes lines 132, 135: uses `kotlinx.datetime.Instant` — correct
- Domain models use String for timestamps — no change needed

## Interface Changes
No interface changes.

## Implementation Plan
1. `kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../application/service/TimelineService.kt`:
   - Change `import java.time.Instant` to `import kotlinx.datetime.Instant`
   - Remove any other java.time.* imports if only Instant was used
   - Lines 23–24: no code change to parse calls needed (same API: Instant.parse(from))
   - Check comparison predicates at lines 42, 59: if the code uses .isAfter()/.isBefore() (java.time API), replace with > / < operators (kotlinx.datetime.Instant implements Comparable<Instant>)
   - If .toEpochMilli() is used anywhere, replace with .toEpochMilliseconds()

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew check --no-daemon` from `kdiab-analyze/` — Detekt clean, existing tests pass
- [ ] `grep -n "java.time" TimelineService.kt` — no results

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No java.time.* imports remain in the application service
- [ ] `./gradlew check` passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- kotlinx.datetime.Instant comparison operators <, > work via Comparable<Instant>.
- After this fix, invalid from/to params throw IllegalArgumentException → 400 (handled by StatusPages).
- kdiab-4dj: do NOT touch TimelineService.kt there (this issue covers it).

title: Disable source maps in production Vite build

# OpenSpec: Disable source maps in production Vite build (kdiab-s4m)

## Goal
`kdiab-ui/vite.config.ts` has `build: { sourcemap: true, minify: false }` which serves the original TypeScript source code and unminified bundle to any user with browser DevTools. ## Context
- `kdiab-ui/vite.config.ts` lines 4-6: `build: { sourcemap: true, minify: false }` — both settings are wrong for production.
- Source maps allow reconstructing original TypeScript from the compiled bundle.
- `minify: false` makes the bundle larger and easier to reverse-engineer.
- The dev server (line 7: `port: 3000`) is unaffected — this is build-only config.
- No error tracking service is configured to consume source maps privately (Sentry, Rollbar, etc.).

No interface changes. Build output changes only.

## Implementation Plan
1. `kdiab-ui/vite.config.ts` — Remove the `build` key entirely (Vite defaults: `sourcemap: false`, `minify: 'esbuild'`). The resulting config:
   ```ts
   export default defineConfig({
     plugins: [react()],
     server: {
       port: 3000,
       proxy: { ... }
     },
     test: { ... }
   })
   ```

## Test Plan

title: Fix unsafe Instant.parse() calls in mappers and services: wrap in BusinessValidationException
description: Instant.parse() is called without try/catch in MeasureMapper.toDomain(), TreatmentMapper.toDomain(), AnalyticsService (lines 66-67, 112-113), TimelineService (lines 23-24), and LocalTimeSerializer. Invalid ISO-8601 input causes uncaught DateTimeParseException that propagates as HTTP 500. These should be caught and rethrown as BusinessValidationException → 400.
design:
# OpenSpec: Fix unsafe Instant.parse() calls in mappers (kdiab-4dj)

## Goal
MeasureMapper.toDomain() and TreatmentMapper.toDomain() call Instant.parse() without exception handling. The mappers should throw BusinessValidationException explicitly with a descriptive message about which field is invalid. TimelineService from/to parsing is covered by kdiab-5ra — do NOT touch TimelineService.kt here.

## Context
- `kdiab-measures/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/inbound/web/MeasureMapper.kt` line 31: `measuredAt = Instant.parse(this.measuredAt)` — uses kotlin.time.Instant, throws IllegalArgumentException on bad input.
- `kdiab-treatments/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/inbound/web/TreatmentMapper.kt` line 108: `treatedAt = Instant.parse(this.treatedAt)` — same.
- AnalyticsService already uses runCatching — safe, no change needed.
- TimelineService lines 23–24: handled by kdiab-5ra. Do NOT touch here.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes.

## Implementation Plan
1. `kdiab-measures/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/inbound/web/MeasureMapper.kt` line 31 — Wrap in try/catch:
   measuredAt = try { Instant.parse(this.measuredAt) } catch (e: IllegalArgumentException) { throw BusinessValidationException("Invalid measuredAt timestamp: '${this.measuredAt}' is not a valid ISO-8601 instant") },
   Add import: org.javafreedom.kdiab.measures.domain.exception.BusinessValidationException

2. `kdiab-treatments/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/inbound/web/TreatmentMapper.kt` line 108 — Same pattern:
   treatedAt = try { Instant.parse(this.treatedAt) } catch (e: IllegalArgumentException) { throw BusinessValidationException("Invalid treatedAt timestamp: '${this.treatedAt}' is not a valid ISO-8601 instant") },
   Add import: org.javafreedom.kdiab.treatments.domain.exception.BusinessValidationException

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew check --no-daemon` from `kdiab-measures/` — tests pass, Detekt clean
- [ ] `./gradlew check --no-daemon` from `kdiab-treatments/` — tests pass, Detekt clean

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Invalid measuredAt in measures returns 400 with descriptive message
- [ ] Invalid treatedAt in treatments returns 400 with descriptive message
- [ ] `./gradlew check` passes in both services

## Risks & Assumptions
- The existing IllegalArgumentException StatusPages handler already returns 400; this adds a specific message.
- Do NOT change AnalyticsService or TimelineService in this issue.
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec in isolated worktree

title: Add pagination to profiles list endpoint (/users/{userId}/profiles returns unbounded array)
description: The kdiab-profiles list endpoint returns all profile versions as an unbounded array with no page/size parameters, while measures and treatments both have paginated list endpoints. A user with many profile versions (common with frequent adjustments) could cause OOM on both client and server.
design:
# OpenSpec: Pagination for profiles list endpoint (kdiab-v1o)

## Goal
`GET /users/{userId}/profiles` returns an unbounded array. Add `page`/`size` query params and a paginated response wrapper, matching the pattern used by kdiab-measures and kdiab-treatments.

## Context
- `kdiab-profiles/api/openapi.yaml` — `listProfiles` returns `array` of Profile objects; no pagination params.
- `ProfileRepository.findAllByUserId(userId)` returns `List<Profile>` (no paging).
- `ProfileService.getProfiles(userId)` delegates directly.
- `ProfileRoutes.listProfiles` — calls `profileService.getProfiles(targetUserId)`, responds with `profiles.map { it.toApi() }`.
- `kdiab-analyze` — `ProfilesClient.getProfiles` calls `/api/v1/users/$userId/profiles`, expects `List<ProfileDto>`. **Must be updated to handle paginated response.**

## Interface Changes
- `kdiab-profiles/api/openapi.yaml`:
  - `GET /users/{userId}/profiles` — add optional query params `page: integer (default 0)` and `size: integer (default 50, max 200)`.
  - Response schema changes from `array<Profile>` to new schema `PagedProfilesResponse { items: array<Profile>, page: integer, size: integer, totalCount: integer }`.
- `kdiab-analyze/api/openapi.yaml` (BFF) — no change needed (it does not expose profile list).

## Implementation Plan
1. `kdiab-profiles/api/openapi.yaml` — Add `page` and `size` query params to `listProfiles`. Add `PagedProfilesResponse` schema with `items`, `page`, `size`, `totalCount`. Change response to `PagedProfilesResponse`.
2. `kdiab-profiles/.../domain/repository/ProfileRepository.kt` — Add: `suspend fun countByUserId(userId: Uuid): Long`. Update `findAllByUserId` signature to: `suspend fun findAllByUserId(userId: Uuid, page: Int = 0, size: Int = 50): List<Profile>`.
3. `kdiab-profiles/.../infrastructure/persistence/ExposedProfileRepository.kt` — Implement `countByUserId` with `ProfilesTable.selectAll().where { userId eq ... }.count()`. Update `findAllByUserId` to add `.limit(size, offset = (page * size).toLong())`.
4. `kdiab-profiles/.../application/service/ProfileService.kt` — Change `getProfiles` signature to accept `page: Int = 0, size: Int = 50`. Add new method `countProfiles(userId)`. Return a data class `PagedProfiles(items: List<Profile>, page: Int, size: Int, totalCount: Long)`.
5. `kdiab-profiles/.../adapters/inbound/web/ProfileRoutes.kt` — In `listProfiles` handler: read `params.page ?: 0` and `(params.size ?: 50).coerceAtMost(200)`. Call `profileService.getProfiles(targetUserId, page, size)` and `profileService.countProfiles(targetUserId)`. Respond with `PagedProfilesResponse { items, page, size, totalCount }` using a local serializable data class.
6. `kdiab-analyze/.../adapters/outbound/http/ProfilesClient.kt` — The existing `getProfiles` call returns `List<ProfileDto>`. Update to expect a paged wrapper. Add a local `PagedProfilesDto(items: List<ProfileDto>, page: Int, size: Int, totalCount: Int)`. Deserialize as paged, return `response.body<PagedProfilesDto>().items` (page 0, size 50 covers all profiles for typical users).

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit: `getProfiles page=0 size=50 returns first page`.
- [ ] Unit: `getProfiles page beyond total returns empty items`.
- [ ] `./gradlew :kdiab-profiles:backend:check` and `./gradlew :kdiab-analyze:backend:check`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `GET /profiles` returns `{ items, page, size, totalCount }`
- [ ] Default page=0 size=50 works without query params
- [ ] kdiab-analyze still fetches active profile correctly
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec: paginated profiles endpoint with BFF compatibility

title: Patient selector displays truncated UUIDs instead of human-readable names
description: The doctor's patient selector (in kdiab-ui) shows raw UUID strings truncated to fit the UI, making it difficult to identify patients at a glance. Doctors managing multiple patients (e.g. dr_house with both sarah and dr_cameron with mike) need a display name or at minimum the username from the JWT/Keycloak profile — not a UUID. This is both a UX problem and a patient safety concern (wrong patient selected).
design:
# OpenSpec: Fix patient selector — display username instead of truncated UUID (kdiab-8xp)

## Goal
The doctor patient selector shows pid.slice(0, 8)... Add an allowed_patient_usernames Keycloak user attribute to each doctor so the frontend can display human-readable names.

## Context
- config/keycloak-realm.json line 57: dr_house has allowed_patients: [11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111] -> maps to sarah.
- Line 70: dr_cameron has allowed_patients: [22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222] -> maps to mike.
- All clients use oidc-usermodel-attribute-mapper for allowed_patients claim. Same pattern for new allowed_patient_usernames.
- kdiab-ui/src/api/tokenProvider.ts: parseAllowedPatientsFromToken() reads allowed_patients claim.
- kdiab-ui/src/App.tsx line 332: {pid.slice(0, 8)}... — the bug site.
- kdiab-ui/src/components/PatientBanner.tsx line 15: {patientId.slice(0, 8)}... — second bug site.
- There are 5 Keycloak clients in the root config. Mapper must be added to every client that has allowed_patients.
- kdiab-analyze/config/keycloak-realm.json also needs the mapper on kdiab-analyze-frontend client.

## Interface Changes
No API interface changes. Keycloak realm config + frontend changes only.

## Implementation Plan
1. `config/keycloak-realm.json` — Add allowed_patient_usernames to dr_house attributes: ["sarah"] and dr_cameron attributes: ["mike"]. For each client that has allowed_patients mapper, add sibling mapper with name=allowed_patient_usernames, protocolMapper=oidc-usermodel-attribute-mapper, user.attribute=allowed_patient_usernames, claim.name=allowed_patient_usernames, multivalued=true, access.token.claim=true.
2. `kdiab-analyze/config/keycloak-realm.json` — Same: add user attribute to doctor users and mapper to kdiab-analyze-frontend client.
3. `kdiab-ui/src/api/tokenProvider.ts` — Add parseAllowedPatientNamesFromToken(token: string): string[] that reads payload['allowed_patient_usernames'] claim.
4. `kdiab-ui/src/App.tsx` — Where allowedPatients is populated, also call parseAllowedPatientNamesFromToken(token). Build patientNames = new Map(allowedPatients.map((id, i) => [id, names[i] ?? id])). Pass to patient selector. Replace {pid.slice(0, 8)}... with {patientNames.get(pid) ?? pid.slice(0, 8) + '...'}.
5. `kdiab-ui/src/components/PatientBanner.tsx` — Accept patientName?: string prop. Replace {patientId.slice(0, 8)}... with {patientName ?? patientId.slice(0, 8) + '...'}.

## Test Plan
- [ ] npm run build in kdiab-ui/ — TypeScript compiles.
- [ ] Visual check: dr_house sees 'sarah' not UUID in selector.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Patient selector shows username (sarah, mike) not truncated UUID.
- [ ] PatientBanner shows username when viewing patient data.
- [ ] Fallback: if claim absent, shows full UUID (not truncated).
- [ ] npm run build passes.

## Risks & Assumptions
- allowed_patients and allowed_patient_usernames arrays must be parallel — Keycloak preserves insertion order.
- Check if kdiab-ui/config/keycloak-realm.json exists for standalone; update if so.
- patientNames map must be accessible in PatientBanner.tsx — use prop drilling or context.
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec

- kdiab-measures/settings.gradle.kts, kdiab-profiles/settings.gradle.kts, etc.: all define rootProject.name = "kdiab-<service>" with no subprojects

Documentation only.

   ./gradlew run                    # Run backend (requires external Postgres + Keycloak)

title: Add unit tests for AGP edge cases: single-bucket reading and negative glucose values
description: AnalyticsServiceTest has no test for AGP percentile calculation when a bucket has exactly one reading (all percentiles should equal that value) or when glucose data contains invalid negative values. These edge cases are clinically important — a single hourly reading could display misleading percentile ranges, and negative values indicate data corruption.
design:
# OpenSpec: Add AGP edge case tests — single-bucket reading and negative glucose filtering (kdiab-16f)

## Goal
AnalyticsServiceTest lacks two clinically important AGP edge cases. Add tests for single-reading buckets and add negative-value filtering to AnalyticsService with a corresponding test.

## Context
- AnalyticsServiceTest.kt lines 127-169: 4 AGP tests. No test for single reading or negative values.
- AnalyticsService.percentile() lines 138-145: for n=1 sorted list, all percentiles compute to the single value (correct but untested).
- AnalyticsService.getAgp() lines 66-96: byHour[hour].add(mgDl) — no filter for negative/zero values.
- AnalyticsService.fetchCgmReadings() (used by getHba1c()): same gap.
- Negative glucose (e.g. -1.0) indicates sensor error codes and must not contaminate percentiles.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes.

## Implementation Plan
1. `kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../application/service/AnalyticsService.kt`:
   - In getAgp(), after val mgDl = ... line, add: if (mgDl <= 0.0) return@forEach
   - In fetchCgmReadings() (used by getHba1c()), add the same guard after computing mgDl.
2. `kdiab-analyze/src/test/.../AnalyticsServiceTest.kt` — Add two tests after the existing AGP section:

Test 1: getAgp single reading in bucket — all percentiles equal that value
- coEvery returns listOf(cgmDto(120.0, "2024-01-15T06:00:00Z"))
- Assert bucket6.count == 1, p10 == 120.0, p25 == 120.0, median == 120.0, p75 == 120.0, p90 == 120.0 (all within absoluteTolerance 0.01)

Test 2: getAgp excludes negative and zero glucose values
- coEvery returns listOf(cgmDto(120.0, "2024-01-15T07:00:00Z"), cgmDto(-5.0, "2024-01-15T07:05:00Z"), cgmDto(0.0, "2024-01-15T07:10:00Z"))
- Assert bucket7.count == 1 and bucket7.median == 120.0 (absoluteTolerance 0.01)

## Test Plan
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check from kdiab-analyze/ — new tests pass, all existing tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Single-reading bucket test: all percentiles equal the single value.
- [ ] Negative/zero-value test: excluded from count and percentile calculation.
- [ ] Negative filter also in fetchCgmReadings (affects HbA1c).
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check passes.

## Risks & Assumptions
- The percentile() function already handles n=1 correctly — test just validates this.
- Filtering mgDl <= 0.0 (includes 0.0) is correct — zero is not a valid glucose reading.
- cgmDto(-5.0) works with the existing test helper (accepts any double).
close_reason: Negative/zero glucose filter added to AnalyticsService; single-bucket and exclusion tests added to AnalyticsServiceTest

title: Add audit trail for measure and treatment deletion
description: Doctors and admins can delete patient measures and treatments but there is no frontend indication or backend audit record of who deleted what or when. Unlike profile changes (which have kdiab-profiles audit logs), deletion of measures and treatments leaves no trace. Add deletion events to the AuditLogsTable in kdiab-measures and an equivalent in kdiab-treatments.
design:
# OpenSpec: Audit trail for measure and treatment deletion (kdiab-ipx)

## Goal
All deletion events (patient self-delete, doctor-for-patient, admin) are tracked with WHO, WHAT, and WHEN in the existing `audit_logs` tables. Currently only doctor reads/writes are audited via `auditIfDoctor`; patient and admin deletions leave no trace.

## Context
- `kdiab-measures/.../adapters/inbound/web/MeasureRoutes.kt` line 176: `auditIfDoctor(call, principal, targetUserId, "measures.delete", auditLogRepository)` — already audits doctor deletions.
- `kdiab-treatments/.../adapters/inbound/web/TreatmentRoutes.kt` line 171: `auditIfDoctor(call, principal, targetUserId, "treatments.delete", auditLogRepository)` — same.
- `audit_logs` schema: `id UUID, doctor_id UUID, patient_id UUID, action VARCHAR(100), occurred_at TIMESTAMP, ip_address VARCHAR, user_agent TEXT`. No `detail` column for recording deleted IDs.
- `auditIfDoctor` helper only fires when principal is a DOCTOR.

## Interface Changes
- Both `kdiab-measures/src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/001-ddl.yaml` and `kdiab-treatments/src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/001-ddl.yaml`:
  - New changeset: add `detail TEXT NULL` column to `audit_logs` table (stores serialized deleted IDs).

## Implementation Plan

### kdiab-measures
1. `001-ddl.yaml` — Add changeset `id: 005, author: javafreedom`: `addColumn tableName: audit_logs, column: detail type: TEXT nullable: true`.
2. `kdiab-measures/.../domain/model/AuditLog.kt` (or wherever AuditLog is defined) — Add `val detail: String? = null` field.
3. `kdiab-measures/.../infrastructure/persistence/ExposedAuditLogRepository.kt` — Map `detail` column in table object and in `save`/`toAuditLog()`.
4. `kdiab-measures/.../adapters/inbound/web/MeasureRoutes.kt` — Add a `auditDeletion(call, principal, targetUserId, ids, auditLogRepository)` helper that saves an audit log regardless of role (patient, doctor, admin). In `deleteMeasures`: replace/supplement `auditIfDoctor` with this new helper. Include `ids.joinToString(",")` as `detail`.

### kdiab-treatments (mirror steps 1-4)
5. `001-ddl.yaml` — same changeset.
6. AuditLog domain + repo — same additions.
7. `TreatmentRoutes.kt` — same `auditDeletion` helper for `deleteTreatments`.

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew :kdiab-measures:backend:check` and `./gradlew :kdiab-treatments:backend:check`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `audit_logs.detail` column exists in both services
- [ ] Patient self-deletion creates audit record with actor=patient userId in doctor_id field (self-audit)
- [ ] Deleted IDs serialized into `detail`
- [ ] `./gradlew check` passes

description: ProfileService catches raw org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.exceptions.ExposedSQLException directly in its create/update methods, leaking infrastructure exceptions through the application layer boundary. # OpenSpec: Wrap ExposedSQLException in domain exceptions in ProfileService (kdiab-1mm)

## Goal
ProfileService.activateProfile() and acceptProposedProfile() directly import and catch org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.exceptions.ExposedSQLException in the application service layer, violating hexagonal architecture. Infrastructure exceptions must be translated to domain exceptions at the repository (infrastructure) boundary, not in the application service.

## Context
- `kdiab-profiles/src/main/kotlin/.../application/service/ProfileService.kt` lines 69 and 95: catch ExposedSQLException and re-throw as ConflictException. This is correct behavior but at the wrong layer.
- `kdiab-profiles/src/main/kotlin/.../infrastructure/persistence/ExposedProfileRepository.kt`: performs the DB operations that can trigger the idx_profiles_user_active unique constraint. This is the correct place to catch ExposedSQLException.
- `kdiab-profiles/src/main/kotlin/.../plugins/StatusPages.kt` lines 70–90: already has a fallback ExposedSQLException handler for 23505 → 409. This fallback remains as safety net.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes.

## Implementation Plan
1. `kdiab-profiles/src/main/kotlin/.../infrastructure/persistence/ExposedProfileRepository.kt` — Read the file first to identify the method(s) that trigger the idx_profiles_user_active unique constraint. Wrap the DB write with:
   try { /* existing DB write */ } catch (e: org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.exceptions.ExposedSQLException) { val sqlState = e.cause?.let { (it as? java.sql.SQLException)?.sqlState }; if (sqlState == "23505") { throw ConflictException("Only one profile can be active at a time — deactivate the current active profile first.") }; throw e }
   Add import: org.javafreedom.kdiab.profiles.domain.exception.ConflictException
2. `kdiab-profiles/src/main/kotlin/.../application/service/ProfileService.kt` — Remove the catch (e: ExposedSQLException) blocks from activateProfile() and acceptProposedProfile(). Remove the import org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.exceptions.ExposedSQLException import.

- [ ] `./gradlew check` passes

title: Fix build.sh --clean: docker builder prune -af deletes build cache for pulled Docker Hub images
description:
## Problem

build.sh clean() runs:
  docker builder prune -af

This removes ALL build cache unconditionally, including cached layers for
pulled base images (postgres:15, nginx:alpine, quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:23.0,
dpage/pgadmin4:9.9.0). After --clean, the next docker compose up --build must
re-download all those layers from Docker Hub, even though --clean should only
reset locally-built kdiab artefacts.

Relevant code (build.sh lines 112-141):

  log "Removing local kdiab images"
  images=$(docker images --filter "reference=localhost/kdiab-*" -q ...)
  docker rmi $images ...

  log "Pruning Docker/Podman build cache"
  docker builder prune -af   ← removes everything, not just kdiab cache

## Expected behaviour

--clean should remove:
- Running containers (compose down -v)
- Locally built kdiab images (localhost/kdiab-*)
- Build cache entries belonging to kdiab images only

--clean should NOT remove:
- Pulled Docker Hub images (postgres, nginx, keycloak, pgadmin)
- Build cache entries for those Hub images

## Fix

Replace the aggressive docker builder prune -af with a targeted prune that
keeps cache entries still referenced by existing images. The --keep-storage
flag or filtering by label may help, but the simplest safe fix is to skip
builder prune entirely in --clean and optionally expose it as a separate
--purge flag:

  # Remove only dangling (unreferenced) build cache, not all cache
  docker builder prune -f 2>/dev/null || true   # dangling only, no -a

Or add a new --purge flag that runs the full prune for users who explicitly
want a complete reset including Hub image layers.
close_reason: Replaced prune -af with prune -f; dangling-only prune preserves pulled Docker Hub image layers

title: feat: kdiab-calc — insulin dose calculation service
description: Create a new stateless Kotlin/Ktor service kdiab-calc that computes a recommended insulin dose given: current blood glucose (value + unit), CGM trend (direction), target glucose (from active profile or default), insulin-sensitivity factor (ISF from profile), insulin-carb ratio (ICR from profile), active carbs (grams), and duration of action (from profile). The service calls kdiab-profiles to retrieve the user's active profile and returns a structured recommendation with breakdown (correction dose + carb dose + trend adjustment). No database — stateless computation only.
design:
# OpenSpec: kdiab-calc — Stateless Insulin Dose Calculator (kdiab-mzb)

## Goal
Create a new stateless Kotlin/Ktor microservice `kdiab-calc` that computes a recommended insulin dose. The caller provides current blood glucose, CGM trend, and grams of carbs to cover; the service fetches the user's active profile from kdiab-profiles to get ISF/ICR/target/duration-of-action, runs the calculation, and returns a structured breakdown. No database — pure computation.

---

## Context

### Reference: kdiab-analyze (stateless BFF pattern)
- No DB; does HTTP calls to upstream services with JWT forwarding
- `Application.kt`: creates `HttpClient(CIO)` with timeout/retry plugins; reads upstream URLs from `application.conf upstream { ... }`
- `ProfilesClient.kt`: `GET /api/v1/users/{userId}/profiles?page=0&size=50`, forwards JWT via `Authorization` header, returns list; throws `UpstreamException` on non-2xx
- `UpstreamException`: fields `service: String, statusCode: Int, message: String, responseBody: String?, url: String?`
- Port: kdiab-analyze uses 8080 internally. **kdiab-calc will use port 8086.**

### Profile segment structure (kdiab-profiles API)
The profiles endpoint returns Profile objects with nested segment arrays. The existing `ProfileDto` in analyze omits segments — kdiab-calc must define its own `ProfileDto` that includes them:
- `isf: List<IsfSegmentDto>` — each: `{ time: String ("HH:MM"), value: Double }` (mg/dL per unit)
- `icr: List<IcrSegmentDto>` — each: `{ time: String, value: Double }` (g/U)
- `targets: List<TargetSegmentDto>` — each: `{ time: String, low: Double, high: Double }`
- `durationOfAction: Int` (minutes)

### Dose calculation algorithm
Given inputs and profile values for the current time-of-day segment:
1. Convert `currentBg` to mg/dL if glucoseUnit = mmol/L (multiply by 18.0)
2. Look up active ISF, ICR, target for current time (or use `useProfileTime` if provided):
   - Segment lookup: find last segment where `segment.time <= localTime`; wrap: if none qualifies, use last segment
   - Target midpoint = (targetLow + targetHigh) / 2.0
3. **Correction dose** = (currentBgMgDl - targetMidpoint) / ISF — can be negative (BG below target)
4. **Carb dose** = carbsGrams / ICR
5. **Trend adjustment** (fixed values, not profile-dependent):
   - DOUBLE_UP → +2.0 U
   - SINGLE_UP → +1.0 U
   - FORTY_FIVE_UP → +0.5 U
   - FLAT → 0.0 U
   - FORTY_FIVE_DOWN → -0.5 U
   - SINGLE_DOWN → -1.0 U
   - DOUBLE_DOWN → -2.0 U
   - NONE / unknown → 0.0 U
6. **Total** = max(0.0, correctionDose + carbDose + trendAdjustment) — clamp to 0 minimum
7. Warnings:
   - If currentBg < 70 mg/dL: add "BG is hypoglycemic — no correction dose recommended; treat hypo first"
   - If correctionDose < 0 and carbDose > 0: add "BG is below target; carb dose only"
   - If total > 20.0: add "Calculated dose is unusually high — please verify inputs"

---

## Interface Changes

### New: kdiab-calc/api/openapi.yaml

`POST /users/{userId}/calc/dose` — compute recommended dose

Request body `DoseRequest`:
```
currentBg: number (required) — blood glucose value
glucoseUnit: string (required) — 'mg/dL' or 'mmol/L'
trend: string (required) — CGM trend: DOUBLE_UP | SINGLE_UP | FORTY_FIVE_UP | FLAT | FORTY_FIVE_DOWN | SINGLE_DOWN | DOUBLE_DOWN | NONE
carbsGrams: number (default 0) — grams of carbs to cover
useProfileTime: string (optional) — ISO-8601 datetime; if absent, use server clock
```

Response `DoseResponse`:
```
correctionDose: number
carbDose: number
trendAdjustment: number
totalRecommended: number (clamped to ≥ 0)
breakdown:
  currentBgMgDl: number
  targetBgMgDl: number
  isf: number
  icr: number
  trend: string
  carbsGrams: number
profileId: string (UUID)
warnings: string[]
```

### Root infrastructure
- `settings.gradle.kts` — add `includeBuild("kdiab-calc")`
- `build.gradle.kts` — add kdiab-calc to all aggregate tasks
- `docker-compose.yml` — add `calc-backend` service (no liquibase — stateless, no DB)
- `kdiab-ui/vite.config.ts` — add `/api/calc` proxy → localhost:8086
- Keycloak: add `calc-audience` mapper to `kdiab-analyze-frontend` client

---

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: kdiab-calc service

**Step 1: Gradle scaffold**
Copy from kdiab-analyze (not kdiab-measures — no DB deps needed):
- Gradle wrapper (gradlew, gradle/, gradle.properties)

```kotlin
class DoseCalculationService(private val profilesClient: ProfilesClient) {

    suspend fun calculateDose(
        userId: String,
        request: DoseRequest,
        authorization: String,
        correlationId: String,
    ): DoseResult {
        val profile = profilesClient.getActiveProfile(userId, authorization, correlationId)
            ?: throw ResourceNotFoundException("No active profile found for user")

        val now = if (request.useProfileTime != null)
            Instant.parse(request.useProfileTime)
        else Clock.System.now()
        val localTime = now.toLocalDateTime(TimeZone.UTC).time  // HH:MM lookup

        val bgMgDl = if (request.glucoseUnit.lowercase() == "mmol/l")
            request.currentBg * 18.0
        else request.currentBg

        val isf = lookupSegment(profile.isf, localTime) { it.value }
        val icr = lookupSegment(profile.icr, localTime) { it.value }
        val target = lookupSegment(profile.targets, localTime) { (it.low + it.high) / 2.0 }

        val correctionDose = (bgMgDl - target) / isf
        val carbDose = request.carbsGrams / icr
        val trendAdj = trendAdjustment(request.trend)
        val total = maxOf(0.0, correctionDose + carbDose + trendAdj)

        val warnings = buildList {
            if (bgMgDl < 70.0) add("BG is hypoglycemic — no correction dose recommended; treat hypo first")
            else if (correctionDose < 0 && carbDose > 0) add("BG is below target; carb dose only")
            if (total > 20.0) add("Calculated dose is unusually high — please verify inputs")
        }

        return DoseResult(
            correctionDose = round2(correctionDose),
            carbDose = round2(carbDose),
            trendAdjustment = trendAdj,
            totalRecommended = round2(total),
            breakdown = DoseBreakdown(bgMgDl, target, isf, icr, request.trend, request.carbsGrams),
            profileId = profile.id,
            warnings = warnings,
        )
    }

    private fun <T> lookupSegment(segments: List<T>, localTime: LocalTime, value: (T) -> Double): Double {
        if (segments.isEmpty()) throw BusinessValidationException("Profile has no segments")
        val time = LocalTime(localTime.hour, localTime.minute)
        // Find last segment whose time <= localTime; if none, use last (wraps midnight)
        val match = segments
            .map { it to parseLocalTime(segmentTime(it)) }
            .filter { (_, t) -> t <= time }
            .maxByOrNull { (_, t) -> t }
            ?: segments.last().let { it to parseLocalTime(segmentTime(it)) }
        return value(match.first)
    }

    private fun trendAdjustment(trend: CgmTrend) = when (trend) {
        CgmTrend.DOUBLE_UP -> 2.0
        CgmTrend.SINGLE_UP -> 1.0
        CgmTrend.FORTY_FIVE_UP -> 0.5
        CgmTrend.FLAT -> 0.0
        CgmTrend.FORTY_FIVE_DOWN -> -0.5
        CgmTrend.SINGLE_DOWN -> -1.0
        CgmTrend.DOUBLE_DOWN -> -2.0
        CgmTrend.NONE -> 0.0
    }

    private fun round2(v: Double) = Math.round(v * 100.0) / 100.0
}
```

Note: `segmentTime(it)` must extract the time string from the segment (use reflection or a common interface). Simpler: define separate private funs for each type that do the lookup directly without generics.

```kotlin
fun Route.calcRoutes(service: DoseCalculationService) {
    authenticate("auth-jwt") {
        post("/users/{userId}/calc/dose") {
            val principal = call.principal<UserPrincipal>()!!
            val userId = call.parameters["userId"] ?: throw BadRequestException("missing userId")
            checkReadAccess(principal, parseUuid(userId))
            val body = call.receive<DoseRequest>()
            val authorization = call.request.headers[HttpHeaders.Authorization] ?: ""
            val correlationId = call.request.headers["X-Correlation-ID"] ?: ""
            val result = service.calculateDose(userId, body, authorization, correlationId)
            call.respond(HttpStatusCode.OK, result.toApi())
        }
    }
}
```

design:
# OpenSpec: Treatment category color-coding in TimelineChart (kdiab-rua)

## Goal
`TimelineChart.tsx` currently renders all treatments as a single `<Scatter>` dataset with one color. Group treatment types into semantic categories (bolus, carbs, activity, device, other) and render each scatter point with a category-appropriate fill color using CSS custom properties.

## Context

**Current state:**
- `kdiab-ui/src/features/timeline/TimelineChart.tsx` — one `<Scatter>` for treatments with a single hard-coded fill. Treatment type is available on each data point as `type` string.
- `kdiab-analyze/api/openapi.yaml` `TimelineTreatmentType` enum: BOLUS, CORRECTION_BOLUS, COMBO_BOLUS, BASAL, TEMP_BASAL, CARBS, EXERCISE, NOTE, BG_CHECK, PUMP_SUSPEND, SITE_CHANGE, SENSOR_INSERT, INSULIN_CHANGE (+ HYPO_TREATMENT from kdiab-sa9).
- CSS custom properties for colors defined in `index.css` / theme file.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes.

## Implementation Plan

1. `kdiab-ui/src/features/timeline/TimelineChart.tsx` — define category map:
   BOLUS/CORRECTION_BOLUS/COMBO_BOLUS → `var(--color-bolus)`
   CARBS/HYPO_TREATMENT → `var(--color-carbs)`
   EXERCISE → `var(--color-activity)`
   BASAL/TEMP_BASAL → `var(--color-basal)`
   SITE_CHANGE/SENSOR_INSERT/INSULIN_CHANGE/PUMP_SUSPEND → `var(--color-device)`
   NOTE/BG_CHECK → `var(--color-other)`

2. In the `<Scatter>` for treatments, use `<Cell>` children to apply per-point color:
   `{treatments.map((entry, index) => <Cell key={index} fill={treatmentColor(entry.type)} />)}`

3. `kdiab-ui/src/index.css` (or theme file) — add CSS custom properties if missing: `--color-bolus`, `--color-carbs`, `--color-activity`, `--color-basal`, `--color-device`, `--color-other`. Use distinct accessible colors for both light and dark themes.

## Test Plan
- [ ] `npm run build` in `kdiab-ui` — TypeScript compiles clean
- [ ] `npm run lint` — no lint errors
- [ ] Manual: open Timeline with 30-day seed data — BOLUS points one color, CARBS another, device events a third

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each treatment scatter point colored by semantic category
- [ ] Color sourced from CSS custom properties (not hard-coded hex)
- [ ] TypeScript compiles clean; lint passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- Check whether `<Cell>` from recharts requires `isAnimationActive={false}` on the parent `<Scatter>` to avoid flicker.
- Verify `type` field on timeline treatment data points is `string` not generated enum type.

design:
# OpenSpec: Analysis range in profiles + wire BFF analytics (kdiab-86y)

## Goal
Add `analysis_low` and `analysis_high` nullable Double columns to the profiles table. These represent the broader clinical TIR thresholds (default 70 mg/dL / 180 mg/dL) distinct from `TargetSegment`. The BFF AnalyticsService replaces its hardcoded `TIR_LOW=70.0`/`TIR_HIGH=180.0` with values from the patient's active profile, falling back to defaults when null.

## Context
- `kdiab-profiles/.../domain/model/Profile.kt` — no `analysisLow`/`analysisHigh` fields.
- `kdiab-profiles/api/openapi.yaml` — Profile schema lacks these fields.
- `kdiab-profiles/src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/` — last changeset is 006. Add 007.
- `kdiab-analyze/.../application/service/AnalyticsService.kt` — `private const val TIR_LOW = 70.0`, `TIR_HIGH = 180.0`, `TIR_VERY_HIGH = 250.0`.
- `kdiab-analyze/.../adapters/outbound/http/ProfilesClient.kt` — `ProfileDto` has no `analysisLow`/`analysisHigh`.
- `kdiab-analyze/.../application/service/ProfilesService.kt` — exposes active profile to BffRoutes.
- `kdiab-analyze/.../adapters/inbound/web/BffRoutes.kt` — calls `analyticsService.getHba1c(userId, from, to, authorization, glucoseUnit, correlationId)`.
- Seed data: `config/postgres/02-seed-data.sql` — inserts profiles for sarah and mike (no analysis_low/analysis_high).

## Interface Changes
- `kdiab-profiles/api/openapi.yaml` — Add `analysisLow: number (nullable)` and `analysisHigh: number (nullable)` to `ProfileResponse` and `CreateProfileRequest`.
- New Liquibase changeset 007 in kdiab-profiles.

## Implementation Plan

### kdiab-profiles backend
1. `db/changelog/changes/007-analysis-range.yaml` — New changeset `id: 007, author: javafreedom`: `addColumn tableName: profiles, columns: [analysis_low DOUBLE nullable, analysis_high DOUBLE nullable]`.
2. `kdiab-profiles/api/openapi.yaml` — Add `analysisLow: { type: number, nullable: true }` and `analysisHigh: { type: number, nullable: true }` to ProfileResponse and CreateProfileRequest.
3. `kdiab-profiles/.../domain/model/Profile.kt` — Add `val analysisLow: Double? = null, val analysisHigh: Double? = null`.
4. `kdiab-profiles/.../infrastructure/persistence/ExposedProfileRepository.kt` — Add `analysis_low` and `analysis_high` to `ProfilesTable`. Map in `toProfile()`. Write in `insert`/`update`.
5. `kdiab-profiles/.../adapters/inbound/web/ProfileMapper.kt` — Include in `toApi()` and `toDomain()`.
6. `config/postgres/02-seed-data.sql` — Add `analysis_low = 70.0, analysis_high = 180.0` to sarah and mike profile inserts.

### kdiab-analyze BFF
7. `kdiab-analyze/.../adapters/outbound/http/ProfilesClient.kt` — Add `val analysisLow: Double? = null, val analysisHigh: Double? = null` to `ProfileDto`.
8. `kdiab-analyze/.../application/service/AnalyticsService.kt` — Add `tirLow: Double = TIR_LOW` and `tirHigh: Double = TIR_HIGH` parameters to `getHba1c` and `getAgp`. Use these params in `computeTir` and AGP bucket logic instead of the constants. Keep the constants as defaults.
9. `kdiab-analyze/.../adapters/inbound/web/BffRoutes.kt` — Before calling `analyticsService.getHba1c`, fetch active profile via `profilesService.getActiveProfile(userId, authorization, correlationId)`. Extract `tirLow = profile?.analysisLow ?: 70.0` and `tirHigh = profile?.analysisHigh ?: 180.0`. Pass these to `getHba1c` and `getAgp`.
10. `kdiab-analyze/.../application/service/ProfilesService.kt` — Expose `getActiveProfile(userId, authorization, correlationId): ProfileDto?` that calls `profilesClient.getProfiles(...)` and filters for status == "ACTIVE".

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew :kdiab-profiles:backend:integrationTest` — schema migration runs
- [ ] `./gradlew :kdiab-analyze:backend:check` — AnalyticsService tests pass with custom thresholds
- [ ] `./gradlew :kdiab-profiles:backend:check`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ProfileResponse includes analysisLow/analysisHigh
- [ ] AnalyticsService uses profile analysis range when available
- [ ] Falls back to 70/180 when profile null or fields null

# OpenSpec: Unit tests for InsulinService (kdiab-558)

## Goal
`InsulinService` in kdiab-profiles has no unit tests. Add `InsulinServiceTest.kt` with 7 tests covering all four service methods (findAll, create, update, delete), including the `ExposedSQLException → ConflictException` translation that is the only non-trivial business logic in the service.

## Context

**Current state:**
- `kdiab-profiles/src/main/kotlin/…/application/service/InsulinService.kt` — thin CRUD delegate to `InsulinRepository`. `create()` and `update()` catch `ExposedSQLException` (unique constraint violation on insulin name) and rethrow as `ConflictException`.
- `kdiab-profiles/src/test/kotlin/…/application/service/ProfileServiceTest.kt` — uses MockK with `val profileRepository = mockk<ProfileRepository>()` pattern. Follow this exactly.
- `InsulinRepository` interface is in `domain/repository/InsulinRepository.kt`.
- No existing test for `InsulinService`.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes — tests only.

## Implementation Plan

1. **`kdiab-profiles/src/test/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/profiles/application/service/InsulinServiceTest.kt`** (new)
   MockK-based JUnit5 tests:
   - `findAll — empty repository returns empty list`
   - `findAll — returns all insulins from repository`
   - `create — returns saved insulin`
   - `create — duplicate name throws ConflictException`: ExposedSQLException → ConflictException
   - `update — returns updated insulin`
   - `update — duplicate name throws ConflictException`: ExposedSQLException → ConflictException
   - `delete — delegates to repository deleteById`: coVerify called

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:test --no-daemon` from `kdiab-profiles/` — 7 new tests pass
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check --no-daemon` — Kover ≥ 80%, Detekt clean

- [ ] `ExposedSQLException → ConflictException` translation tested for both `create` and `update`
- [ ] No new Detekt violations

## Risks & Assumptions

- `Insulin` domain model fields: check `domain/model/` before writing the test fixture.

# OpenSpec: Add un-archive functionality for measures and treatments (kdiab-sak)

## Goal
Patients can archive but not undo accidental archives. Add POST /unarchive endpoints and a "Show Archived" toggle in MeasureList/TreatmentList with an Unarchive button per row.

## Context
- Archive pattern: POST /users/{userId}/measures/archive body { measureIds } -> UPDATE status=ARCHIVED. Mirror with status=ACTIVE.
- kdiab-ui/src/api/measuresApi.ts — listMeasures has no status param; archiveMeasures exists.
- kdiab-ui/src/features/measures/MeasureList.tsx — no show-archived toggle, no unarchive button.
- Check if kdiab-measures GET /measures already accepts status query param in openapi.yaml before adding it.

## Interface Changes
- kdiab-measures/api/openapi.yaml: Add POST /users/{userId}/measures/unarchive (body: BulkMeasureRequest). Add optional status query param (default ACTIVE) to GET /users/{userId}/measures if not already present.
- kdiab-treatments/api/openapi.yaml: Mirror: POST /users/{userId}/treatments/unarchive. Add status param to GET if not present.
- No DB changes.

## Implementation Plan

### kdiab-measures backend
1. kdiab-measures/api/openapi.yaml — Add POST /unarchive operation. Add optional status query param to list endpoint if absent.
2. kdiab-measures/.../domain/repository/MeasureRepository.kt — Add suspend fun unarchive(ids: List<Uuid>, userId: Uuid).
3. kdiab-measures/.../infrastructure/persistence/ExposedMeasureRepository.kt — unarchive: MeasuresTable.update(...) { it[status] = MeasureStatus.ACTIVE.name }. Update findByUserId to accept optional status: MeasureStatus? = MeasureStatus.ACTIVE.
4. kdiab-measures/.../application/service/MeasureService.kt — Add unarchiveMeasures(ids, userId). Update getMeasures to pass status through.
5. kdiab-measures/.../adapters/inbound/web/MeasureRoutes.kt — Add unarchiveMeasures handler (same access control as archive). Update list handler to read optional status query param.

### kdiab-treatments backend (mirror)
6-10. Same steps for treatments stack.

### kdiab-ui
11. kdiab-ui/src/api/measuresApi.ts — listMeasures gains optional status?: string param. Add unarchiveMeasures.
12. kdiab-ui/src/api/treatmentsApi.ts — Same: listTreatments gains status?, add unarchiveTreatments.
13. kdiab-ui/src/features/measures/MeasureList.tsx — Add [showArchived, setShowArchived] toggle button. When true, pass status='ARCHIVED' to listMeasures query. Add Unarchive button per row (only when showArchived=true).
14. kdiab-ui/src/features/treatments/TreatmentList.tsx — Same.

## Test Plan
- [ ] Integration: POST unarchive -> status changes to ACTIVE
- [ ] Integration: GET measures with status=ARCHIVED returns only archived rows
- [ ] ./gradlew check for both services
- [ ] npm run build

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] POST /unarchive sets status ACTIVE
- [ ] GET /measures?status=ARCHIVED returns archived measures
- [ ] Show Archived toggle visible in UI; Unarchive button appears for archived rows
- [ ] npm run build passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- kdiab-sak agent must run AFTER kdiab-bfl is merged to main (shared files: MeasureList.tsx, TreatmentList.tsx, measuresApi.ts, treatmentsApi.ts).
- Check GET /measures openapi.yaml for existing status param before adding it.
close_reason: POST /unarchive endpoints added to both services. Show Archived toggle and Unarchive button added to MeasureList and TreatmentList. All quality gates pass.

# OpenSpec: Overlay profile change events on BFF timeline chart (kdiab-u2g)

## Goal
The kdiab-ui Timeline chart shows CGM and BGM glucose readings over time but gives no indication of when a patient's insulin pump profile changed. Adding vertical reference lines labelled "Profile changed" at each profile activation date allows doctors to visually correlate profile changes with glucose control improvements. The validFrom timestamp is already returned by the existing /profiles/active endpoint — this is a frontend-only change.

## Context

Current state:
- kdiab-ui/src/features/timeline/TimelineView.tsx — queries analyzeApi.getTimeline() only; renders TimelineChart without any profile marker data.
- kdiab-ui/src/features/timeline/TimelineChart.tsx — Recharts ComposedChart with a Line for CGM, Scatter for BGM, Scatter for treatments, and two ReferenceLine components at 70 and 180 mg/dL. No profile change markers.
- kdiab-ui/src/features/analytics/AnalyticsView.tsx — already queries analyzeApi.getActiveProfiles(userId, from, to). Profile data is cached by React Query and will not trigger duplicate network requests if the same query key is used in TimelineView.tsx.
- kdiab-analyze domain model Analytics.kt — ProfileSummary already has validFrom: String? (ISO-8601 timestamp of when the profile became active/archived).
- kdiab-analyze api/openapi.yaml — ProfileSummary already has validFrom field. No schema changes required.

Recharts API: <ReferenceLine x={ms} stroke="color" strokeDasharray="4 2" label="…" /> where x is a timestamp in ms (same unit as the chart's ts x-axis data key).

## Interface Changes
No interface changes — the validFrom field already exists in ProfileSummary.

## Implementation Plan

1. kdiab-ui/src/features/timeline/TimelineView.tsx — Add a second React Query call for analyzeApi.getActiveProfiles(userId, from, to). Extract validFrom timestamps from profiles whose validFrom is non-null and within [from, to]. Convert to epoch ms and pass as profileChangeDates: number[] to TimelineChart.

2. kdiab-ui/src/features/timeline/TimelineChart.tsx — Add optional prop profileChangeDates?: number[] to the component. Inside the ComposedChart, after the existing 70/180 ReferenceLine components, render one per profile change date.

3. kdiab-ui/src/i18n/locales/en.json — Add "profileChanged": "Profile changed" inside the "timeline" section.

4. kdiab-ui/src/i18n/locales/de.json — Add "profileChanged": "Profil geändert" inside the "timeline" section.

## Test Plan
- [ ] npm run build in kdiab-ui — TypeScript compile clean, no errors
- [ ] npm run lint — no new lint errors

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Timeline chart renders a dotted vertical reference line for each profile activation date within the selected timeframe
- [ ] Lines are labelled "Profile changed" (or locale equivalent)
- [ ] TypeScript compiles clean; npm run lint passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- validFrom may be null for old profiles — filter null values before rendering.
- The chart x-axis unit is epoch ms; new Date(validFrom).getTime() converts correctly.
close_reason: Implemented: profile change ReferenceLine markers added to TimelineChart

title: Fix HttpClient not closed on BFF shutdown
description: BFF Application.kt creates an HttpClient(CIO) at startup but never closes it on application shutdown. When the Ktor application stops (SIGTERM in container), CIO connection pool is not drained. Fix: subscribe to the ApplicationStopping monitor event and call httpClient.close(): environment.monitor.subscribe(ApplicationStopping) { httpClient.close() }. This ensures clean connection teardown during rolling deployments and avoids connection pool leaks in repeated test runs.
close_reason: Implemented per spec

title: Fix AGP empty-bucket percentiles: return null instead of 0.0 when no readings
description: AnalyticsService.getAgp() returns AgpHourlyData(p10=0.0, p25=0.0, ..., count=0) for hours with no CGM readings. This is ambiguous: 0.0 is a valid glucose reading (severe hypoglycaemia below detectable range). The frontend cannot distinguish 'no data at 3am' from 'median glucose at 3am is 0 mg/dL'. Fix: change AgpHourlyData percentile fields to Double? (nullable) and return null for empty buckets. Update the OpenAPI schema and frontend AgpChart to treat null as 'no data' (render gap in the chart).
close_reason: Implemented per spec

description: TimeInRangeBar.tsx shows 4 coloured zones (Below/In Range/Above/High) but no clinical context. A patient does not know that 'Below < 70' means hypoglycaemia risk or that the TIR target is > 70% in range. Add: (1) a help section below the bar explaining each zone and the clinical target, (2) aria-describedby attributes on each zone segment linking to the explanation for screen readers, (3) a 'Your TIR goal: > 70% in range' indicator with colour coding (green if met, orange if not).

# OpenSpec: TIR goal indicator and clinical explanations (kdiab-urb)

## Goal
The Time In Range bar in the analytics view shows coloured zones but gives no clinical target guidance. Add a visual indicator showing whether the patient meets the clinical TIR goal (>70% in-range), style the indicator green (meets) or orange (below), add a dl/dt/dd clinical explanation block below the bar, and add aria-describedby on the zone segments for accessibility.

## Context

**Current state:**
- `kdiab-ui/src/features/analytics/TimeInRangeBar.tsx` — renders coloured zone segments proportional to `tir.inRangePercent`, `tir.lowPercent`, `tir.highPercent`. No goal indicator.
- `kdiab-analyze/api/openapi.yaml` `TirSummary` schema already includes `inRangePercent`.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes — frontend only.

## Implementation Plan

1. `kdiab-ui/src/features/analytics/TimeInRangeBar.tsx` — compute `meetsGoal = tir.inRangePercent >= 70`. Render goal indicator div with class `meets-goal` or `below-goal` and aria-label.

2. Add `aria-describedby` to each zone segment div pointing to a hidden description element naming the zone (e.g. "In Range: 72%").

3. Add clinical explanation block below the bar using dl/dt/dd elements with i18n keys.

4. `kdiab-ui/src/index.css` — add `.tir-goal-indicator.meets-goal { color: var(--color-success) }` and `.tir-goal-indicator.below-goal { color: var(--color-warning) }`.

5. `kdiab-ui/src/i18n/locales/en.json` — inside `analytics` section add 8 keys: `tirGoalMet`, `tirGoalNotMet`, `tirTarget`, `tirTargetValue` ('>70% in range (clinical target)'), `tirInRange`, `tirLow`, `tirHigh`, `tirVeryLow`.

6. `kdiab-ui/src/i18n/locales/de.json` — add German equivalents.

## Test Plan
- [ ] `npm run build` — TypeScript clean
- [ ] `npm run lint` — no lint errors
- [ ] Manual: sarah's analytics view — green 'Goal met' if ≥70%, orange 'Below goal' if not

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Goal indicator visible, green/orange based on `inRangePercent >= 70`
- [ ] Clinical explanation block renders below the bar
- [ ] `aria-describedby` present on zone segments
- [ ] TypeScript compiles clean; lint passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- `--color-success` and `--color-warning` CSS variables must exist in the theme or be added.
- TIR goal of 70% is the international consensus target (Battelino et al. 2019) — safe to hard-code.
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec in isolated worktree

title: Fix N+1 query in ProfileService.assertUniqueNameForUser
description: ProfileService.assertUniqueNameForUser() calls profileRepository.findAllByUserId(userId) to load all profiles, then filters in memory with .any { it.name == name }. For a user with many profiles this loads all of them from the database. Add a repository method existsByUserIdAndName(userId, name, excludeId) that executes a SQL EXISTS query instead. This changes the N+1 scan (all profiles) to a single O(1) indexed lookup.
close_reason: Implemented per spec

title: Validate BFF date-range params: from must precede to and both must be valid ISO-8601
description: BffRoutes.kt requireParam() only checks that from and to exist (not null). It does not validate that they are valid ISO-8601 Instant strings or that from < to. If from is an invalid string, Instant.parse() in TimelineService throws DateTimeParseException which becomes an unhandled 500. If from > to, all services return empty results with no error. Fix: parse both params in BffRoutes with runCatching and throw BusinessValidationException on parse failure or when from >= to.
close_reason: Implemented per spec

title: Remove plaintext secret defaults from docker-compose.yml and add .env.example
description: docker-compose.yml has hardcoded fallback defaults: POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-password and KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin. If a developer runs docker compose up without a .env file, the database runs with a known weak password. Remove all :-default fallbacks from secret variables. Create .env.example at repo root with placeholder values (POSTGRES_PASSWORD=changeme). Add .env to .gitignore. Document: 'cp .env.example .env and set real values before first run' in how-to-run.adoc.
close_reason: Implemented and committed

title: Add readiness probe /readyz endpoint separate from liveness /healthz
description: All services expose /healthz for liveness (is the process running?). There is no separate readiness probe (is the service ready to accept traffic?). A service can be alive but not ready (database connection pool not initialised, JWKS not fetched yet). The docker-compose depends_on should use condition: service_healthy on the readiness probe. Add a /readyz endpoint to all four backends that checks: (1) database connection can be obtained from the pool, (2) returns 200 if ready, 503 if not. Update docker-compose depends_on conditions.
close_reason: Implemented per spec

title: Add resource limits (memory, CPU) to all services in docker-compose.yml
description: No service in docker-compose.yml has deploy.resources.limits configured. A single runaway service can OOM-kill the host. Add deploy.resources.limits.memory and cpus to every service. Recommended: backend services 512M / 1.0 CPU each; bff-backend 256M / 0.5 CPU; postgres 1G / 2.0 CPU; keycloak 512M / 1.0 CPU; frontend nginx services 64M / 0.25 CPU. Also add reservations at half the limits. This is a prerequisite for Kubernetes deployment.
close_reason: Implemented and committed

title: Add composite indexes (user_id, timestamp) to measures and treatments tables
description: The measures and treatments tables have separate indexes on user_id, type, and measured_at/treated_at individually. All list queries filter by (user_id, date range) but no composite index exists for this pattern. For a user with years of CGM data, the query must scan all user rows and then filter by date. Add Liquibase changesets creating: INDEX idx_measures_user_time ON measures(user_id, measured_at DESC) and INDEX idx_treatments_user_time ON treatments(user_id, treated_at DESC). Mark with dbms: postgresql.
close_reason: Implemented per spec

title: Add from/to date filter params to measures and treatments list endpoints
description: The BFF TimelineService fetches ALL measures and ALL treatments for a user and filters in memory by timeframe. For a user with years of data this is slow and wastes bandwidth. The measures and treatments list endpoints do not support from/to query parameters. Add optional from and to ISO-8601 query parameters to GET /users/{userId}/measures and GET /users/{userId}/treatments. Apply as WHERE measured_at BETWEEN from AND to in Exposed queries. Update OpenAPI specs. The BFF should then pass its from/to params through to both services.

# OpenSpec: Add from/to query params to measures and treatments list endpoints (kdiab-wrt)

## Goal
The measures and treatments list endpoints currently return all records for a user. Add optional `from` and `to` ISO-8601 timestamp query parameters for server-side date filtering. The BFF (kdiab-analyze) must also forward these params to the upstream services.

## Context

**Current state:**
- `MeasureRepository.findByUserId(userId)` and `TreatmentRepository.findByUserId(userId)` — no date range parameters.
- Route handlers in `MeasureRoutes.kt` and `TreatmentRoutes.kt` — no from/to extraction.
- `kdiab-analyze/.../MeasuresClient.kt` and `TreatmentsClient.kt` — build URLs with userId only.
- Both OpenAPI specs have the list endpoint but no from/to query params defined.

## Interface Changes
`kdiab-measures/api/openapi.yaml` and `kdiab-treatments/api/openapi.yaml`: add optional `from` and `to` query params (type: string, format: date-time) to the list endpoints.

## Implementation Plan

**kdiab-measures:**
1. `domain/repository/MeasureRepository.kt` — add `from: Instant? = null, to: Instant? = null` to `findByUserId`.
2. `infrastructure/persistence/ExposedMeasureRepository.kt` — add `andWhere` clauses for measuredAt >= from and measuredAt <= to.
3. `application/service/MeasureService.kt` — propagate from/to to repository.
4. `adapters/inbound/web/MeasureRoutes.kt` — extract from/to from query params with `Instant.parse()`.
5. `kdiab-measures/api/openapi.yaml` — add from/to params to list endpoint.

**kdiab-treatments:** Mirror steps 1–5 for Treatment equivalents.

**kdiab-analyze:**
6. `adapters/outbound/http/MeasuresClient.kt` — add from/to params; append to URL if non-null.
7. `adapters/outbound/http/TreatmentsClient.kt` — same.
8. `application/service/TimelineService.kt` — pass from/to through to both clients.

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check --no-daemon` in `kdiab-measures/` — existing tests pass; Detekt clean
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check --no-daemon` in `kdiab-treatments/` — same
- [ ] `./gradlew :check --no-daemon` in `kdiab-analyze/` — BFF quality gate green
- [ ] Manual: GET /measures?from=2024-01-01T00:00:00Z&to=2024-01-02T00:00:00Z returns only measures in range

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] from/to params filter results at the DB level (not post-fetch)
- [ ] Absent params return all records (backwards compatible)

# OpenSpec: Squash Liquibase changelogs (kdiab-ppws)

## Goal
Collapse all incremental Liquibase changesets into a single `001-initial-schema.yaml` per service (representing the final schema as if it was always there), author javafreedom. No released version exists so existing DBs can be recreated.

## Context

### kdiab-measures
- `src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/001-ddl.yaml` — single file with changesets 001 (measures table), 002-003 (indexes), 004 (audit_logs table + indexes).
- New changeset 005 (audit_logs.detail) will be added by kdiab-ipx — **include it here** if merged after kdiab-ipx, otherwise omit.
- Root: `db.changelog-root.yaml`.

### kdiab-treatments
- `src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/001-ddl.yaml` — changesets 001 (treatments table), 002-004 (indexes), 005+ (status column, audit_logs).
- Read full file before squashing.
- Root: `db.changelog-root.yaml`.

### kdiab-profiles
- Six files: 001-initial-schema.yaml (profiles, profile_statuses, insulins + pg/h2 indexes), 002-initial-data.yaml (insulin seed data), 003-audit-schema.yaml (audit_logs), 004-profile-timestamps.yaml (activated_at, archived_at on profile_statuses), 005-proposal-reason.yaml (proposal_reason on profiles), 006-created-by-rejection-reason.yaml (created_by, rejection_reason on profiles).
- Root: `db.changelog-master.yaml`.

## Implementation Plan

### kdiab-measures
1. Read the full `001-ddl.yaml`. Create a NEW `001-ddl.yaml` with a single changeset `id: 001, author: javafreedom` containing ALL columns and indexes inline (measures table + all indexes + audit_logs table + all audit indexes). This represents the final state.
2. `db.changelog-root.yaml` — verify it still references `changes/001-ddl.yaml` (no change needed if already correct).

### kdiab-treatments
3. Read the full `001-ddl.yaml`. Create NEW `001-ddl.yaml` with single changeset `id: 001, author: javafreedom` containing all tables (treatments, status column if it exists, audit_logs) and all indexes.
4. `db.changelog-root.yaml` — verify.

### kdiab-profiles
5. Create NEW `001-initial-schema.yaml` with single changeset `id: 001, author: javafreedom` containing ALL final-state DDL:
   - profiles table with ALL columns (including: proposal_reason TEXT NULL, created_by UUID NULL, rejection_reason TEXT NULL)
   - profile_statuses table with ALL columns (including: activated_at, archived_at timestamps NULL)
   - insulins table
   - PostgreSQL partial unique index (dbms: postgresql)
   - H2 workaround generated column + index (dbms: h2)
   - audit_logs table + indexes
6. Keep `002-initial-data.yaml` as-is (it holds insulin seed inserts, which are data not schema).
7. Delete files: 003-audit-schema.yaml, 004-profile-timestamps.yaml, 005-proposal-reason.yaml, 006-created-by-rejection-reason.yaml.
8. `db.changelog-master.yaml` — update `include` list to reference only `001-initial-schema.yaml` and `002-initial-data.yaml`.

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew :kdiab-measures:backend:integrationTest` — H2 starts from clean schema
- [ ] `./gradlew :kdiab-treatments:backend:integrationTest`
- [ ] `./gradlew :kdiab-profiles:backend:integrationTest`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each service has ≤2 changelog files after squash
- [ ] Integration tests pass (H2 recreates from squashed schema)
- [ ] All squashed changesets have `author: javafreedom`
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec: single-changeset changelogs per service

design:
# OpenSpec: Add glucose unit validation warning (kdiab-7b6)

## Goal
AnalyticsService uses the JWT `glucoseUnit` claim for all CGM conversions, but each measure DTO already carries `data["unit"]`. When a patient switches units, measures stored in the old unit are silently mis-converted. Fix: read each measure's own `data["unit"]` for conversion and warn when the dominant storage unit differs from the JWT claim.

## Context
- `kdiab-analyze/.../application/service/AnalyticsService.kt`
  - `fetchCgmReadings`: `val mgDl = if (glucoseUnit == "mmol/L") sgv * MMOL_TO_MGDL else sgv` — uses JWT claim
  - `getAgp`: same pattern
  - Constant `MMOL_TO_MGDL = 18.0` already defined
- `kdiab-analyze/.../application/service/AnalyticsServiceTest.kt` — MockK, existing HbA1c tests

## Interface Changes
No API changes. Internal logic and warning messages only.

## Implementation Plan
1. `AnalyticsService.kt` — In `fetchCgmReadings`:
   - Extract storage unit per measure: `val storageUnit = dto.data["unit"]?.toString() ?: glucoseUnit`
   - Convert using storage unit: `val mgDl = if (storageUnit.lowercase() == "mmol/l") sgv * MMOL_TO_MGDL else sgv`
   - Count mismatches (storageUnit != glucoseUnit). After processing all measures, if mismatch count > 0, append warning: "Unit mismatch detected: $count readings stored in a different unit than your profile setting. Values may be inaccurate." Return from getHba1c with the extra warning.
   - Refactor `fetchCgmReadings` to return a data class `CgmFetchResult(readings: List<Double>, mismatchCount: Int)` so warnings can propagate.
2. `AnalyticsService.kt` — Apply same fix to `getAgp` using storage unit for each measure.
3. `AnalyticsServiceTest.kt` — Add tests:
   - `measures stored in mmol/L with glucoseUnit=mg/dL are correctly converted to mg/dL`: provide two measures with unit=mmol/L and glucoseUnit=mg/dL; assert mean is ~130 mg/dL (7.2 * 18) and warning is present.
   - `measures with matching unit produce no unit-mismatch warning`.

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit tests in AnalyticsServiceTest.kt
- [ ] `./gradlew :kdiab-analyze:backend:check`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each measure is converted using its own `data["unit"]`, not the JWT claim
- [ ] Warning added to HbA1c result when mismatch detected
- [ ] Tests green
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec: per-measure unit conversion with mismatch warning

title: Replace build.sh with a root Gradle composite build task
description: build.sh is a bash script that orchestrates building all 4 services and the frontends. It duplicates logic that could live in the root Gradle composite build (ADR-003). design:
# OpenSpec: Replace build.sh with root Gradle composite build tasks (kdiab-0my)

## Goal
`build.sh` is a 215-line Bash script that orchestrates Gradle builds for 4 backend services and an `npm ci && npm run build` for the `kdiab-ui` gateway frontend. The root `build.gradle.kts` already declares aggregate tasks (`build`, `check`, `clean`) that reference `:buildAll`, `:checkAll`, `:cleanAll` in each service — but those per-service tasks don't exist yet, so the aggregate tasks are broken. This issue implements the missing tasks, adds an npm Exec wrapper, and removes the Bash script entirely, giving developers a single `./gradlew` entry point for all monorepo builds.

## Context

**Root composite build:**
- `settings.gradle.kts` — includeBuild for all 4 services; no kdiab-ui (pure npm, no Gradle).
- `build.gradle.kts` — declares `build` (→ `:buildAll`), `check` (→ `:checkAll`), `clean` (→ `:cleanAll`) on each included build. These tasks currently fail because the per-service targets don't exist.

**build.sh — what it currently does:**
- Default: runs `./gradlew :build --no-daemon` in each service dir (in parallel via &) + npm build for kdiab-ui
- `--check`: same but `./gradlew :check`
- `--backend-only`: skip frontend
- `--frontend-only`: skip Gradle
- `--docker`: runs docker compose build for 8 images
- `--clean`: docker compose down -v + remove images + prune cache
- `--no-parallel`: sequential builds

**Per-service Gradle tasks (exist already):**
- `:build`, `:check` (= test + integrationTest + e2eTest + detekt + kover), `:clean`
- Each service build.gradle.kts is at the service root

**kdiab-ui:** pure npm/Vite project at `kdiab-ui/`. No build.gradle.kts. Not in composite build.

## Interface Changes
Command-line interface changes:

| Old (build.sh) | New (./gradlew) |
|---|---|
| `./build.sh` | `./gradlew build` |
| `./build.sh --check` | `./gradlew check` |
| `./build.sh --backend-only` | `./gradlew buildBackends` |

# OpenSpec: Refactor measures and treatments Liquibase changelogs to includes-based structure (kdiab-7xj)

## Goal
`kdiab-measures` and `kdiab-treatments` both define all changesets inline in a single `db.changelog-root.yaml` file. Extract the changesets into a `changes/001-ddl.yaml` file and replace the root file with an explicit `include` directive. Add `logicalFilePath` to the extracted file to prevent Liquibase checksum mismatches.

## Context

**Current state:**
- `kdiab-measures/src/main/resources/db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml` — flat file with inline changesets for the measures table.
- `kdiab-treatments/src/main/resources/db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml` — flat file with inline changesets for the treatments table (including a `dbms: postgresql` changeset for an index).
- `kdiab-profiles` already uses the includes pattern: `db.changelog-master.yaml` includes files from `changes/` — follow this exact pattern.

**Critical:** Liquibase identifies changesets by (filename, id, author) triple. Moving changesets to a new file changes the filename unless `logicalFilePath` is set.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes — Liquibase file reorganisation only.

## Implementation Plan

**kdiab-measures:**
1. Create `kdiab-measures/src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/001-ddl.yaml` — copy all changesets from the current root file.
2. Add `logicalFilePath: db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml` at the top of `changes/001-ddl.yaml`.
3. Replace `db.changelog-root.yaml` with includes-only form pointing to `db/changelog/changes/001-ddl.yaml`.

**kdiab-treatments:**
4. Create `kdiab-treatments/src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/001-ddl.yaml` — same extraction including the dbms:postgresql changeset.
5. Add `logicalFilePath: db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml` to `changes/001-ddl.yaml`.
6. Replace `db.changelog-root.yaml` with includes-only form.

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check --no-daemon` in `kdiab-measures/` — integration tests (H2 + Liquibase) pass
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check --no-daemon` in `kdiab-treatments/` — same
- [ ] `docker compose up --build` from repo root — Liquibase init containers complete without errors

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Both services' Liquibase migration succeeds against a fresh DB
- [ ] Both services' Liquibase migration succeeds against an existing DB (no duplicate changeset errors)
- [ ] Quality gates pass; `logicalFilePath` present in both extracted files

## Risks & Assumptions
- `logicalFilePath` must match original file path in DATABASECHANGELOG table exactly: `db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml` (relative, no leading slash).
- The `dbms: postgresql` changeset in treatments is skipped by H2 — safe for integration tests.
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec: extracted inline changesets to changes/001-ddl.yaml with logicalFilePath in both kdiab-measures and kdiab-treatments. Integration tests and detekt pass.

design:
# OpenSpec: Add upstream request latency logging to BFF HTTP clients (kdiab-8su)

## Goal
MeasuresClient, TreatmentsClient, and ProfilesClient log fetch start/end at debug level but record no timing. Operators cannot detect slow upstreams from logs. Wrap each httpClient.get() call with System.currentTimeMillis() timing and emit an INFO log with round-trip ms and HTTP status code. Log at WARN level on non-success responses.

## Context
All three clients are in kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/adapters/outbound/http/:
- MeasuresClient.kt: paginated loop; httpClient.get() at line 57 inside while loop; debug log at line 75
- TreatmentsClient.kt: single httpClient.get() at line 36; debug log at line 35
- ProfilesClient.kt: single httpClient.get() at line 30; debug log at line 29
- Logger: private val logger = KotlinLogging.logger {} in all three files

## Interface Changes
No interface changes.

## Implementation Plan

1. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/outbound/http/TreatmentsClient.kt — Wrap the httpClient.get() call:
   val start = System.currentTimeMillis()
   val response = httpClient.get(...) { ... }
   val ms = System.currentTimeMillis() - start
   if (response.status.isSuccess()) {
       logger.info { "Fetched treatments from upstream in ${ms}ms [status=${response.status.value}]" }
   } else {
       logger.warn { "Upstream treatments returned ${response.status.value} in ${ms}ms" }
       throw UpstreamException(...)
   }
   Remove the existing pre-request debug log.

2. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/outbound/http/ProfilesClient.kt — Same pattern around the httpClient.get() at line 30.

3. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/outbound/http/MeasuresClient.kt — Apply timing around each page request inside the loop. Track per-page timing and log per page. Also emit a summary log after the loop with total items, total pages, total elapsed time.

## Test Plan
- [ ] ./gradlew :check --no-daemon from kdiab-analyze/ — Detekt + Kover + existing tests green
- [ ] Manual: start the full stack, open Timeline tab — check logs for timing entries at INFO level

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each upstream call logs round-trip ms at INFO level on success
- [ ] Non-success HTTP responses logged at WARN with status code and ms
- [ ] MeasuresClient logs per-page timing and a post-loop summary
- [ ] ./gradlew :check passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- System.currentTimeMillis() has ~1ms granularity — acceptable for HTTP latency logging.
- Existing debug logs that duplicate the new INFO logs should be removed to avoid log spam.
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec in isolated worktree
